player_card.summary: Study a visible relationship and record it as an Observed Tie.

Effect: Choose one creature, object, Asset, Anchor, location or active spiritual effect you can perceive. Learn one visible relationship involving it.

Learn each side’s broad role; whether the tie is willing, coerced, inherited, possessive, protective, contractual, grief-born, hostile or concealed; whether its Source CL is lower than, equal to or higher than yours; and whether it is active, dormant, damaged, false, severed-but-scarred or externally anchored.
Tug the Visible Thread: Once per turn when you place or refresh a Resonance Mark on a creature involved in an Observed Tie, you may choose one option below.
Choices: Move the marked creature 5 feet toward or away from the other side of the Tie.
Learn whether it is currently acting to protect, obey, pursue, possess, restore or abandon the other side.
Prevent it from becoming Hidden from the other side until the start of your next turn.
Limits: Available at CL 3. You do not automatically learn names, exact contract terms, hidden motives, complete memories or protected secrets.
Forced movement cannot place a creature in an obviously lethal hazard without another Source Rule.

Once per turn when you place or refresh a Resonance Mark on a creature involved in an Observed Tie, you may choose one:

Cultivation Level 14 — Sever the False Thread

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 6 Resonance

Choose one charm, fear, possession, compulsion, false memory bond, coercive oath expression, hostile sympathetic link, controller-Asset link, or emotional manipulation affecting a creature you can perceive.

Make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s save DC or Source CL.

Success:

- An ordinary lower-Source-CL false or coercive tie ends.
- A Restricted or equal-Source-CL tie is suppressed for the scene. Its source may attempt restoration through its printed procedure or a Cultivation Check after one Meaningful Intervention defined in the Normalized Execution Notes.
- A higher, Rare, Forbidden, Secret, divine, artifact, tribulation, Foundation, Method, or identity-defining tie has one coercive expression suppressed until the end of your next turn.

Failure: The target gains Advantage on its next saving throw or Cultivation Check against that tie, and you learn one Anchor, maintenance condition, lawful release, or reconstruction route.

Honest Bonds Remain

Severance Scar

When you fully end a coercive tie, the target may retain a Severance Scar visible to Soul Gaze until it completes one Severance Scar recovery procedure. The scar provides evidence that a tie existed but grants no control and does not count as an Observed Tie for hostile benefits.

player_card.summary: Gain spiritual contact with a distant Handspan Subject, follow its movement and escape its hold.

Effect: Contact Without Adjacency: While your Handspan Subject is within 30 feet and you have line of effect, treat it as within 5 feet only for Spirit-Touch Unarmed Strikes, Nothing Crosses Unanswered, Palm Across Emptiness, ordinary Spiritual Pressure from a Last-Inch feature, or one single-target Spirit Awakening technique whose Source Rule expressly requires spiritual touch and does not move, Grapple, carry or hand off an object.

Follow the Contact: Once per round when your Handspan Subject voluntarily moves, teleports or uses conceptual movement while remaining within 60 feet, you may move up to 15 feet toward a legal space within 10 feet of its destination. This does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the subject.

Follow the Contact cannot cross a sealed boundary or unknown destination. It cannot exceed the distance the subject moved unless you win a Cultivation Check against its movement Source Rule. While Grappled or Restrained, it fails unless you first escape or suppress that effect.

If the subject used equal or higher Space, Boundary, Time, Formation, Void or route authority, make a Cultivation Check to follow. Failure leaves you in place but reveals the movement’s broad authority category.

Open the Gripping Hand: Bonus Action; Cost: 2 Resonance. If you are Grappled, Restrained, possessed through bodily contact, swallowed, pinned, or held by your Handspan Subject, make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s escape DC or Source Rule.

Success: end one ordinary Grappled or Restrained condition, escape one ordinary bodily enclosure to the nearest legal adjacent space, or suppress one equal-authority contact expression until the end of the turn. Against higher authority, success creates enough separation to use one Last-Inch feature, but only ends the full effect if that effect’s own rules permit it. Failure leaves the effect in place; you cannot retry Open the Gripping Hand against the same effect during that turn.
Choices: Soul Splitting — Second Palm: While your Soul Fragment exists, it may maintain a second Handspan Subject. Designate it when the fragment damages that subject with Echo Spike, imposes Pressure on it, or is within 10 feet when you place your Resonance Mark on it.

You and the fragment each maintain one subject. Each activation chooses one subject and one origin. Contact Without Adjacency can originate from the fragment for its subject; Nothing Crosses Unanswered can protect a willing creature adjacent to it; Palm Across Emptiness can originate from it, but you remain the source and pay the cost.
The fragment cannot make unarmed strikes, Grapple, carry objects or create independent contact activations. Its Handspan designation ends when it ends.
Limits: Available at CL 14. Contact Without Adjacency does not make you physically adjacent, allow weapon Opportunity Attacks, Help, Grapple, Shove or delivery of poison or bodily substances, bypass total cover, satisfy an ally’s adjacency requirement or let another creature target through you.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.last_inch_palm..player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 — Inside Every Guard

Contact Without Adjacency

While your Handspan Subject is within 30 feet and you have line of effect, treat it as within 5 feet of you for the following only:

- Spirit-Touch Unarmed Strikes;
- Nothing Crosses Unanswered;
- Palm Across Emptiness;
- ordinary Spiritual Pressure imposed by a Last-Inch feature;
- one single-target Spirit Awakening technique whose Source Rule expressly requires spiritual touch and does not move, Grapple, carry, or hand off an object.

This rule does not make you physically adjacent, allow Opportunity Attacks with a weapon, permit Help, allow a Grapple or Shove, deliver poison or bodily substances, bypass total cover, satisfy an ally's adjacency requirement, or let another creature target through you.

Follow the Contact

Once per round when your Handspan Subject voluntarily moves, teleports, or uses conceptual movement while remaining within 60 feet, you may move up to 15 feet toward a legal space within 10 feet of its destination. This movement:

- does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the subject;
- cannot cross a sealed boundary or unknown destination;
- cannot exceed the distance the subject moved unless you win a Cultivation Check against its movement Source Rule;
- fails while you are Grappled or Restrained unless you first escape or suppress that effect.

If the subject used equal or higher Space, Boundary, Time, Formation, Void, or route authority, make a Cultivation Check to follow. On failure, you remain in place but learn the movement's broad authority category.

Open the Gripping Hand

Bonus Action  
Cost: 2 Resonance

If you are Grappled, Restrained, possessed through bodily contact, swallowed, pinned, or held by your Handspan Subject, make a Cultivation Check against the effect's escape DC or Source Rule.

- Success: End one ordinary Grappled or Restrained condition, escape one ordinary bodily enclosure to the nearest legal adjacent space, or suppress one equal-authority contact expression until the end of the turn.
- Failure: The effect remains. You cannot attempt Open the Gripping Hand against the same effect again during the turn.
- Higher authority: On success, create enough separation to use one Last-Inch feature, but do not automatically end the complete effect unless its own rules permit it.

Soul Splitting — Second Palm

While your Soul Fragment exists, it may maintain a second Handspan Subject. Designate the second subject when the fragment damages it with Echo Spike, imposes Pressure on it, or is within 10 feet when you place your Resonance Mark on it.

- You and the fragment each maintain one subject.
- One activation chooses one Handspan Subject and one origin.
- Contact Without Adjacency can originate from the fragment for its subject.
- Nothing Crosses Unanswered can protect a willing creature adjacent to the fragment.
- Palm Across Emptiness can originate from the fragment, but you remain the source and pay the cost.
- The fragment cannot make unarmed strikes, Grapple, carry objects, or create independent contact activations.

When the fragment ends, its Handspan designation ends.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.last_inch_palm..player_text:
Cultivation Level 6 — Nothing Crosses Unanswered

You can alter the final interval of hostile contact.

Reaction  
You can use this when  Your Handspan Subject within 15 feet targets you or a willing creature adjacent to you with a melee attack, Grapple, Shove, touch-range hostile technique, possession entry, or other effect that requires bodily or spiritual contact  
Cost: 2 Resonance

The subject makes a Wisdom saving throw before the trigger resolves.

Failed Save: For that trigger, increase the required reach or contact distance by 10 feet.

- If the effect no longer has legal reach or contact, it fails against the protected creature.
- If it remains legal, an attack has Disadvantage, the protected creature has Advantage on its check or saving throw, and the source cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Successful Save: The required distance is unchanged. The protected creature gains +2 AC against an attack roll or Advantage on its check or saving throw against the trigger.

After the trigger resolves, you may move 5 feet to a legal space adjacent to the protected creature or the subject. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the subject.

Nothing Crosses Unanswered does not affect an area effect, internal poison already delivered, a true-name effect, an attack originating inside the target, or a technique that expressly ignores distance and contact. Equal or higher contact, Space, Boundary, possession, divine, artifact, or Secret authority can require a Cultivation Check.

Palm at the Threshold

If Nothing Crosses Unanswered causes the trigger to fail, miss, or be resisted successfully, choose one:

- make one Spirit-Touch Unarmed Strike against the subject if it is within your Last-Inch reach;
- use Mind Spike against it, reducing the damage by one die, minimum one die;
- move it 5 feet on a failed Strength or Wisdom saving throw;
- impose one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect until the start of its next turn.

This counter is part of the same Reaction. It cannot activate Truth-Forged Strike, Measured Return, Compass Strike, or another feature that grants an attack.

Effect: Target: Your Handspan Subject or one creature bearing your Resonance Mark. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw.
Failure: it takes 5d8 + Wisdom modifier Psychic or Force damage and becomes your Handspan Subject until the end of the scene. Choose one contact expression below.
Success: it takes half damage and becomes your Handspan Subject until the end of your next turn, with no contact expression.
Choices: Draw Into the Palm: Move it to a legal space adjacent to you. If at least two size categories larger than you, or protected by bodily, gravity, Space, Boundary, anchoring or higher-Source-CL authority, it can make a Strength saving throw after the failed Wisdom save to reduce the movement to 10 feet toward you.

Hold at the Last Inch: Its Speed becomes 0 and it cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.

Touch the Spirit, Not the Flesh: Suppress one ordinary possession entry, disguise-body relation, external controlling link or incorporeal passage expression until the end of your next turn. Equal or higher authority requires a Cultivation Check.
Limits: Available at CL 10. Requires line of effect. This is not a projectile and does not cross intervening spaces. It can pass through an ordinary narrow opening that spiritual contact could cross, but not total cover, a sealed wall, a Domain boundary denying contact or an expressly higher-authority separation.
An ordinary object, spiritually empty corpse or mindless nonspiritual construct is ineligible unless it is an external Anchor or Cultivation Asset that spirit techniques can affect.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.last_inch_palm..player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 — World of One Handspan

You manifest a local spiritual law in which every hostile soul remains at the threshold of your palm.

Bonus Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Area: 30-foot-radius aura centered on you  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required

The aura is your World of One Handspan Domain and moves with you.

All Within Reach of the Spirit

Every hostile creature of your choice in the Domain that you can perceive counts as your Handspan Subject for Last-Inch features. This does not end your normal designation outside the Domain.

You may make Spirit-Touch Unarmed Strikes against such a creature from anywhere in the Domain with legal line of effect. These strikes use your Cultivation Attack Modifier and deal 1d8 + Wisdom modifier Bludgeoning or Psychic damage instead of any higher unarmed damage die granted by another source unless that source expressly combines with projected spiritual contact.

This reach does not permit Grapples, Shoves, weapon attacks, object manipulation, Opportunity Attacks against every creature in the Domain, or delivery of unrelated touch features.

Contact Cannot Be Stolen

The first time each round that each hostile Handspan Subject in the Domain targets a chosen ally with a melee attack, Grapple, Shove, touch technique, possession entry, or contact-dependent effect, it makes a Wisdom saving throw.

- Failed Save: The effect has Disadvantage or grants Advantage on the protected creature's check or save. If the source is more than 5 feet from the protected creature and the effect does not expressly operate at that distance, it fails against that creature.
- Successful Save: The effect resolves normally, but the source cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

This does not consume your Reaction and does not activate Palm at the Threshold.

Ten Thousand Hands, One Contact

Action  
Limit: Once per turn

Choose one:

- use Palm Across Emptiness without spending Resonance, but its damage becomes 3d8 + Wisdom modifier and it cannot use Touch the Spirit, Not the Flesh;
- make one Spirit-Touch Unarmed Strike against up to your Proficiency Bonus different hostile Handspan Subjects in the Domain, making a separate attack roll for each. Each hit deals only the strike's 1d8 + Wisdom modifier damage and cannot activate another once-per-turn rider;
- move one willing creature in the Domain up to 15 feet to a legal space as your palm carries its spiritual contact. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks;
- require one hostile Handspan Subject to make a Wisdom saving throw, moving it up to 15 feet on a failure or 5 feet on a success.

The multi-target option is one technique activation, not an Attack action, and cannot deliver weapons, poisons, Insights, Recorded Arts, or Forged Technique riders.

Sanctuary at the Last Inch

Once during the activation, when a chosen creature in the Domain would be Grappled, possessed, swallowed, pulled through a portal, banished through contact, or reduced to 0 Hit Points by a melee or touch-range effect, you may use your Reaction and spend 3 Resonance.

Move the creature to a legal space adjacent to you and defer only the contact-dependent portion of the trigger until the end of its next turn.

- Damage that did not depend on contact still applies immediately.
- The creature can answer the deferred contact by leaving the Domain, ending the source's reach, exorcising the link, destroying an Anchor, or winning the appropriate contest.
- If the source still has legal contact and authority when the delay ends, the deferred portion occurs.
- Permanent, Secret, divine, artifact, true-name, internal, or higher-Source-CL consequences require a Cultivation Check. On failure, the movement can still occur if legal, but the consequence is not deferred.

This is a contact-bound delay, not time manipulation, and cannot defer an unrelated consequence.

Domain Collision and Ending

Law of Near and Far, Boundary, Space, possession, true-name contact, Domains, Seals, divine touch, artifacts, and higher-Source-CL contact laws contest only the contradictory expression. World of One Handspan cannot reach through total cover, across planes, or into an unknown sealed space.

When the Domain ends, its temporary Handspan subjects end. Your normal Handspan designation remains for its normal duration.

Success on the initial save: reduce its reach and hostile technique ranges by 10 feet until the start of your next turn, minimum 5 feet for techniques that normally have range.

Far-Side Anchor: When the target fails its initial save, create this conceptual Anchor in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of it. Its AC equals your Cultivation Save DC, Hit Points equal 5 × PB, Wisdom and Charisma saving throw bonuses use yours, and Source CL is your effective Spirit Awakening CL. It is immune to Poisoned, Disease and Psychic damage.

Destroying, exorcising or conceptually reconnecting the Anchor immediately ends Far-Sided. The target and allies can perceive it as a distant door, horizon line, receding lantern, endless road or another symbol of remoteness.
Choices: Soul Splitting — Near Twin: While your soul fragment is within 60 feet, it is always Near to you without counting against your relation limit. Once per turn, you may use a Bonus Action and spend 2 Resonance to exchange spaces with it by conceptual translation. The exchange destroys the fragment; this voluntary destruction causes no normal Soul Splitting backlash damage.
Limits: Available at CL 14. Maintain only one Far-Side Anchor at a time.

Cultivation Level 14 — Cast Them to the Far Side

You can make a creature spiritually remote from the battlefield without erasing it from existence.

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 7 Resonance  
Duration: 1 minute

Choose one creature you can perceive. It makes a Charisma saving throw.

Failed Save: The target becomes Far-Sided. At the end of each of its turns, it repeats the save, ending the effect on a success.

While Far-Sided:

- every other creature is treated as 30 feet farther away from it for its attacks, hostile techniques, auras, commanded Assets, and voluntary movement toward them;
- it cannot take Opportunity Attacks;
- it cannot benefit from allied auras, Help, touch effects, or reactions originating from another creature unless the source wins a Cultivation Check against your Source Rule;
- teleportation and route effects it uses have their range halved;
- it remains visible, audible, damageable, and present in its actual space.

Successful Save: Until the start of your next turn, its reach and hostile technique ranges are reduced by 10 feet, minimum 5 feet for techniques that normally have range.

Far-Side Anchor

When a target fails the initial save, create a conceptual Far-Side Anchor in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of it.

- AC: your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 5 × Proficiency Bonus
- Saving Throws: uses your Wisdom and Charisma saving throw bonuses
- Immunities: Poisoned, Disease, Psychic damage
- Source CL: your effective Spirit Awakening CL

Destroying, exorcising, or conceptually reconnecting the Anchor ends Far-Sided immediately. The target and its allies can perceive the Anchor as a distant door, horizon line, receding lantern, endless road, or another symbol of remoteness.

You can maintain one Far-Side Anchor at a time.

Soul Splitting — Near Twin

While your soul fragment is within 60 feet, it is always Near to you and does not count against your relation limit. Once per turn, you may exchange spaces with it as a Bonus Action by spending 2 Resonance. This is conceptual translation. The fragment is destroyed after the exchange, but this voluntary destruction does not cause the normal Soul Splitting backlash damage.

You interpose conceptual remoteness between an attack and its intended victim.

Choose one result:

Ease Pain

Suppress one ordinary pain, fear symptom, despair symptom, or minor spiritual disturbance until the end of the scene. The underlying source remains and resumes afterward unless treated.

Take the Edge

The target gains Temporary Hit Points equal to Proficiency Bonus + Wisdom modifier and Advantage on its next saving throw against Frightened or Spiritual Pressure before the end of your next turn.

Lift the Tremor

End one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect, or allow the target to repeat one saving throw against an ordinary Charmed or Frightened effect.

After resolving the chosen result, take Psychic damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. This damage cannot be reduced.

If Gentle Knife suppresses or ends an effect created by a meaningful hostile creature, you may gain 1 Mercy Scar instead of taking this damage.

Diagnostic Incision

When you touch the target, you also learn whether its pain or disturbance is ordinary, Restricted, Forbidden, Secret, divine, artifact-level, cultivation-based, bodily, emotional, memory-based, identity-based, or possession-based. Protected causes can require a Cultivation Check.

Cultivation Level 10 — Give the Pain a Name

You can transfer a burden after defining what it is.

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 4 Resonance  
Requirement: The receiving target is Resonance Marked by you, bears your Mercy Scar through a prior link, or is touching a Flayed Burden Anchor

Choose one Mercy Scar carried by you, a willing ally within 30 feet, or a Flayed Burden Anchor. Name its broad burden aloud: fear, pain, despair, contamination, possession-pressure, nightmare, curse-pressure, or another accurate category.

A willing receiving target accepts the transfer. An unwilling receiving target makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save: Transfer the Mercy Scar to the target until the end of its next turn. Choose one expression appropriate to the burden:

- impose one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect;
- impose Frightened until the end of its next turn if the Scar came from fear;
- reduce Speed by 10 feet and prevent Reactions if the Scar came from pain;
- impose Disadvantage on the next Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma save if the Scar came from spiritual contamination;
- suppress one source of healing or Temporary Hit Points until the end of its next turn if the Scar came from a curse or bodily wound.

At the end of the target’s next turn, the Scar returns to its prior bearer or Anchor unless another procedure receives it.

Successful Save: The transfer fails. The target suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect, and the Scar remains where it was.

Permanent and Protected Burdens

This feature cannot transfer a permanent injury, destroyed organ, complete curse, complete possession, memory deletion, identity severance, Foundation damage, Method damage, or Secret-Law harm unless a separate Source Rule expressly permits it. It may transfer one symptom or pressure expression from such harm for the printed duration.

Named Relief

When a willing creature accepts a Mercy Scar from another willing creature, both gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. This can occur only once per scene for each creature.

Cultivation Level 6 — Peel the Wound

Action  
Range: Touch  
Cost: 3 Resonance  
Target: One willing creature, or one restrained/unconscious creature whose current custodian lawfully permits emergency treatment

Choose one poison, disease, Charmed effect, Frightened effect, ordinary curse, ordinary possession, Nightmare Scar, Devoured Dream, spiritual contamination, or Spiritual Pressure package affecting the target. Make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s save DC. If it has no save DC, use 8 + source Proficiency Bonus + source key ability modifier.

Success: Choose one result.

- Suppress: Suppress the effect for the scene.
- Extract: If the effect is ordinary and has lower Source CL, end it and gain 1 Mercy Scar.
- Expose: Reveal the effect’s Anchor, current host, transmission route, restoration condition, or one legal way to remove it.

Failure: The target gains Advantage on its next saving throw or Cultivation Check against the effect. You take Psychic damage equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus.

Flayed Burden

When you Extract an effect, you may place the Mercy Scar into a prepared strip of cloth, paper skin, wax figure, surgical thread, spirit parchment, or other suitable vessel instead of carrying it personally. The vessel becomes a Flayed Burden Anchor:

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 4 × Proficiency Bonus
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
- Immunities: Poison, Psychic, and ordinary bodily conditions
- Duration: Until treated, destroyed, deliberately opened, or the burden is transferred

A Flayed Burden Anchor can hold one Mercy Scar. You can maintain a number of such Anchors equal to your Wisdom modifier, minimum one.

Cultivation Level 18 — White Room Mercy

Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Duration: The scene

Create a silent 30-foot aura of white spiritual pressure centered on you. The aura is a Spirit Awakening field with your Source CL. Sound can exist within it, but cries of pain, panic, and involuntary confession do not travel beyond its boundary unless you permit them.

While the White Room lasts:

- Allies of your choice have Advantage on death saving throws and saves against Charmed, Frightened, possession, despair, pain, ordinary spiritual contamination, and ordinary memory or identity pressure.
- Once on each of your turns, choose one ally in the aura. It regains 3d8 + Wisdom modifier Hit Points or repeats one save against an effect listed above.
- A willing creature in the aura can transfer one ordinary pain, fear, Spiritual Pressure effect, Nightmare Scar, Mercy Scar, or minor contamination to an empty Flayed Burden Anchor as an Action.
- Hostile creatures cannot force a willing ally to reveal information through pain, fear, or ordinary spiritual coercion while that ally remains in the aura.

Once During the White Room — Impossible Triage

When a creature in the aura would die, suffer a permanent wound, lose a memory, have its identity altered, become possessed, have its soul displaced, or suffer permanent cultivation-system harm, you may use your Reaction and choose one result:

Defer

Delay the complete consequence until the end of the scene. The target remains alive and functional enough to act, though it may be at 1 Hit Point and visibly unstable. If the consequence is not properly repaired, escaped, exorcised, or otherwise changed before the scene ends, it returns in full.

Take the Burden

If the consequence is ordinary or lower Source CL, transfer it to yourself as a White Mercy Scar. The target avoids it. A White Mercy Scar counts as two Mercy Scars, cannot rupture for a save bonus, and cannot be removed by an ordinary Full Cultivation Session. It requires the White-Mercy Restoration procedure in the Procedure Addendum or treatment by an explicit equal-or-higher-authority restoration Source Rule.

House the Burden

Place the consequence into a specially prepared White Room Anchor occupying one space in the aura. The Anchor has:

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 10 × Proficiency Bonus
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
- Immunities: Poison, Psychic, Necrotic, Radiant, and ordinary bodily conditions

The Anchor persists after the aura ends until the burden is reconstructed, transferred, purified, or released. If destroyed without completing a transfer, purification, or reconstruction, resolve Escaped Burden Priority from the Procedure Addendum using the housed consequence as the burden.

Authority Limits

Secret-Law erasure, divine judgment, artifact execution, tribulation injury, complete soul destruction, voluntary refusal to return, and equal- or higher-Source-CL permanent harm can resist Impossible Triage. On a successful Cultivation Check, you may still stabilize the victim and prevent escalation until a proper restoration procedure is attempted.

White Room Mercy is powerful because it creates time and custody. It does not make catastrophic harm cease to exist without someone or something carrying it.

Soul Splitting Expression — Burden-Bearing Double

While Soul Splitting is active, use Burden-Bearing Double as your Subpath Expression. Move your Soul Fragment up to 20 feet, then transfer one Mercy Scar you carry to the fragment or return one Scar it carries to you. The Scar still counts against your maximum. While carried by the fragment, it cannot be ruptured for a saving-throw bonus, but Give the Pain a Name and White Room Mercy may treat the fragment as its bearer and origin. If the fragment is destroyed or Soul Splitting ends, the Scar immediately returns to you; if that exceeds your maximum, resolve overflow normally.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.miko.feature.ka.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 — Kami’s Messenger

Your messengers can cross the border between ordinary distance and recognized spiritual relationship.

Omen Message

Action  
Cost: 3 Resonance and 1 Offering

Send a message of up to 25 words to one creature you have met, one recognized shrine, one willing ancestor, one bonded spirit, or one community that knows your shrine name. The target must be on the same plane.

The message arrives within 1 hour through one chosen omen form: dream, foxfire, reflected text, moving paper charm, bird call, shrine sign, sudden scent, or writing produced by an unattended brush. The form is cosmetic and grants no concealment, control, damage, item activation, or additional information. The recipient knows the message is spiritually sent and can send a response of up to 25 words if willing.

Omen Message cannot cross a sealed planar boundary, reach a creature whose soul is completely hidden by equal or higher Source CL without a Cultivation Check, or force a target to read or answer.

Petition the Local Kami

Ritual: 10 minutes  
Cost: 4 Resonance and 1 Offering

Petition the most relevant willing local kami, shrine spirit, land memory, river presence, household spirit, grave guardian, or equivalent minor authority. Ask for one service:

- Reveal one recent spiritual disturbance within 1 mile.
- Identify the direction of a known spirit, curse, shrine, grave, possession, or sacred boundary within 1 mile.
- Carry a message or Tiny object within 10 miles through a legal route.
- Grant safe passage through one ordinary environmental or spiritual inconvenience under the kami’s authority.
- Provide one omen concerning a proposed action within the next day.
- Consecrate one additional Sacred Ground Aspect on an existing Shrine Anchor for 1 hour.

The petition uses the Kami Petition Price procedure in the Procedure Addendum. The kami either accepts the printed cost or names exactly one additional recorded price from that procedure. You learn the exact price before accepting and may decline without losing the Resonance or Offering. A local kami cannot grant power outside its recorded Nature, jurisdiction, or Source CL.

Manifest Messenger Asset

As an Action, spend 4 Resonance to manifest one previously contacted willing messenger kami for the scene. It is a Small Spirit Cultivation Asset:

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC.
- Hit Points: 4 × Proficiency Bonus.
- Speed: 40 feet; choose fly, climb, swim, or walking when contacted.
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL.
- Resistances: Psychic.

It has no independent turn. At the end of your turn, it moves up to its Speed. Once on each of your turns after you use a Miko or Spirit Awakening support feature, it can deliver that feature’s touch or 30-foot-range effect from its space if the feature is not hostile and does not create another Asset.

If destroyed, it returns to its shrine or local spirit state and cannot be manifested again until you complete a Full Cultivation Session or make restitution required by its Taboo.

Soul Splitting Expression — Procession of Two Worlds

While Soul Splitting is active, use Procession of Two Worlds as your Subpath Expression. Move your Soul Fragment or Manifest Messenger up to 20 feet. One willing creature adjacent to the moved Asset gains Advantage on its next save against possession, curse, Frightened, or spiritual contamination before the start of your next turn.

Cultivation Level 3 — Purification Dance

You learn two forms of Purification Dance.

Brief Purification

Action  
Range: Touch  
Cost: 1 Offering or 2 Resonance

Touch one willing creature, object, corpse, threshold, or 5-foot space. Choose one result:

- End the Poisoned condition if caused by an ordinary poison.
- Grant Advantage on the target’s next save against an ordinary disease, curse, possession, Frightened effect, dream intrusion, or spiritual contamination before the end of the scene.
- Remove one ordinary Resonance Mark, tracking mark, minor curse-sign, spiritual scent, or contamination with Source CL lower than yours.
- Suppress one ordinary possession, curse, or spiritual contamination until the start of your next turn.
- Make one invisible ordinary spirit, curse residue, or possession trace visible to Spiritual Sense until the end of your next turn.

Brief Purification cannot end severe disease, a permanent curse, a Heart Demon, willing possession, divine punishment, Secret-Law effect, or equal/higher-Source-CL contamination without a check and its proper recovery condition.

Full Purification Dance

Ritual: 1 minute  
Range: Touch  
Cost: 1 Offering and 1 Resonance

End one ordinary poison, disease, curse, minor possession, nightmare residue, or spiritual contamination affecting the target. Against an equal- or higher-Source-CL effect, make a Cultivation Check against its save DC. On success, choose one:

- End it if its Source Rule permits ordinary removal.
- Suppress it until the target completes its next Full Cultivation Session.
- Reveal its Source, Anchor, taboo, offering, restitution, or recovery condition.
- Prevent it from worsening until the end of the next scene.

Shrine Etiquette

You may use Wisdom instead of Intelligence for Religion checks concerning kami, shrines, local spirits, offerings, purification, funerary boundaries, and sacred customs.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.miko.feature.sa.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 — Sacred Ground

You establish a reciprocal sanctuary rather than merely projecting a hostile aura.

Action  
Area: 20-foot-radius sphere centered on a point within 30 feet  
Cost: 5 Resonance and 1 Offering  
Duration: 1 hour  
Concentration: No

Place or suspend the consumed Offering as a visible Shrine Anchor at the center.

Shrine Anchor Profile

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC.
- Hit Points: 5 × Proficiency Bonus.
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL.
- Immunities: Poison, Disease, and Psychic damage.
- It can be perceived by Spiritual Sense and by creatures able to perceive sacred or spiritual objects.

Sacred Ground ends if the Anchor is destroyed, willingly dismissed, or moved more than 5 feet. When you create it, choose one Profanation Condition from the Procedure Addendum and record it on the Anchor. The Ground is profaned only when that exact condition occurs inside the Ground and the responsible creature knowingly performs the act.

Choose one Ground Aspect when you create it:

Purifying Ground

Allies in the Ground have Advantage on saves against possession, curses, disease, poison, Frightened, and spiritual contamination. A willing ally that starts its turn there can repeat one save against an ongoing qualifying effect once per scene.

Hostile undead, fiends, demons, and Intruders have Disadvantage on the first attack roll they make each turn in the Ground.

Welcoming Ground

Willing spirits, ancestors, kami, projected souls, and Spirit Companions in the Ground can communicate intelligibly with creatures they could normally reach through language, emotion, image, or spiritual impression. This does not grant universal knowledge or remove a spirit’s Taboo.

A hostile spirit that enters for the first time on a turn makes a Charisma saving throw. On failure, it cannot take hostile actions until the start of its next turn unless attacked.

Restorative Ground

A willing creature that spends at least 10 minutes resting in the Ground regains additional Hit Points equal to 2 × your Spirit Awakening CL when it spends one or more Hit Dice and gains Advantage on its next save against Exhaustion, Heart Demon escalation, dream intrusion, or spiritual contamination before the target completes its next Full Cultivation Session.

A creature can receive this restorative benefit only once between its Full Cultivation Sessions.

Sacred-Ground Collision

An equal- or higher-Source-CL Domain, desecration, curse field, or hostile shrine can contest one Ground law with a Cultivation Check. Losing the contest suppresses only the contradictory law until the start of the winner’s next turn unless a Source Rule says otherwise.

You force the reflected self to answer when the presented self refuses.

Cultivation Level 18 — Grand Mudang Procession

You call a greater manifestation into a moving court of drum, breath, ancestor, and local spirit authority.

Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Duration: The scene  
Concentration: No

Create a Grand Spirit Procession, a Huge Spirit Cultivation Asset occupying a 15-foot-square space within 30 feet. It may appear as a masked giant, ancestral palanquin, spectral animal, procession of banners, storm of paper spirits, or another lineage-appropriate manifestation.

Procession Profile

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 10 × Proficiency Bonus
- Speed: 40 feet; it can hover
- Saving Throws: Uses your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throw bonuses
- Resistances: Psychic, Necrotic, Radiant
- Immunities: Poison, Disease, Poisoned, Prone, Grappled, Restrained, and ordinary bodily effects
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
- Action economy: No independent turn. At the end of each of your turns, it moves up to its Speed. You direct one Procession Expression as a Bonus Action.

Procession Expressions

Choose one:

- Spirit Strike: Make a Cultivation Attack against a creature within 15 feet of the Procession. On a hit, deal 4d10 + Wisdom modifier Psychic, Necrotic, Radiant, Thunder, or Force damage, chosen to fit the invited court.
- Carry the Living: Move one willing Large or smaller creature adjacent to the Procession with it. That creature has Half Cover until it leaves the Procession’s space.
- Reveal the Hidden Court: Until the start of your next turn, ordinary invisible spirits, projections, possessing entities, and lower-Source-CL spiritual disguises within 30 feet of the Procession are revealed.
- Beat Back the Intruder: One spirit, possessed creature, or incorporeal undead within 30 feet makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, move it up to 20 feet, end one ordinary possession it maintains, and impose one Spiritual Pressure effect. On a success, move it 5 feet or impose one Spiritual Pressure effect.
- Communal Mending: One creature within 15 feet regains 3d8 + Wisdom modifier Hit Points and may repeat one saving throw against Charmed, Frightened, ordinary possession, or ordinary spiritual contamination.

A creature can benefit from Communal Mending only once per activation of Grand Mudang Procession.

Grand Hospitality

Spirits with lower Source CL cannot enter the Procession’s space, possess a creature inside it, or conceal their broad category from you without succeeding on a Charisma saving throw. A willing spirit may instead enter under hospitality and speak through the Procession without gaining control of it.

Destruction and Departure

If the Procession is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it disperses and you take 4d10 Psychic damage that ignores Resistance. You cannot use Grand Mudang Procession again until you complete a Full Cultivation Session.

The Procession ends cleanly if dismissed. Invited spirits depart with memory of how they were treated. A spirit is not permanently bound, duplicated, or converted into a companion by this feature.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.plain_truth_fis.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 — Hall of Spoken Deeds

You manifest a Domain in which every combatant's first purpose becomes visible enough for heaven to judge its consistency.

Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Area: 40-foot-radius sphere centered on a point you can perceive within 60 feet  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required

The sphere is your Hall of Spoken Deeds Domain.

Willing Declarations

At the start of a chosen ally's turn in the Hall, it may declare one of the following deeds: Challenge, Pursuit, Guard, Break, or Hold.

- Hold: Remain within 5 feet of its starting space and take a primarily defensive, observational, recovery, or preparation action.

If the ally completes the declared deed before the turn ends, choose one benefit:

- move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks;
- gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus;
- add 1d8 to one damage or healing roll made as part of the deed;
- gain Advantage on its next Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw before the start of its next turn.

A creature gains one benefit per turn. Its declaration does not create your Credence.

Hostile Intention

At the start of each hostile creature's turn in the Hall, it makes a Wisdom saving throw.

- Failed Save: It chooses an Intent from Unspoken Intention and is subject to Contradiction until the turn ends.
- Successful Save: It is not bound, but you learn the broad category of its first present intention and may impose one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect until the start of its next turn.

A creature that succeeded on two saves against Hostile Intention during the same activation becomes immune to automatic binding by this Domain for the remainder of the activation, though Unspoken Intention can still target it normally.

Credence Before Heaven

You gain 1 Credence the first time each round that:

- you complete an Open Declaration in the Hall; or
- a hostile creature suffers Contradiction in the Hall.

You cannot exceed your normal maximum.

Deed Without Hesitation

Once on each of your turns, you may use Deed Follows Word without paying its Resonance cost. You must still spend 1–3 Credence. You cannot also use a paid Deed Follows Word during that turn.

Final Pronouncement

Once during the activation, choose one Resonance Marked hostile creature in the Hall and make one declaration:

- Face Me: It cannot willingly target another creature with a hostile single-target effect while you remain a legal target.
- Do Not Flee: Its Speed is halved when moving away from you, and ordinary teleportation cannot carry it outside the Hall.
- Release What Is Not Yours: It must release one ordinary Grapple, possession expression, controlled Asset command, stolen object, or maintained coercive effect of your choice.
- Speak the Deed: It must state the broad purpose of one active technique, Domain, Asset, Anchor, or transformation it is maintaining.

The target makes a Charisma saving throw.

- Failed Save: The pronouncement lasts until the start of your next turn.
- Successful Save: It suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect until the start of your next turn.

Final Pronouncement cannot force self-harm, reveal a protected secret name or complete technique text, end a willing bond, release a higher-authority possession automatically, or override a Secret, divine, artifact, or equal-or-higher conceptual law without a Cultivation Check.

Hall Anchor and Counterplay

The Hall manifests a visible Witness Stone in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of its center:

- AC: your Cultivation Save DC;
- Hit Points: 8 × Proficiency Bonus;
- Saving Throws: uses your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throw bonuses;
- Resistances: Psychic damage;
- Source CL: your effective Spirit Awakening CL.

A creature adjacent to the Stone can use an Action to make Charisma (Deception), Wisdom (Insight), Intelligence (Arcana), or an appropriate Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC. On a success, it suppresses Hostile Intention for itself until the end of its next turn. Destroying or fully suppressing the Stone ends the Domain.

Domain Collision and Ending

Oath, Contract, Sovereignty, Fate, Mind, illusion, true-name, Secret Law, divine command, artifact, or higher-Source-CL authority contests only the contradictory declaration or revelation. When the Hall ends, declarations and Intents created by it end. Credence remains until the scene ends.

- suppressing the movement or Martial Strike required by the declaration.

Bonus Action

- “This appearance conceals another identity.”

Cultivation Level 10 — Burn Away the Lesser Self

You can shed an affliction into a temporary spiritual cast-off.

Bonus Action  
Cost: 5 Resonance  
Optional cost: Gain 1 Molt Debt to strengthen the result

Choose one effect on yourself:

- Charmed;
- Frightened;
- Poisoned;
- one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect;
- one ordinary dream influence;
- one ordinary emotional corruption;
- one ordinary or lower-Source-CL possession symptom;
- one minor curse or spiritual contamination.

If the effect is ordinary and lower Source CL, end it. If equal or higher authority, suppress it until the end of your next turn and make a Cultivation Check. On success, suppress it for the scene instead.

The removed or suppressed burden becomes a Cast-Off Self in an adjacent space:

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 5 × Proficiency Bonus
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
- Speed: 0 feet
- Immunities: Poison, Psychic, and ordinary bodily conditions
- Duration: Until the scene ends, it is destroyed, or you reintegrate it

The Cast-Off is not a creature and takes no turn. It visibly expresses the shed weakness.

Cast-Off Consequences

While the Cast-Off exists:

- You cannot gain the exact same ordinary effect from the same source again.
- If the hostile source was within 60 feet when you shed it, that source becomes Resonance Marked by you.
- A creature can target the Cast-Off as though it were an Anchor for the removed effect.

If the Cast-Off is destroyed by hostile action, the burden does not return, but you gain 1 Molt Debt. If you voluntarily reintegrate it as an Action, regain Resonance equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down, and the original effect returns only if its duration and source still legally persist.

If you gained Molt Debt on activation, the Cast-Off’s Hit Points double and the effect is treated as one Source CL higher for resisting restoration by its original source.

Cultivation Level 18 — Molt the Mortal Name

You shed the layer of identity by which ordinary death, weakness, and mortal limitation recognize you.

Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance and 1 Molt Debt  
Duration: The scene

Manifest a complete Seraphic Ascension Form. Choose two Ascension Anatomies when the form begins and a third when you reach half your Hit Point maximum or lower.

Throne Wings

Gain a fly Speed of 60 feet and hover. Your movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from creatures with lower Source CL unless they possess a specific anti-flight or anti-spirit Source Rule.

Thousand Eyes

Your Spiritual Sense extends 60 feet farther. You cannot be surprised by spiritually perceptible creatures, and ordinary concealment cannot make a creature you already detected count as unseen against you.

Burning Name

Gain Resistance to Psychic and Radiant damage. When a creature damages you with one of those types, it becomes Resonance Marked by you.

Crown of Unselfing

You have Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws. When you succeed on one, impose one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect on the source if it is within 60 feet.

Mercyless Purity

At the start of each of your turns, end one ordinary Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned, possession, curse, disease, spiritual contamination, or emotional corruption effect on yourself. Equal or higher authority requires a Cultivation Check and is suppressed until the start of your next turn on success.

Swordless Judgment

Once on each of your turns when you deal Psychic, Radiant, or Necrotic damage with a Spirit Awakening feature, deal an additional 2d8 damage of one of those types and impose one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.

Death and the Shed Name

The first time during the form that you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, displaced from your body, or have your soul imprisoned by an ordinary or lower-Source-CL effect, you may shed the consequence into a Mortal Name Husk and remain at 1 Hit Point.

The Husk appears in an adjacent space with:

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 10 × Proficiency Bonus
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
- Immunities: Poison, Psychic, Radiant, Necrotic, and ordinary bodily conditions

If the Husk survives until the form ends, reintegrate it and gain 1 additional Molt Debt. If it is destroyed, the prevented consequence remains prevented, but you gain a Permanent Seraphic Sign and cannot use Molt the Mortal Name again until you complete the Mortal Name Husk identity-reconstruction procedure.

End of the Form

When the form ends, choose one cost:

- gain 1 additional Molt Debt;
- lose one Hit Die until treated during a Full Cultivation Session;
- accept Disadvantage on your next meaningful Charisma check involving ordinary mortal empathy;
- become spiritually obvious to trained observers for 24 hours;
- manifest a new visible Seraphic Sign until purified.

Secret-Law erasure, divine custody, artifact imprisonment, tribulation destruction, voluntary surrender of identity, and equal- or higher-authority soul destruction can contest the Husk and Ascension Form through their printed procedures. Molting is not universal immortality.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.soul_warden_nec.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 — Lord of the Dead

You establish temporary jurisdiction over the dead in the scene and manifest a warden-wraith built from your cultivated office.

Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance and 1 Soul Fragment  
Duration: The scene  
Concentration: No

Create a Warden-Wraith, a Large Spirit Cultivation Asset in an unoccupied space within 30 feet.

Warden-Wraith Profile

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 12 × Proficiency Bonus
- Speed: Fly 50 feet; hover
- Saving Throws: Uses your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throw bonuses
- Resistances: Psychic, Necrotic, Radiant
- Immunities: Poison, Disease, Poisoned, Prone, Grappled, Restrained, and ordinary bodily effects
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
- Action economy: No independent turn. At the end of each of your turns, it moves up to its Speed. As a Bonus Action, direct one Wraith Expression.

Wraith Expressions

- Warden’s Scythe: Make a Cultivation Attack against one creature within 10 feet. On a hit, deal 4d10 + Wisdom modifier Necrotic, Psychic, or Radiant damage. A spirit or undead hit cannot take Reactions until the start of your next turn.
- Chain the Departing: One spirit, incorporeal undead, projected soul, or creature attempting teleportation, reincarnation, soul escape, or possession within 30 feet makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the attempted movement or transition fails and the creature is Restrained by spiritual chains until the end of its next turn. On success, its Speed is halved or it suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.
- Open the Proper Gate: Release one willing spirit, end one ordinary lower-Source-CL coercive binding, or permit one soul under Death Custody to depart through the correct afterlife, reincarnation, ancestor court, or Soul Anchor route. Equal or higher custody requires a Cultivation Check.
- Procession of Witnesses: Up to Proficiency Bonus corpses, grave residues, or willing local dead within 60 feet produce brief testimony, reveal their direction of death, or indicate the presence of a murderer, possessor, necromantic Anchor, or concealed spirit they genuinely perceived.
- Burial Silence: Create a 20-foot-radius zone centered on the wraith until the start of your next turn. Hostile spirits and undead in the zone cannot regain Hit Points, restore Cultivation Points, become invisible, or create new possessed hosts.

Jurisdiction of the Dead

While the Warden-Wraith exists:

- Ordinary lower-Source-CL undead and unbound specters within 60 feet cannot attack you unless they succeed on a Charisma saving throw at the start of their turn.
- You know when a creature dies within 60 feet and whether its soul departs, remains, is seized, reincarnates, or becomes concealed.
- You may maintain a number of Soul Fragments equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus for the activation’s duration.
- Coerced fragments cannot be hidden from you by ordinary means.

Complete Soul Boundary

Once during the activation, when a hostile spirit at least 5 Source CL lower than you, undead ruler, or soul predator is reduced to 0 Hit Points within 60 feet, you may attempt Final Custody.

The target makes a Charisma saving throw.

- Failed Save: Its complete soul or governing death-fragment is sealed inside the Warden-Wraith until the feature ends. While sealed, it cannot reform, possess, reincarnate, return to a phylactery-like Anchor, or activate a death-triggered escape. Before the feature ends, you must release it, transfer it to a legal prison or afterlife route, or create a specific long-term Anchor under a separate Source Rule.
- Successful Save: Its attempted escape is delayed until the end of its next turn and it suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.

Final Custody is not permanent soul destruction. Equal- or higher-Source-CL targets use their printed escape procedures and may force a Cultivation Check contest.

Wraith Destruction

If the Warden-Wraith is destroyed, you take 6d10 Psychic damage that ignores Resistance, every Soul Fragment beyond your normal maximum is released, and any complete soul held by Final Custody escapes to the nearest legal route. You cannot use Lord of the Dead again until you complete a Full Cultivation Session.

Forbidden Consequences

Using Lord of the Dead to release, protect, or lawfully imprison spirits creates no Grave Debt. Each of the following creates 2 Grave Debt when completed: consume an unwilling Complete Soul; create permanent slavery of a Complete Soul; obstruct a recorded rightful afterlife route for personal gain; or weaponize a protected ancestor against its recorded will. One act can create Grave Debt only once under this list, even if several descriptions apply. Higher spiritual authorities may perceive or contest the act according to their Source Rules.

Effect: Choose one creature; it makes a Constitution saving throw. A spirit, incorporeal undead, possessed creature or creature bearing your Resonance Mark may use Charisma instead if that bonus is higher.

Failure: Deal 6d8 + Wisdom modifier Necrotic or Psychic damage, your choice. Until the end of its next turn, it cannot regain HP or restore CP. A spirit or undead also cannot become incorporeal, possess another creature or return to a prepared vessel during that time.
Success: Half damage; it cannot become spiritually concealed until the start of your next turn.
Capture at the Brink: If Soul Drain reduces a qualifying hostile creature to 0 HP, choose one result below.

Death Custody: While custody lasts, the creature is stable at 0 HP and does not die, depart, reincarnate, become undead, or have its soul seized by an ordinary lower-Source-CL effect. Choose one custody outcome below before the scene ends.
Choices: Capture at the Brink — Fragment: Create one Soul Fragment without using your Reaction.
Capture at the Brink — Custody: Stabilize the creature and hold its departing residue under Death Custody until the end of the scene.
Death Custody — Release: Let it die or depart normally.
Death Custody — Healing: Permit legal healing.
Death Custody — Transfer: Transfer custody to a willing healer, funerary authority or prepared vessel.
Death Custody — Interrogation: If death occurs, attempt a lawful interrogation through Speak with the Dead.
Death Custody — Coerced Fragment: Convert the residue into a Coerced Soul Fragment. Gain 1 Grave Debt unless this is necessary to prevent a greater spiritual catastrophe.

Warden’s Reversal: As a Reaction when an ally within 30 feet would have its soul displaced, consumed, trapped or converted into an undead manifestation, spend one Soul Fragment. tianxia.tradition.spirit.thrum_of_the_gr.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 — Burial Drum

You establish a rhythm in which healing, courage, and false immortality struggle to take hold.

Action  
Cost: 5 Resonance  
Duration: 1 minute  
Area: 20-foot-radius aura centered on you  
Concentration: Required

While the Burial Drum persists:

- The aura moves with you.
- Hostile creatures treat the aura as Difficult Terrain while moving closer to you.
- When a hostile creature in the aura would regain Hit Points, it makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save: It regains no Hit Points. If it is undead, possessed, Resonance Marked, Frightened, dying, or sustained by a death-related effect, it also takes Necrotic or Psychic damage equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus.

Successful Save: The healing is halved.

A creature makes this save no more than once per turn, regardless of how many healing sources affect it.

Beat of Interment

Once on each of your turns, you may spend 1 Gravebeat to pulse the Drum. Choose one hostile creature in the aura. It makes a Constitution saving throw.

Failed Save: It takes 3d8 + Wisdom modifier Necrotic or Psychic damage and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Successful Save: It takes half damage.

If the target is at 0 Hit Points, an ordinary creature, and not protected by a death ward, the pulse instead causes one failed death saving throw. Major enemies, player characters, named rivals, and creatures protected by stronger authority use the damage procedure unless the campaign explicitly permits lethal battlefield finishing.

Burial Marker Anchor

You may plant a drum, staff, weapon, bell, grave tablet, banner, bone stake, or spiritual marker in an adjacent space as a Burial Marker Anchor:

- AC: your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 7 × Proficiency Bonus
- Resistances: Necrotic and Psychic damage
- Source CL: your effective Spirit Awakening CL

While it remains, the aura is centered on the Anchor and does not require Concentration. Destroying or suppressing it ends the aura.

player_card.summary: Create an Unquiet Echo to channel the memory of death.

Effect: Create one Unquiet Echo in an unoccupied space adjacent to the source; you can maintain only one at a time. This Medium Cultivation Asset has AC equal to your Cultivation Save DC, HP equal to 6 × PB, and Source CL equal to your effective Spirit Awakening CL.
It uses your Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saving throw bonuses. Resistances: Necrotic and Psychic damage. Immunities: Poisoned, Disease and ordinary suffocation.

Speed: 30 feet. It can pass through creatures and objects as Difficult Terrain, but takes 2d10 Force damage if it ends its turn inside one. It has no independent turn; on your turn, it moves when you move or direct it as a Bonus Action.
Choose one Death Memory below when you create the Echo.

Grave Cry: Once on each of your turns, you may spend 1 Gravebeat to have the Echo cry at one creature within 30 feet. It makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failure: 3d8 Psychic damage and Frightened until the end of its next turn. Success: Half damage.
Choices: Soldier’s March: When you use Dead March, you may originate it from the Echo and increase one target’s forced movement by 10 feet on a failed save.
Mourner’s Cry: Once per turn when a creature within 15 feet of the Echo fails a Wisdom saving throw against you, it becomes Frightened of the Echo until the end of its next turn.
Grave Keeper: Allies within 10 feet of the Echo have Advantage on death saving throws; ordinary lower-Source-CL effects cannot remove their souls.
Unfinished Violence: Once per turn when you deal Psychic or Necrotic damage to a marked hostile creature within 15 feet of the Echo, add 2d8 damage.
Limits: Available at CL 14. Requires a corpse, grave, battlefield, death-haunted object, or at least 2 Gravebeats.
The Echo cannot use weapons, hold objects, flank, make Opportunity Attacks, maintain Concentration or provide a second copy of you.

The Echo does not automatically contain the corpse’s soul. An actual willing soul that remains and chooses to answer may shape its appearance and provide one sensory impression; it is not trapped, copied or permanently bound.

Cultivation Level 3 — Gravebeat

You begin the rhythm that every corpse remembers.

Bonus Action  
Cost: 1 Resonance  
Duration: The scene

While Gravebeat persists:

- You know the direction and broad category of corpses, undead, dying creatures, grave-soil, active death magic, and death-haunted objects within 30 feet, unless blocked by higher concealment.

player_card.summary: Strike a wounded or marked foe with grave force that spreads across the battlefield.

Effect: Choose one primary target: A Bloodied or Resonance Marked hostile creature standing on or touching earth, stone, grave-soil, a structure, or a battlefield surface. You may spend up to 3 Gravebeats; the target makes a Constitution saving throw.
Failure: 12d10 + Wisdom modifier Necrotic or Psychic damage, no regained HP until the end of its next turn, and knocked Prone. Choose one additional consequence below per Gravebeat spent.
Success: Half damage, and its next healing before the end of its next turn is halved. It is not knocked Prone.

Battlefield Afterbeat: Every other hostile creature you choose within 20 feet of the primary target touching the same continuous surface makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failure: 5d10 Psychic or Necrotic damage and no Reactions until the start of its next turn. Success: Half damage. Each creature is affected by at most one Afterbeat per activation.

Lower-Realm Interment: If this feature reduces an ordinary creature at least 5 Source CL below you to 0 HP, you may kill it outright, bury it under the blow’s spiritual weight or leave it dying, if the campaign’s stakes permit.

Against equal or higher authority, major enemies, divine protection, artifact death wards, Secret immortality, reincarnation authority, complete incorporeality or explicit immunity to earthbound death effects, use the printed save and damage. A successful Cultivation Check lets you suppress one relevant protection until the end of the target’s next turn; it does not permanently erase it.
Choices: Suppress one ordinary lower-Source-CL regeneration or death-prevention expression until the end of the scene.
Reduce its Speed to 0 until the start of your next turn.
Force it to lose Concentration.
Create a Grave Fracture under it: a 10-foot-radius area of Difficult Terrain lasting for the scene.
If it is undead, possessed, a haunt or externally soul-sustained, give Disadvantage on its next save to maintain that state.
Limits: Available at CL 18. Does not grant ownership of the dead, prevent lawful resurrection after the scene, destroy souls or overwrite dedicated death, burial, reincarnation or conceptual laws.

You strike the grave-rhythm beneath a living body and make the whole battlefield answer.

Action  
Range: 90 feet  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Requirement: A Bloodied or Resonance Marked hostile creature standing on or touching earth, stone, grave-soil, a structure, or a battlefield surface

Choose one primary target. You may spend up to 3 Gravebeats. The target makes a Constitution saving throw.

- suppress one ordinary lower-Source-CL regeneration or death-prevention expression until the end of the scene;
- reduce its Speed to 0 until the start of your next turn;
- force it to lose Concentration;
- create a Grave Fracture under it, a 10-foot-radius area of Difficult Terrain lasting for the scene;

Every other hostile creature of your choice within 20 feet of the primary target that is touching the same continuous surface makes a Wisdom saving throw.

On a successful Cultivation Check, you may suppress one relevant protection until the end of the target’s next turn, but you do not erase it permanently.

The Earth Beats Once does not grant ownership of the dead, prevent lawful resurrection after the scene, destroy souls, or overwrite dedicated death, burial, reincarnation, or conceptual laws.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.unwritten_footp.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 — No Trace Returns

Your movement can leave behind an explanation that excludes you.

Erase the Last Passage

Reaction  
You can use this when  A creature notices you, a ward identifies you, a tracking effect acquires your trail, or an attack targets you  
Cost: 5 Resonance

Move up to half your Speed by spiritual step. You may pass through occupied spaces and ordinary cover during this movement but not sealed solid barriers. You must end in a legal space.

Then choose one result:

- False Trail: Create a false spiritual trail from your former space to another point within 30 feet. Lower-Source-CL tracking follows it automatically. Equal authority contests it normally.
- Blank Interval: Creatures of your choice that witnessed the movement make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, they remember your former and final circumstances but not the route, speed, intermediate spaces, or technique used.
- Afterimage Victim: Against the triggering attack, leave a 1-HP afterimage Asset in your former space. If the attack can legally target it, the triggering attack targets the afterimage instead. The afterimage has AC equal to your Cultivation Save DC and vanishes after the attack or at the start of your next turn.
- Cut the Acquisition: One ordinary lower-Source-CL tracking lock, scrying lock, scent lock, Resonance lock, or targeting mark on you ends. Equal or higher authority requires a Cultivation Check.

Ghost Through the Hold

When Erase the Last Passage moves you while Grappled or Restrained, make a Cultivation Check against the restraint’s escape DC or Source Rule. On a success, the restraint ends and you move. On a failure, you remain in place, but can still choose False Trail or Blank Interval.

Soul Splitting — False Author

Your soul fragment can appear to be the source of your Mind Spike or Spiritual Pressure. When you originate either from your space, you may make it appear to originate from the fragment. This changes perceived attribution, not actual range or line of effect, unless another feature already allows the fragment as an origin.

player_card.summary: Gain a brief movement, task or attack by taking on Time Debt.

Effect: Choose one option below. The ordinary options create 1 Time Debt; the weapon-attack and Mind Spike options create 2 Time Debt.

Pay the Second Back: At the start of your turn, before moving, taking an Action or Bonus Action, or using a Reaction, you may choose to pay the current. Until the start of your next turn, your Speed becomes 0, you cannot take Reactions or use Borrowed Second, and you cannot voluntarily move, teleport, spiritually step, conceptually translate or activate a Source Rule whose primary effect moves you. Then remove 2 Time Debt.

Involuntary movement neither cancels this payment nor restores voluntary movement. Declare payment before the turn’s actions; you cannot do so after benefiting from movement, a Reaction or another Well of Hours feature during that turn.
Choices: Move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Stand from Prone and move up to 10 feet.
Draw, stow, pick up, hand off, open, close or manipulate one ordinary object.
Use Spiritual Sense or Soul Gaze.
Take the Disengage or Search action.
Make one attack with a weapon you are already proficient with against a creature bearing your Resonance Mark within the weapon’s normal reach or range.
Use Mind Spike against a creature bearing your Resonance Mark; reduce its damage by one die, to a minimum of one die.
Limits: Available at CL 6. Borrowed Second cannot activate a Domain; a CL 10-or-higher Subpath feature; Soul Vessel, Soul Splitting or another feature creating a separately acting Asset; a full multi-packet Forged Technique; or an item power usable once per scene or less often.
It cannot activate another feature whose primary effect grants an additional Action, Bonus Action, Reaction or turn, or be used during a turn granted by another extra-turn effect.

player_card.summary: Create a Well of Hours that aids allies, delays foes and can restore a recorded moment.

Effect: Area: 30-foot-radius sphere. It becomes a Well of Hours, a spiritual-temporal field and Source Rule.

When it appears, record each creature you choose currently inside: its space, current HP and ordinary conditions. This is its Round Image. At the start of each of your turns, replace the image of each chosen creature currently in the field with its current state.
You may choose a creature that enters after the field appears. If chosen and still inside, it gains its Round Image at the start of your next turn.
Friendly Current: Each willing creature you choose that starts its turn in the field chooses one benefit below.

Hostile Undertow: The first time each round a hostile creature in the field voluntarily moves, attacks, activates a technique or takes a Reaction, it makes a Wisdom saving throw. Failure: Apply Delayed Movement, Delayed Strike, Delayed Technique or Delayed Reaction without spending Resonance or gaining Time Debt; it also becomes Resonance Marked until the end of its next turn. Success: Choose Speed reduced by 10 feet or no Reactions until the start of its next turn.
After two successes against Hostile Undertow in this activation, a creature is immune to it for the remainder of the activation unless your Source CL increases.

Return to the Bell: Once during the activation, when a creature you choose in the field takes damage, fails a save, is moved, gains a condition or is reduced to 0 HP, you may use your Reaction to return it to its Round Image. Place it in its recorded space or the nearest legal space within 15 feet; if recorded HP is higher, set HP to that value; remove ordinary conditions gained since the image.

After Return to the Bell, set your Time Debt to maximum and take 3d10 Psychic damage. This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity and cannot be redirected, deferred, transferred or reduced by a Well of Hours feature.

Drink the Unlived Hour: Once on each of your turns, you may gain 1 Time Debt to use Borrowed Second without spending Resonance. Its weapon-attack or Mind Spike option can be chosen only once during this entire activation.

Collapse of the Well: When the field ends, every Deferred Consequence whose subject is inside resolves immediately unless already answered; convert your remaining Time Debt into Temporal Arrears normally.
Choices: Friendly Current — Step: Move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Friendly Current — Rise: Stand from Prone without spending movement.
Friendly Current — Prepare: Draw or stow one item and use Spiritual Sense.
Friendly Current — Endure: Gain Temporary HP equal to 2 × your PB.
Friendly Current — Relief: Suppress one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect on itself until the end of the turn.
Limits: Available at CL 18. Return to the Bell restores no Resonance, Stamina, Qi, Hit Dice, item charges, consumed materials, actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, movement, Concentration, Sphere resources, Insight uses, Domain activations or other spent resources.

It cannot restore a destroyed Cultivation Asset, severed limb, broken Foundation, consumed soul, permanent Hidden Injury, completed death or higher-authority consequence unless both a successful Cultivation Check and the originating Source Rule permit temporal restoration.

To activate this feature again, you must have no Time Debt or Temporal Arrears and, after the previous field ends, complete the Temporal Arrears clearing procedure even if no Arrears remained. This uses that cultivation-recharge procedure, not a short-rest or long-rest limit.

Higher-Source-CL Time, Fate, Void, Samsara, Boundary, Seal, Formation, divine, artifact or conceptual authority can contest individual field operations. Ordinary anti-magic does not automatically erase it unless it also suppresses cultivation Source Rules.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.well_of_hours.f.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 — The Well Has No Bottom

You reveal the local truth that every present moment rests above an immeasurable depth of moments that might have been.

Action  
Range: 90 feet  
Area: 30-foot-radius sphere  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute

The area becomes a Well of Hours, a spiritual-temporal field and Source Rule.

When the field appears, record the following for every creature of your choice currently in the area:

- its space;
- its current Hit Points;
- its ordinary conditions.

This record is its Round Image.

At the start of each of your turns, replace the Round Image of each chosen creature currently in the field with its current state. When a creature enters the field after it appears, you may choose it for the field. If chosen and still in the field, it gains a Round Image at the start of your next turn.

Friendly Current

Each willing creature you choose that starts its turn in the field chooses one benefit:

- move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks;
- stand from Prone without spending movement;
- draw or stow one item and use Spiritual Sense;
- gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 2 × your Proficiency Bonus;
- suppress one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect on itself until the end of the turn.

Hostile Undertow

The first time each round a hostile creature in the field voluntarily moves, makes an attack, activates a technique, or takes a Reaction, it makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save: Apply Delayed Movement, Delayed Strike, Delayed Technique, or Delayed Reaction without spending Resonance or gaining Time Debt. The creature also becomes Resonance Marked until the end of its next turn.

Successful Save: Choose one:

- reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of its next turn;
- it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

A creature that succeeds against Hostile Undertow twice during the same activation becomes immune to it for the remainder of that activation unless your Source CL increases.

Return to the Bell

Once during the activation, when a creature of your choice in the field takes damage, fails a saving throw, is moved, gains a condition, or is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you may use your Reaction to return it to its Round Image.

- Place it in its recorded space or the nearest legal space within 15 feet.
- If the recorded Hit Point value is higher, set its Hit Points to that value.
- Remove ordinary conditions gained after the image was recorded.
- Restore no Resonance, Stamina, Qi, Hit Dice, item charges, consumed materials, actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, movement, Concentration, Sphere resources, Insight uses, Domain activations, or other spent resources.
- Do not restore a destroyed Cultivation Asset, severed limb, broken Foundation, consumed soul, permanent Hidden Injury, completed death, or higher-authority consequence unless a successful Cultivation Check and the originating Source Rule both permit temporal restoration.

After using Return to the Bell:

- set your Time Debt to its maximum;
- take 3d10 Psychic damage.

This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity and cannot be redirected, deferred, transferred, or reduced by a Well of Hours feature.

Drink the Unlived Hour

Once on each of your turns, you may gain 1 Time Debt to use Borrowed Second without spending Resonance.

You can choose Borrowed Second’s weapon-attack or Mind Spike option only once during the entire activation of The Well Has No Bottom.

Collapse of the Well

When the field ends:

- every Deferred Consequence whose subject is inside it resolves immediately unless already answered;
- your remaining Time Debt is converted into Temporal Arrears normally.

You cannot activate The Well Has No Bottom again until:

1. you have no Time Debt;
2. you have no Temporal Arrears;
3. after the previous field ends, you complete the Temporal Arrears clearing procedure, even if you had no Arrears remaining.

This is a defined cultivation-recharge procedure, not a short-rest or long-rest limit.
