tianxia.tradition.spirit.yokai_channeler.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 — Yokai’s Bargain

Yokai bargains are voluntary exchanges enforced by hospitality, appetite, clever wording, and spiritual face. They are not Oath-Ledger debts, Soul-Collateral Contracts, or Karma judgments.

Action or 10-minute negotiation  
Range: 30 feet during action use; conversational range during negotiation  
Cost: 3 Resonance  
Duration: Up to 24 hours

Offer a bargain to one creature that can understand the terms. State:

- What each party will give, do, refrain from doing, reveal, or protect.
- The duration or completion condition.
- Whether the bargain uses a Declared Claim or an Open Claim. A Declared Claim selects one Claim use from the printed Breach list when the bargain forms. An Open Claim permits the nonbreaching party to choose any one printed Claim use after breach. No consequence outside that list is created by this feature.

The bargain forms only if both parties knowingly accept. Magical coercion that removes meaningful choice prevents formation unless the bargain’s Source Rule expressly allows coerced contracts.

Each party gains a visible-to-spiritual-senses Bargain Mark. A party can bear only one Bargain Mark from you at a time.

Permitted Benefits

The bargain may grant each party one of the following while it remains honored:

- Advantage on one defined category of skill check directly related to fulfilling the bargain.
- A 10-foot increase to one movement mode while traveling toward the bargain’s objective.
- Temporary Hit Points equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus at the start of the first scene in which the bargain is actively pursued.
- The ability to communicate telepathically within 1 mile for purposes related to the bargain.
- Permission to cross one ward, threshold, territory, or hospitality boundary controlled by the other party, if that party has authority to grant permission.

Breach

When a party knowingly breaches, the nonbreaching party immediately knows the broad category of breach and gains one Yokai Claim against the violator. The Bargain Mark remains until the claim is used or the parties reconcile.

The claimant may spend the Claim in one of these ways:

- Impose Disadvantage on one d20 Test the violator makes within 60 feet.
- Gain Advantage on one saving throw against the violator.
- Learn the violator’s direction while on the same plane for 1 hour, unless blocked by equal or higher spiritual concealment.
- Deal 4d10 Psychic damage to the violator as a Reaction when it directly benefits from the breach. The violator makes a Charisma saving throw, taking half damage on a success.

A Yokai Claim cannot force future obedience, seize a soul, create unlimited pursuit, or punish an ambiguous technical breach. If the bargain’s meaning is genuinely disputed, resolve it through the stated terms, witnesses, and a Cultivation Check rather than automatic punishment.

Cultivation Level 18 — Ancestral Ascension

A great ancestor, composite lineage spirit, or perfected Office overshadows you without erasing your identity.

Bonus Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Duration: The scene  
Concentration: No

Choose one Ancestor Office as the Ascendant Office. You gain the following benefits:

- +2 AC.
- Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.
- You cannot be unwillingly possessed by an ordinary or lower-Source-CL effect.
- Borrow the Office for the Ascendant Office activates without cost and does not prevent you from maintaining one different borrowed Office.
- Once per turn when you activate a Spirit Awakening Path or Subpath feature, impose one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect on one creature Resonance Marked by you within 60 feet.
- You may originate Spirit Awakening features from yourself, your Soul Fragment, or one Ancestral Legion shade, but each activation still has only one origin unless a Source Rule says otherwise.

Ascendant Office Authority

Once during the activation, invoke the Office’s greater expression:

- Archivist — Precedent of the Dead: Ask one precise question about a creature, site, technique, lineage, or spiritual event perceived during the scene. If any ancestor genuinely knew the answer, receive it. Otherwise learn the closest relevant precedent and one missing source needed for certainty.
- Healer — Hands That Remember Life: Touch one creature or affect one ally within your Domain. Restore 8d8 + Wisdom modifier Hit Points and end one ordinary poison, disease, possession, curse, madness, or spiritual contamination.
- Magistrate — Judgment of the Lineage Court: One creature within 60 feet makes a Charisma saving throw. On failure, it must either cease one named hostile act for the scene or publicly state the genuine reason it refuses. A creature cannot be forced to reveal magically concealed information it does not consciously know.
- Warrior — Thousand Battles in One Body: Make one weapon attack, unarmed strike, or Cultivation Attack. On a hit, deal an additional 8d8 Force or Psychic damage and the target cannot take Reactions or regain Hit Points until the start of your next turn.
- Wayfarer — Road Remembered Before Birth: Move yourself and up to Proficiency Bonus willing creatures you can perceive to one legal place on the same plane that your lineage has physically reached and that you can name or identify through an accepted ancestral memory. Sealed boundaries and stronger route prohibitions still apply.
- Ritualist — Ceremony Without Error: Complete one ritual you know with a normal completion time of 8 hours or less as an Action, paying every printed Resonance, Cultivation Point, Offering, Hit Die, material, Anchor, and participant cost. The ritual must primarily perform one of these functions: spiritual diagnosis; ordinary exorcism or cleansing; burial or funerary passage; willing spirit communication; creation, repair, or consecration of a nonpermanent ward, vessel, shrine, or Spiritual Anchor; a recorded Offering, restitution, Bond renegotiation, or hospitality rite; or opening a legal same-plane route whose Source Rule already permits acceleration. The ritual’s Source CL cannot exceed yours. This expression cannot accelerate a breakthrough, training, Forged Technique creation, item creation, permanent companion creation, Complete-Soul reconstruction, resurrection, reincarnation, permanent transformation, Secret-Law initiation, tribulation, or any ritual that forbids acceleration.

Identity and Price

You remain the acting character. The ancestor cannot seize the character sheet, spend resources without your decision, or override player agency.

When Ancestral Ascension ends, make a Wisdom saving throw against your own Cultivation Save DC.

- Success: The ancestor withdraws cleanly.
- Failure: Gain 1 level of Exhaustion and your Soul Anchor becomes Strained until you complete a 1-hour reconciliation rite with the lineage.

If you acted directly against the recorded Lineage Taboo during the activation, the save automatically fails. This automatic failure is waived only when the prohibited act was the sole available way to prevent one of these recorded greater violations: the destruction of a Complete Soul; the permanent severance of the lineage’s recognized Soul Anchor; the death of a protected descendant, adopted successor, sworn kin, or student; or violation of a higher-ranked Duty written into the Lineage Covenant before the scene began.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.black_current_w.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 — No Bank Holds the River

Your soul no longer treats enemy control zones as fixed geography.

Continuous Current

You gain the following benefits:

- Your Speed increases by 10 feet.
- You gain a swim Speed equal to your Speed and can breathe while your spirit remains connected to your body, including underwater or in spiritual dream-rivers.
- Moving through a hostile creature’s space with a Black Current feature does not cost extra movement.
- Once on each of your turns, when you enter the space of a Resonance Marked hostile creature, you may exchange positions with it. The creature makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a success, the exchange fails, but your movement can continue through its space.
- When you leave a Grapple or ordinary Restrained effect through a Black Current spiritual step, make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s DC or Source Rule. On a success, the effect ends. On a failure, the movement fails and is not spent.

Undertow Pursuit

Reaction  
You can use this when  A Resonance Marked creature within 60 feet moves at least 15 feet, teleports, or is forcibly moved  
Cost: 4 Resonance

Move up to half your Speed by spiritual step toward a legal space within 10 feet of the target’s destination. This movement cannot cross a sealed boundary or exceed 60 feet even if your Speed is greater.

After arriving, choose one:

- use Mind Spike against the target, reducing its damage by one die;
- make one weapon attack against it with a weapon you are proficient with;
- impose one Spiritual Pressure effect on it without a save;
- move one willing creature adjacent to you 10 feet along your Soulwake.

A higher-Source-CL teleportation, boundary, concealment, or route effect can require a Cultivation Check to follow.

Soul Splitting — Tributary

Your soul fragment can occupy a space in your Soulwake without blocking it. Once per turn when you use Flow After the Strike, the fragment may move 10 feet along the wake. It cannot trigger Wake Mark or River-Cut Passage independently.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.boundary_walker.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 — Gate of No Return

You create a temporary border-prison by giving one marked threshold authority over a target’s return.

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Requirement: The target is Resonance Marked by you or currently crossing a meaningful threshold

Choose one creature. It makes a Charisma saving throw.

Failed Save: The target is exiled into a nearby border-realm. Remove it from the battlefield and create a Gate of No Return Anchor in an unoccupied space within 30 feet of where it vanished.

The Anchor has:

- AC: your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 10 × Proficiency Bonus
- Saving Throws: your Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throw bonuses
- Resistance: all damage from sources other than the exiled creature and creatures spiritually tied to it
- Source CL: yours

At the end of each of its turns, the exiled creature repeats the save.

- An equal- or higher-Source-CL creature returns after two successes.
- A lower-Source-CL creature returns after three successes.
- Destroying the Anchor immediately returns the creature.
- If you become Incapacitated, the creature gains Advantage on its next save.

While exiled, the creature can perceive a symbolic border-prison and can attack the Anchor spiritually using its normal attack or Cultivation Attack Modifier. It cannot target other battlefield creatures, receive ordinary healing from them, or use the border-realm as a legal destination for unrelated teleportation.

When the creature returns, place it in the nearest unoccupied space of your choice within 30 feet of the Anchor. It suffers two different Spiritual Pressure effects until the start of its next turn.

Successful Save: It remains, but until the end of its next turn it cannot teleport, become incorporeal, enter a creature or object, or cross planar or spiritual boundaries. It also suffers one Spiritual Pressure effect.

Permanent Exile Boundary

Gate of No Return does not permanently exile a major enemy, destroy a route, erase a homeland connection, or close a world-scale Gate. Such outcomes require a dedicated ritual, lawful destination, suitable Anchors, Source CL superiority, and a separate ritual Source Rule.

Threshold Mark Profile: When hostile effects depend on it, a marked threshold can be attacked or cleansed as an Anchor. AC 12 + PB; Hit Points 5 × PB; Resistance to Psychic and Force; Immunity to Poison and Disease.

Cultivation Level 14 — All Eyes Open

Bonus Action  
Cost: 6 Resonance  
Duration: The scene

Manifest a Choir of Unopened Eyes, a Spirit Awakening field extending 30 feet from you. Invisible spiritual eyes, reflected faces, harmonized whispers, or rings of unreadable script fill the field.

While the field lasts:

- You cannot be surprised by a spiritually perceptible creature in the field unless protected by higher authority.
- Ordinary invisibility, ordinary illusion, mundane disguise, and ordinary voice mimicry cannot grant Advantage against you.
- Hostile creatures of your choice have Disadvantage on Deception checks made in the field and on saves made to maintain ordinary disguises or illusions against your observation.
- A creature bearing your Witness Note cannot teleport, cross a planar boundary, or spiritually project out of the field without leaving a visible departure chord that identifies the direction and broad method used.
- Once per round when a hostile creature in the field becomes Resonance Marked or contradicts a witnessed statement, impose one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect on it.

Chorus Assets

When the field manifests, create three Unopened Eyes. They are stationary Cultivation Assets placed in unoccupied spaces you can see in the field.

Each Eye has:

- Type and Size: Tiny stationary Spirit Cultivation Asset
- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 3 × Proficiency Bonus
- Speed: 0 feet
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
- Damage Immunities: Poison and Psychic
- Condition Immunities: Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained
- Perception: Shares your Spiritual Sense within 15 feet of itself
- At 0 Hit Points: It is destroyed, deals the printed Psychic damage to you, and leaves no creature or corpse.

An Eye does not take a turn. Once on each of your turns, choose one surviving Eye as the origin of Spiritual Sense, Soul Gaze, Hymn of Stillness, Forced Confession, or a technique that expressly permits a spiritual Asset as its origin.

Destroying all three Eyes ends the field. If an Eye is destroyed, you take Psychic damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Soul Splitting cannot duplicate these Eyes or grant them independent actions.

Closed Testimony

tianxia.tradition.spirit.compass_breakin.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 — Heaven Has No Fixed North

You manifest a battlefield in which orientation follows cultivated intent rather than passive geography.

Bonus Action  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Area: 40-foot-radius aura centered on you  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required

The aura is your Compass Domain and moves with you.

Chosen Bearings

At the start of each chosen ally's turn in the Domain, it may declare Approach, Orbit, or Depart relative to you. If it completes that movement category during the turn, it gains the matching benefit until the start of its next turn:

- Approach: Temporary Hit Points equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus.
- Orbit: +2 AC against Opportunity Attacks and attacks made as Reactions.
- Depart: 10 feet of additional movement that must be used before the turn ends.

A creature can gain one Chosen Bearing benefit per turn. These benefits do not create your Bearing tokens.

False North

At the start of each of your turns, choose one hostile creature in the Domain as your False North until the start of your next turn. It counts as your Pole without ending your underlying Pole.

You gain one temporary token of each Bearing relative to the False North. These temporary tokens expire at the start of your next turn and cannot be carried outside the Domain.

Turn the Whole Field

Bonus Action  
Limit: Once per turn

Choose one Resonance Marked hostile creature in the Domain. It makes a Wisdom saving throw. Choose Approach, Orbit, or Depart relative to you.

- Failed Save: Move it up to 15 feet in the chosen category, and it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Successful Save: Move it 5 feet in the chosen category if a legal space exists. It retains its Reactions.

For Orbit, the final space must be within 5 feet of the creature's original distance from you. A creature protected by higher-Source-CL anchoring, Space, Formation, Boundary, or bodily authority can force a Cultivation Check.

Compass-Breaking Procession

Once on each of your turns, you may use Break the Four Directions against your False North without paying its Resonance cost. You may spend no more than two temporary Bearing tokens on this free use, and its added damage is 2d8 + 1d8 per token spent. You cannot also use a paid Break the Four Directions during the same turn.

No Direction of Escape

Once during the activation, when a Resonance Marked hostile creature in the Domain teleports, uses conceptual movement, enters a route, or crosses the Domain's boundary, you may use your Reaction to contest that movement.

Make a Cultivation Check against the movement's Source Rule.

- Success: Choose one result:
  - If the movement has a traversed path, it ends at the last legal space no farther than half the declared distance from its origin.
  - If it is teleportation or another pathless relocation, it arrives in a legal space you choose within 10 feet of the geometric halfway point between origin and declared destination; if no such space exists, it arrives in the nearest legal space to that midpoint that the movement's own Source Rule could reach.
  - It arrives in the nearest legal space still inside the Domain.
  - It completes the movement, and you move to a legal space within 10 feet of its destination.
- Failure: The movement resolves normally, but you learn its destination direction and whether it crossed Space, Boundary, Time, Formation, Void, or another route authority.

No Direction of Escape cannot follow a creature across planes or into an unknown sealed location unless the opposing Source Rule already permits that relation.

Domain Collision and Ending

A conflicting Domain that fixes direction, seals movement, controls gravity, establishes absolute geometry, or denies conceptual relation contests by Source CL and then Cultivation Check if necessary. Losing the contest suppresses only the contradictory Compass expression.

When the Domain ends, temporary Bearings and False North end. Creatures are not moved merely because ordinary orientation returns.

Cultivation Level 18 — Dream Eater Ascension

You enter the vulnerable inner dream and consume something the target uses to remain psychologically whole.

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 10 Resonance and up to 3 Dream Morsels  
Target requirement: Sleeping, helpless, in Cursed Sleep, or bearing both your Resonance Mark and Nightmare Scar  
Duration: Instantaneous injury; stolen effects persist as described

The target makes a Wisdom saving throw. It has Disadvantage if you spent at least 2 Dream Morsels and it is asleep or helpless.

Failed Save

The target takes 10d10 Psychic damage. Choose one Consumption:

- Recent Memory: Remove one significant memory formed within the last 30 days. The target knows a gap exists but cannot access the content.
- Restful Dream: The target cannot receive recovery benefits from a Long Rest until it completes one successful Devoured-Dream Recovery. It can still sleep, avoid ordinary sleep-deprivation consequences, and complete a Full Cultivation Session if another rule permits; only the Long Rest benefits are withheld.
- Practiced Confidence: Suppress one skill proficiency, tool proficiency, or language linked to a memory you have identified. This cannot suppress a Path, Sphere, talent, Method, Foundation, Insight, or entire ability score.
- Defining Hope: Suppress one stated aspiration, source of courage, or positive bond. While suppressed, the target has Disadvantage on saves against Frightened and cannot use that hope as a Soul Anchor invocation. This does not sever or replace the Soul Anchor itself.
- Prepared Dream: Suppress one dream-based, memory-based, or emotional technique the target has used or revealed during the scene. The suppression lasts until recovery and cannot affect a feature of higher minimum CL than your Source CL.

You retain the consumed content as a Devoured Dream. You can hold only one Devoured Dream at a time. While holding it:

- Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to half the Psychic damage dealt.
- Gain one relevant language, skill proficiency, or narrow emotional insight if the consumed content supports it.
- You can reproduce the consumed memory or dream as an illusion or symbolic vision.

Holding a Devoured Dream does not give you the victim’s Path, Sphere, technique, statistics, true identity, or Soul Anchor.

Successful Save

The target takes half damage, suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect, and you may steal one ordinary Dream Fragment under Stolen Dreams without additional cost.

Recovery

The target can recover the consumed content through one of these routes:

- Spiritual Exorcism followed by a Full Cultivation Session and a successful Wisdom or Charisma saving throw against your Cultivation Save DC.
- A Dreams, Spirit, Medicine, Memory, Samsara, Karma, or appropriate Secret-Law procedure that explicitly restores lost memory or identity content.
- Destroying or forcing you to release the Devoured Dream, followed by a Long Rest or Full Cultivation Session.
- Completing the Witnessed Reconstruction procedure in the Procedure Addendum using witnesses, journals, Soul Anchor relationships, dream records, or lived repetition.

An equal- or-higher-Source-CL Consumption requires the printed Source CL contest or a restoration Source Rule of equal or higher authority. Secret, divine, artifact, tribulation, or conceptual protection uses its own explicit counterprocedure; this feature does not create an undefined quest requirement. A Devoured Dream cannot be permanently destroyed merely because you die; it is released as recoverable spiritual residue unless another explicit effect consumes it.

Hunger’s Reflection

While holding a Devoured Dream, Soul Gaze and spiritual diagnosis can perceive that you contain another creature’s dream-content. If you retain it through a Full Cultivation Session, make a Wisdom saving throw against your own Cultivation Save DC. On failure, roll or choose one Dream Intrusion from the Procedure Addendum. It persists until you release the dream or complete Spiritual Exorcism on yourself. This is a spiritual consequence, not the mechanical Daemonic tag.

Soul Splitting Expression — Mouth Behind Sleep

While Soul Splitting is active, your Soul Fragment may enter the outer threshold of a dream through Dream Walker and may serve as the origin for Nightmare Touch or Sleeping Curse. You still activate the feature once, pay one cost, and cannot affect a target through total cover unless the dream connection already exists.

You can approach the edge of another creature’s dream without immediately harming it.

Ritual or Action  
Range: 1 mile during the ritual; 60 feet during action use  
Cost: 1 Resonance  
Duration: Up to 10 minutes during the ritual; until the end of your next turn during action use

Choose one sleeping creature whose broad location you know, or one sleeping or Resonance Marked creature you can perceive.

A willing creature admits you automatically. An unwilling creature makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save

You enter the dream’s outer threshold. Your body remains where it is, and this is not Astral Projection. You may:

- Speak to the dreamer in symbolic or ordinary language.
- Present one image, sensation, warning, or memory you willingly disclose.
- Learn the dream’s dominant emotional tone.
- Determine whether another dream intruder, nightmare parasite, memory seal, or obvious dream curse is present.
- Create a Resonance Mark on the dreamer that lasts until it wakes or until the normal mark duration expires after waking, whichever is later.

You cannot deal damage, compel behavior, steal information, rewrite memory, or move beyond the outer dream through Dream Walker alone.

Successful Save

You perceive that the dream is closed, warded, lucidly defended, absent, or beyond your current authority. You do not learn its content.

Defended Dreams

A ward, Spirit technique, Dreams technique, trained lucid dreamer, Soul Anchor, spirit companion, equal- or higher-Source-CL soul, or creature that does not truly dream can block entry or require a Cultivation Check. On failure, you cannot attempt Dream Walker against that creature again until its dream changes or the next scene begins.

Wakeful Taste

When a creature Resonance Marked by you within 60 feet becomes Frightened or fails a save against Mind Spike, choose one of these categories and learn its result:

- A symbolic image associated with its present fear.
- Whether it slept normally during its last long rest.
- Whether a nightmare, dream parasite, or dream-derived memory currently influences it.

This does not reveal a hidden fact merely because the target fears discovery.

Cultivation Level 6 — Nightmare Touch

You can bite into the spiritual residue of sleep, helplessness, or a marked fear.

Action

The target makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save: It takes 4d8 + Wisdom modifier Psychic damage, gains a Nightmare Scar, and cannot regain Hit Points from sleep or rest until the start of your next turn. Successful Save: It takes half damage and does not gain a Scar.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.dream_eater.fea.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 — Sleeping Curse

You can drag an exhausted or spiritually opened soul into predatory sleep even during battle.

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 6 Resonance  
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute

Choose one creature that is Bloodied, Frightened, Resonance Marked by you, or bearing your Nightmare Scar. It makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save

The creature falls into Cursed Sleep. It is Unconscious, falls Prone if able, and cannot be awakened by ordinary noise or an ally’s simple action.

At the end of each of its turns, it repeats the saving throw, ending the effect on a success. It also immediately repeats the save with Advantage when it takes damage.

While it sleeps, you may use one of these options once on each of your turns:

- Feed: Spend 1 Dream Morsel. The sleeper takes 3d10 Psychic damage and you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to half the damage dealt. This damage grants the normal immediate repeat save with Advantage.
- Question: Ask one question about a fear, dream, or recent emotionally important event. The sleeper’s dream answers symbolically. Protected information can require a Cultivation Check.
- Deepen the Scar: The target’s Nightmare Scar cannot be removed by an ordinary long-rest save until after the next scene.
- Maintain Stillness: The target does not repeat the save at the end of this turn, but you cannot choose this option on consecutive turns.

Successful Initial Save

The target becomes Drowsy until the end of its next turn: its Speed is halved, it cannot take Reactions, and it suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect.

Intervention

An ally adjacent to the sleeper may use an Action to perform one intervention:

- Inflict damage, granting the repeat save with Advantage.
- Invoke the sleeper’s Soul Anchor, true name, or meaningful bond, granting an immediate repeat save.
- Use Spiritual Exorcism, a Dreams or Spirit technique, or a suitable stimulant or ritual.
- Contest your Source CL with a Cultivation Check to break the curse’s dream connection.

Lower-Realm Dominance

A substantially lower-Source-CL ordinary creature that fails the initial save cannot wake through ordinary immunity to magical sleep unless the immunity explicitly protects the soul or dreams. It retains the printed repeat saves and intervention procedures.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.dream_eater.fea.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 — Stolen Dreams

You can take usable fragments of fear, longing, and recent dream-memory.

You can use this when  A creature bearing your Nightmare Scar fails its save against Mind Spike, Nightmare Touch, Domain Pressure, or another Dream Eater feature.  
Cost: 2 Resonance or 1 Dream Morsel  
Limit: Once per turn

Choose one Dream Fragment to steal:

- A recent dream image.
- A surface fear relevant to the current scene.
- A person, place, or object presently associated with safety or danger.
- One ordinary emotional vulnerability.
- One language fragment, face, route, or sensory memory encountered during the last 24 hours.

Protected memories, sealed secrets, Soul Anchor material, training secrets, plot-critical knowledge, and memories hidden by equal or higher authority require a Cultivation Check. On failure, you learn the category of protection rather than the memory.

You can retain a number of Stolen Dreams equal to your Wisdom modifier, minimum 1. A Stolen Dream lasts until your next Full Cultivation Session unless preserved through a legal item, Sphere, ritual, or Insight. When you exceed the limit, release one existing fragment.

Spend a Stolen Dream

As a Bonus Action, release one retained fragment for one benefit:

- Gain Advantage on one Insight, Investigation, Perception, Persuasion, Deception, or Survival check directly related to the fragment.
- Give the original creature Disadvantage on one attack roll or saving throw it makes against you before the end of your next turn by confronting it with the fragment.
- Reproduce one harmless sensory image, voice, scent, or dream-symbol for up to 1 minute.
- Find the direction of a person, place, or object shown in the fragment if it is within 1 mile and not hidden by stronger authority.

Releasing the fragment removes it from you but does not erase it from the original creature.

Memory Theft Boundary

Stolen Dreams reads or copies a fragment; it does not remove a proficiency, delete an entire relationship, replace identity, or grant the full knowledge required to use another creature’s feature, Sphere, manual, password system, or Secret.

player_card.summary: Impose Disadvantage on an attack roll by catching the attacker’s intent in a dream.

Effect: Trigger: A creature you can perceive within 60 feet makes an attack roll.
If the triggering attack already has Disadvantage, instead subtract your PB after the roll but before the result is announced; do not add a third die.
If the attack misses, choose one miss option below.
Threaded Reverie: When you use Soul Gaze on a creature bearing your Dream Thread, you may learn one additional item below.
Choices: Miss — mark: The attacker becomes Resonance Marked by you.
Miss — thread: Create a Dream Thread on the attacker.
Threaded Reverie — emotion: Learn the strongest emotion currently shaping its next intended action.
Threaded Reverie — state: Learn whether it is asleep, dreaming, affected by a dream intrusion or maintaining an illusion.
Threaded Reverie — symbol: Learn the symbolic image its current fear or desire would take in a dream.
Limits: Available at CL 3.

Cannot alter an attack you cannot spiritually perceive, an environmental collapse without an attacker, or an effect expressly immune to alteration by Reactions. A blind, invisible or incorporeal attacker can be affected if Spiritual Sense or another legal sense perceives it.
Threaded Reverie provides diagnosis, not private memories, hidden mechanics or an exact future action.

Cultivation Level 3 — Dream Stitch

Reaction  
You can use this when  A creature you can perceive within 60 feet makes an attack roll.  
Cost: 1 Resonance

Stitch a moment of dream hesitation into the attacker’s intent. Impose Disadvantage on the triggering attack roll.

If the attack misses, choose one:

- The attacker becomes Resonance Marked by you.
- Create a Dream Thread on the attacker.

If the attack already had Disadvantage, Dream Stitch does not add a third die. Instead, subtract your Proficiency Bonus from the attack roll after the roll is made but before the result is announced.

Dream Stitch cannot alter an attack you cannot spiritually perceive, an environmental collapse with no attacking creature, or an effect that expressly cannot be altered by Reactions. It can affect a blind, invisible, or incorporeal attacker if Spiritual Sense or another legal sense perceives that attacker.

When you use Soul Gaze on a creature bearing your Dream Thread, you may learn one additional item:

- The strongest emotion presently shaping its next intended action.
- Whether it is asleep, dreaming, affected by a dream intrusion, or maintaining an illusion.
- The symbolic image through which its current fear or desire would appear in a dream.

This is diagnostic information. It does not reveal private memories, hidden mechanics, or an exact future action.

player_card.summary: Create a protective Dream Refuge when you fall to 0 Hit Points.

Effect: Trigger: You would be reduced to 0 Hit Points while conscious and your soul is not sealed, possessed, or prevented from dreaming.

Fall Unconscious without immediately starting death saves. Create a 20-foot Emanation centered on your body for up to 3 rounds. This Dream Field uses your body as its sole Anchor; your body keeps its normal AC, Hit Points, size and conditions.
While the Refuge exists, you are stable. Your body has Resistance to all damage except Psychic, Force and damage from effects that can strike dreams or souls.

An enemy makes a Wisdom saving throw when it first enters the Refuge on a turn or starts its turn there. Failure: Dream Sleep until the end of its next turn, until it takes damage, or until another creature uses an action to wake it. Success: Speed reduced by 10 feet and no Reactions until the start of its next turn.

An ally in the Refuge may use an Action for one Refuge Recall method below. A successful Recall restores your consciousness and Hit Points equal to 2 × PB, ending the Refuge. A creature can attempt only one Recall during this Refuge unless it uses a different listed method.
At the end of the third round, if no ally wakes you and you remain alive, awaken with 1 Hit Point and 1 level of Exhaustion; the Refuge ends.

If an equal- or higher-Source-CL anti-dream effect breaks the Refuge, you become stable but lose its other protections. At the start of your next turn, begin death saves normally if still at 0 Hit Points.
Choices: Refuge Recall — shared memory: Speak your name and at least one specific shared event in a sentence of no more than 25 words.
Refuge Recall — Soul Anchor: Invoke one recorded Soul Anchor relationship or principle.
Refuge Recall — healing: Spend and resolve a legal healing feature on you.
Refuge Recall — check: While physically touching your body, succeed on a Wisdom (Medicine), Wisdom (Insight) or Charisma (Performance or Persuasion) check against your Cultivation Save DC.

Dream Double: While Soul Splitting is active, you may choose this Subpath Expression. Move your Soul Fragment up to 20 feet without provoking reactions from spirit-affecting creatures. One creature bearing your Dream Thread within 30 feet of the fragment has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the start of your next turn.
Limits: Available at CL 14.

The Refuge is not a separate targetable Asset. An effect directly suppressing dreams, Fields, souls or spiritual Anchors may contest it under the Source CL rules without first destroying a separate object.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.dreamweaver.fea.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 — Eternal Dream Refuge

You cultivate a hidden dream-body that catches you when the waking body collapses.

You can use this when  You would be reduced to 0 Hit Points while conscious and your soul is not sealed, possessed, or prevented from dreaming.  
Cost: 6 Resonance  
Limit: Once per scene

You fall Unconscious at 0 Hit Points but do not immediately begin making death saving throws. Create a Dream Refuge in a 20-foot Emanation centered on your body. The Refuge lasts for up to 3 rounds. It is a Dream Field anchored to your body, not a separate targetable Asset. Your body is its sole Anchor and retains its normal AC, Hit Points, size, and conditions. An effect that can directly suppress dreams, Fields, souls, or spiritual Anchors may contest the Refuge under the Source CL rules without first destroying a separate object.

While the Refuge exists:

- You are stable.
- Your body has Resistance to all damage except Psychic, Force, and damage from an effect that can strike dreams or souls.
- Enemies that first enter the Refuge on a turn or start their turn there make a Wisdom saving throw.
- On a failed save, a creature falls into Dream Sleep until the end of its next turn, until it takes damage, or until another creature uses an action to wake it.
- On a successful save, its Speed is reduced by 10 feet and it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- An ally in the Refuge can use an Action to complete one Refuge Recall: speak your name and at least one specific shared event in a sentence of no more than 25 words; invoke one recorded Soul Anchor relationship or principle; spend and resolve a legal healing feature on you; or succeed on a Wisdom (Medicine), Wisdom (Insight), or Charisma (Performance or Persuasion) check against your Cultivation Save DC while physically touching your body. A successful Recall restores you to consciousness with Hit Points equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus, and the Refuge ends. A creature can attempt only one Recall during the same Refuge unless it uses a different listed method.

At the end of the third round, if no ally wakes you and you remain alive, you awaken with 1 Hit Point, gain 1 level of Exhaustion, and the Refuge ends.

If the Dream Refuge is broken by an equal- or higher-Source-CL anti-dream effect, you become stable but lose its other protections and begin death saving throws normally at the start of your next turn if still at 0 Hit Points.

Soul Splitting Expression — Dream Double

While Soul Splitting is active, you may use Dream Double as your Subpath Expression. Move your Soul Fragment up to 20 feet without provoking reactions from spirit-affecting creatures. player_card.summary: Reroll a completed d20 Test or move a Dream Thread to another creature.

Effect: Trigger: You, an ally you can perceive, or a creature bearing your Dream Thread within 60 feet completes a d20 Test.
Choose one revision below. The revision must pass through one of your Dream Threads; it is not Fate alteration.

Lucid Resistance: Gain Advantage on saves against sleep, dream intrusion, nightmare effects and memory alterations through dreams. When you succeed, you may spend 1 Resonance to identify the effect’s direction, dream-symbol or spiritual signature if its Source CL does not exceed yours. Equal or higher authority can require a Cultivation Check.
Choices: Rehearse Success: If you or an ally made the Test, reroll it and use the new roll.
Rehearse Failure: If a hostile creature bearing your Dream Thread made the Test, force a reroll; it must use the new roll.

Change the Symbol: Instead of rerolling, move your Dream Thread from the creature involved in the Test to another creature you can perceive within 30 feet of it. The new creature makes a Wisdom saving throw and receives the Thread on failure.
Limits: Available at CL 10.
Use before the Test’s consequences produce a new independent roll, instance of damage, movement or another completed activation.
Cannot reroll a natural 20 that an explicit rule makes unalterable, or modify breakthrough, training, forging or tribulation resolution unless a Source Rule explicitly permits dream intervention.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.dreamweaver.fea.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 — Waking Dream Revision

You can revise a moment by forcing the soul to rehearse a different dream-version of it. This is not Fate alteration; the revision must pass through one of your Dream Threads.

Reaction  
You can use this when  You, an ally you can perceive, or a creature bearing your Dream Thread within 60 feet completes a d20 Test.  
Cost: 3 Resonance  
Limit: Once per round

Choose one of the following:

- Rehearse Success: If the Test was made by you or an ally, reroll it. The new roll must be used.
- Rehearse Failure: If the Test was made by a hostile creature bearing your Dream Thread, force it to reroll. The new roll must be used.
- Change the Symbol: Do not reroll. Instead, move your Dream Thread from the creature involved in the Test to another creature you can perceive within 30 feet of it. The new creature makes a Wisdom saving throw, receiving the Thread on a failure.

You must use Waking Dream Revision before the Test’s consequences produce a new independent roll, damage packet, movement, or another completed activation. It cannot reroll a natural 20 where an explicit rule makes that result unalterable, and it cannot modify breakthrough, training, forging, or tribulation resolution unless a Source Rule explicitly permits dream intervention.

Lucid Resistance

You have Advantage on saving throws against sleep, dream intrusion, nightmare effects, and memory alterations that occur through dreams. When you succeed on such a save, you may spend 1 Resonance to identify the effect’s direction, dream-symbol, or spiritual signature if its Source CL does not exceed yours. Equal or higher authority can require a Cultivation Check.

tianxia.tradition.spirit.dreamweaver.fea.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 — World of One

You isolate one soul inside a personal dream-world whose symbols obey your cultivated authority.

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Duration: The scene  
Concentration: Yes

Choose one creature you can perceive. A creature bearing your Dream Thread makes the initial saving throw with Disadvantage. The target makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save

The target’s consciousness is drawn into a World of One. Its body becomes Incapacitated, falls Prone if able, and cannot perceive or affect the ordinary battlefield. The body remains present and can be moved or damaged.

At the end of each of its turns, the target takes 6d10 Psychic damage and may attempt to escape by choosing one procedure:

- Repeat the Wisdom saving throw.
- Make an Intelligence (Investigation), Wisdom (Insight), or Charisma (Performance or Persuasion) check against your Cultivation Save DC to identify, accept, reinterpret, or break the governing dream-symbol.
- Destroy a dream Anchor that you manifest inside the World. The Anchor has AC equal to your Cultivation Save DC, Hit Points equal to 5 × your Proficiency Bonus, and can be damaged only by the target’s spiritual, cultivated, magical, or symbolic actions.

A successful procedure ends the effect. The target chooses one procedure each turn; it does not attempt all three.

Successful Initial Save

The target takes half of 6d10 Psychic damage, suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect, and you may create a Dream Thread on it.

Authority and Realm

- A creature whose Source CL is at least 5 lower than yours and that fails the initial save cannot use an ordinary legendary resistance or mundane immunity to ignore the dream unless that protection explicitly applies to dream entry, soul isolation, or conceptual imprisonment.
- An equal- or higher-Source-CL target retains every printed escape procedure and may contest a contradictory dream law with a Cultivation Check.
- A mindless entity, a being that truly cannot dream, or a creature with no coherent soul is immune unless another Source Rule gives you an appropriate dream-symbol or consciousness route.
- Damage dealt to the target’s body grants it Advantage on its next escape attempt but does not automatically end World of One.
- If your Concentration ends, the target returns immediately and knows it was attacked through a dream.

Domain Integration

While Domain Manifestation is active, you may originate World of One from yourself or your Soul Fragment. A target inside your Domain that bears both your Resonance Mark and Dream Thread cannot benefit from ordinary sleep immunity on the initial save; equal- or higher-authority immunity remains valid.

player_card.summary: Store spiritual events as Living Entries and spend them to reduce their consequences.

Effect: Manifest a Living Chronicle as pages, floating script, carved tablets or remembered verses. Choose up to PB creatures you can perceive as Recorded Souls for the duration.

Without an action, you may record a Living Entry when a Recorded Soul succeeds or fails an Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma save; fails a death save; is reduced to 0 Hit Points; becomes Charmed, Frightened, possessed, spiritually transformed or identity-wounded; loses Concentration; has a Soul Anchor, Cultivation Asset, spiritual bond or companion bond suppressed; or willingly makes a defining vow, confession, sacrifice or betrayal.
Maintain up to PB Living Entries. Recording beyond that maximum erases the oldest.
Rewrite the Margin: Once on each of your turns, you may spend 4 Resonance and consume one relevant Living Entry for one lesser result below.

A rewrite applies as printed against an ordinary lower-Source-CL effect. Against equal or higher, Rare, Forbidden, Secret, divine, artifact, tribulation, Foundation, Method, bloodline, true-name, reincarnation or campaign-scale authority, make a Cultivation Check. Failure: The Entry is not consumed; the rewrite does not occur, and you learn one required recovery or counterprocedure.
Choices: Erase one recorded failed death saving throw.
Reduce the damage that reduced the creature to 0 Hit Points by 2 × Spirit Awakening CL, potentially leaving it above 0.
Suppress one Charmed, Frightened, possession, ordinary transformation or identity-wound expression until the end of the creature’s next turn.
Restore Concentration if the creature has not begun another Concentration effect and the original duration has not expired.
Allow the creature to reroll the recorded Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma saving throw with Advantage.
Convert a recorded betrayal, confession or vow into undeniable spiritual evidence without changing whether it occurred.

Chronicle Asset: You may externalize the Chronicle as a Medium Cultivation Asset in an adjacent space. AC equals your Cultivation Save DC; Hit Points equal 8 × PB; it uses your Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma save bonuses, has Resistance to Psychic damage, and uses your effective Spirit Awakening CL as Source CL. You may originate Echo Scribe features from it. Destruction loses all unused Living Entries and ends the activation.
Internal Chronicle: If kept internal, it cannot be targeted separately, but each Rewrite the Margin costs 1 additional Resonance.
Limits: Available at CL 18.

Cannot undo an event after the scene meaningfully changes, resurrect someone whose death is no longer current, restore resources spent before the recorded event, duplicate consumed items, reverse a breakthrough, erase consent or rewrite the campaign’s past.

- sound or spoken emotional tone;
- touch, force, injury, or direction of movement;
- fear, grief, loyalty, anger, desire, or intent;
- spiritual pressure, possession, curse, dream influence, death, or another supernatural disturbance.

Record the Disturbance

Reaction

Debts of the Aggressor

A hostile creature in the Domain gains one Debt of the corresponding kind the first time each round one of its activations causes a chosen ally in the Domain to receive:

- qualifying damage for Impact;
- qualifying movement or restraint for Motion;
- a qualifying spiritual or mental consequence for Intent.

until the start of your next turn. This is one exceptional judgment package, not three conditions.

- End one ordinary Charmed or Frightened condition.
- Repeat one save against possession, curse, dream intrusion, memory alteration, or Spiritual Affliction or Heart Demon influence with Advantage.
- Return a displaced soul to its body if both are in the Emanation and no equal- or higher-authority seal prevents return.
- Suppress one equal- or higher-authority spiritual affliction until the end of the scene, provided you succeed on a Cultivation Check against its save DC.

High-Authority Limits

Grand Exorcism does not automatically destroy a deity, erase a Secret Law, annul a willing Soul Anchor, break a lawful Spirit Companion bond, reverse reincarnation, or release a soul held by higher Source CL without a contest and the relevant recovery procedure. It must still expose useful information or create a temporary opening when it cannot produce complete removal.

Domain Integration

When used inside your Domain Manifestation, Grand Exorcism treats every ordinary possession link, invisible hostile spirit, and lower-Source-CL curse Anchor in the Domain as perceived. You may originate the Emanation from yourself or your Soul Fragment.

Cultivation Level 14 — Seal of Binding

You create an exorcist seal that restrains a designated spiritual threat and exposes its removal procedure.

Action  
Range: 30 feet  
Cost: 6 Resonance  
Duration: The scene  
Concentration: No

Choose one Intruder, Restless Dead, fiend, demon, incorporeal undead, curse Source, hostile spirit Asset, or possessed creature you perceive. The target makes a Charisma saving throw.

Failed Save

Create a Binding Seal Anchor in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the target or attach it visibly to the Host, object, corpse, threshold, or ground.

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC.
- Hit Points: 5 × Proficiency Bonus.
- Saving Throws: Uses your Wisdom saving throw bonus.
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL.
- Immunities: Poison, Disease, Psychic damage, and ordinary bodily conditions.

While the Anchor remains:

- The target is Restrained.
- It cannot become invisible, incorporeal, or enter a Host unless the new state is an inherent passive quality that cannot be suppressed.
- It cannot teleport, cross planar boundaries, or move more than 30 feet from the Anchor.
- A possessing Intruder is forced out of its Host and remains adjacent to the Host or Anchor if it lacks a legal body.
- The target repeats the Charisma saving throw at the end of each of its turns. Three total successful repeat saves destroy the Anchor and end the effect. These successes need not be consecutive.

Successful Initial Save

The target is Restrained until the start of your next turn, becomes Resonance Marked by you, and you learn one of the following if it has one:

- Its immediate escape condition.
- Its sustaining Anchor category.
- Its invitation or possession route.
- The true name, title, taboo, burial need, payment, or unfinished obligation most relevant to peaceful resolution.

Breaking or Resolving the Seal

A creature can attack the Anchor if it can perceive and affect spiritual objects. Destroying it ends the binding but does not harm the target.

You, the Host, or an ally can also end the binding by completing one exposed lawful resolution. The resolution must be one of the following: Revoke Invitation by the willing Host or the authority that granted it; Break or Suppress the Sustaining Anchor through its printed profile; Return Remains or Complete Burial when that need was diagnosed; Pay the Recorded Restitution or Offering; Speak the Recorded True Name or Release Formula when a Source Rule grants it that function; Accept Surrender and Provide a Legal Departure Route; or complete Spiritual Exorcism or another printed removal procedure. A resolution cannot be invented after the seal is applied merely to deny the feature.

Soul Splitting Expression — Seal Warden

While Soul Splitting is active and a Binding Seal Anchor exists, use Seal Warden as your Subpath Expression. Move the Soul Fragment to a legal space adjacent to the Anchor. Until the start of your next turn, the Anchor has Resistance to all damage and the sealed target has Disadvantage on its next repeat saving throw.

Cultivation Level 14 — Borrowed Ending

You can detach a consequence from the moment it was supposed to occur.

Reaction  
You can use this when  You or an ally within 30 feet would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, fail a death saving throw, become Charmed or Frightened, become possessed, suffer a curse, lose a memory, have identity altered, suffer a permanent wound, or fail a Cultivation Check with an immediate consequence  
Cost: 6 Resonance and 1 Fate Tension

Create a Borrowed Ending and delay the triggering consequence until the end of the target’s next turn.

During the delay:

- The target remains at a minimum of 1 Hit Point if the trigger was reduction to 0 Hit Points.
- A failed death saving throw is not recorded yet.
- A condition, possession, curse, memory wound, identity wound, or permanent injury has not yet taken hold, though signs of it are visible.
- The target has one meaningful opportunity to alter the branch through healing, escape, exorcism, surrender, counter-technique, bargain, destroying an Anchor, accepting another cost, or another action capable of changing the cause.

At the end of the target’s next turn:

- If the cause was legally removed or the situation genuinely changed, the Borrowed Ending dissolves.
- If nothing changed, the original consequence occurs.
- If the source is equal or higher authority, a successful Cultivation Check is required for complete dissolution. On failure, reduce the consequence’s severity by one step where logically possible or delay it until the end of the scene.

Ending Token

The Borrowed Ending appears as a visible spiritual token attached to the target: a black thread, unfinished sentence, inverted hourglass, unfallen drop of blood, severed shadow, or another omen.

It is a Cultivation Asset with:

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 6 × Proficiency Bonus
- Source CL: Your effective Spirit Awakening CL
- Immunities: Poison, Psychic, and ordinary bodily conditions

Destroying the token by hostile action causes the original consequence to occur immediately unless the destructive effect expressly consumes or rewrites fate. A willing equal- or higher-authority healer, exorcist, fate cultivator, or source-specific countermeasure may instead target the token to dissolve it.

No Repeated Borrowing

A creature cannot carry more than one Borrowed Ending from you at a time. You cannot use Borrowed Ending on the same underlying consequence twice unless a distinct Source Rule recreated it after genuine resolution.

Cultivation Level 3 — Omen Glimpse

You can read one outcome before it becomes attached to an action.

Prepare an Omen

After at least 1 minute observing meaningful signs—cards, bones, stars, smoke, dreams, spirit behavior, battlefield movement, blood patterns, falling leaves, or another legal omen medium defined in the Normalized Execution Notes—spend 1 Resonance and roll one d20. Record the result as your Omen die.

- You can hold only one Omen die.
- Preparing a new one replaces the old one.
- An Omen die lasts until used, until the current scene ends, or until circumstances change so completely that the divination’s subject no longer exists.
- If a scene begins without preparation because you were genuinely surprised, you may prepare an Omen as a Bonus Action by spending 2 Resonance and gaining 1 Fate Tension.

Invoke the Omen

Reaction  
You can use this when  A creature you can see within 60 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, saving throw, death saving throw, or Cultivation Check  
Cost: 1 Resonance

Before the final outcome is declared, replace the d20 with your Omen die. The Omen die is then expended.

If the target is unwilling and the replacement would make its result worse, it may make a Charisma saving throw.

- Failed Save: The replacement applies.
- Successful Save: The original roll stands, but the creature becomes Resonance Marked by you and you retain the Omen die until the end of your next turn.

Omen Limits

An Omen cannot replace a roll that has no d20, retroactively change a fully resolved event, or automatically override a higher-authority fixed result. A Secret Law, divine decree, artifact prophecy, tribulation law, or equal- or higher-Source-CL certainty can require a Cultivation Check.

Cultivation Level 6 — Read the Thread

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 3 Resonance  
Target: One creature, object, location, active plan, or imminent event you can meaningfully observe

Choose one Thread Question from the Normalized Execution Notes:

- What is this subject most likely to do next?
- What is it trying hardest to protect?
- What immediate danger is connected to it?
- What choice would most alter its next likely outcome?
- Is fate around it ordinary, Restricted, Forbidden, Secret, divine, artifact-level, tribulation-bound, or otherwise distorted?
- What visible sign will precede the next major consequence tied to it?

The answer is symbolic but operationally useful. It must identify a real pressure, likely action, danger, leverage point, omen, or distortion rather than empty atmosphere.

Thread Clarity

- Against ordinary and lower-Source-CL concealment, the answer is direct enough to guide immediate action.
- Equal or higher authority can require a Cultivation Check.
- On a failed check, you learn which category is obscured and one visible sign of the concealment rather than receiving false information.
- Protected fate can reveal a branch rather than a certainty: “If no one intervenes,” “if the oath remains intact,” or “if the artifact is used.”

Mark the Branch

After receiving the answer, choose one creature involved in the predicted branch. If it knowingly takes the predicted action before the end of your next turn, it becomes Resonance Marked by you and you may move 10 feet or allow one ally within 30 feet to move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from that creature.

Cultivation Level 18 — Sever One Thread

You can cut one resolved possibility away from the world and force another nearby possibility to occupy its place.

Reaction  
You can use this when  A creature within 90 feet succeeds or fails on an attack roll, ability check, saving throw, death saving throw, or Cultivation Check, or an immediately resolved event creates a single discrete outcome  
Cost: 10 Resonance  
Requirement: You are not Fate-Tangled, and the event has not yet produced further dependent rolls or completed a later action

Name the thread you are severing in a brief statement: “the blade lands,” “the seal holds,” “the soul escapes,” “the gate opens,” or another precise outcome.

Choose one procedure.

Reroute the Roll

Force the creature to reroll the d20 and choose which result applies. If the creature is unwilling, it makes a Charisma saving throw first.

- Failed Save: You choose which result applies.
- Successful Save: The reroll occurs, but the target chooses which result applies and suffers two different ordinary Spiritual Pressure effects as one exceptional package.

Restore the Omen

If you used an Omen die on the triggering roll or on a directly connected roll this scene, replace the final d20 with the expended Omen result instead. An unwilling target makes the same Charisma saving throw described above.

Cut the Immediate Event

For a discrete non-roll event—an ordinary teleport completing, an ordinary possession taking hold, an ordinary gate opening, an ordinary execution trigger firing, or an ordinary Anchor collapsing—make a Cultivation Check against the effect’s Source Rule.

- Success: The named event does not occur. Costs already paid remain paid unless the source says otherwise.
- Failure: Delay the event until the end of the current turn and reveal one legal condition that could stop or alter it.

Severed-Thread Consequence

After Sever One Thread resolves:

- Set your Fate Tension to its maximum.
- You become Fate-Tangled.
- Choose and record one Severed Thread Consequence from the fixed list before play continues. It must arise from the altered event.
- You cannot use Sever One Thread again until that consequence is resolved through its recorded completion condition. Restoring Resonance or completing an ordinary rest does not restore access.

Examples include:

- an authority notices the impossible divergence;
- the spared death returns as a future tribulation;
- a sealed enemy gains a prophetic connection to you;
- the abandoned possibility becomes a hostile omen-spirit;
- a different branch claims the cost that was refused;
- your name disappears from one relationship, record, or prophecy until repaired.

Secret-Law Authority

An equal- or higher-Source-CL Secret Law, divine decree, artifact destiny, tribulation law, fixed reincarnation event, voluntary self-sacrifice, or campaign-defining outcome can resist Sever One Thread. Resolve the contest by Source CL and then Cultivation Check. Even on failure, you learn whether the outcome was fixed, protected, willingly accepted, or anchored elsewhere.

Fate Reader changes possibility. It does not erase Karma already earned, invalidate a lawful Soul Contract, or remove the moral and spiritual consequences of the action that created the roll.

• entire cities;
• divine structures;
• Secret Formations;
• world-scale terrain;
• legendary artifacts;
• Realm-defining geography.

Ten-Thousand-Metal Sovereign Edict - Secret, Metal Sovereign

To learn this, you need  Nascent Soul Realm, at least three Metal Methods, and access to a sovereign metal scripture, White Tiger mandate, immortal mine-heart, ancestral bell, imperial armory seal, or comparable revelation
Use an action.
Range: Self
Area: 1-mile-radius region centered on you
Duration: Instantaneous, with aftermath until the end of your next turn
Cost: 5 cultivation points (your Path resource)
Use Limit: Once per week
You declare that every piece of metal in the region remembers Heaven's command. The edict can act only through metal-bearing creatures, metal objects, weapons, armor, ore-rich terrain, mineralized structures, formation metal, ringing bells, battlefield armaments, or targets carrying your Metal Qi. This keeps the inheritance comparable in scale to heavenly lightning decrees while preserving Metal's boundary: it rules what bears metal, not everything under the sky.
Choose up to three decrees:
All Weapons Bow. Hostile creatures of your choice in the region that are holding metal weapons, wearing metal armor, carrying metal tools, made partly of metal, standing in ore-rich ground, or directly connected to battlefield metal make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, a creature is pulled 30 feet, pushed 30 feet, knocked Prone, or forced to drop one non-artifact metal object, your choice. On a success, it is moved 5 feet or keeps its grip, your choice.
The Edge Finds the Gap. Choose up to twice your Proficiency Bonus metal-bearing creatures, armored creatures, weapon-bearing creatures, constructs, or creatures carrying your Metal Qi that you can perceive in the region. Each makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes 8d8 slashing or piercing damage and cannot regain HP until the end of its next turn. On a success, it takes half damage and can regain HP normally.
The Bell Names the Flaw. Choose one visible or spiritually perceived non-Secret ward, barrier, armor technique, formation node, talisman frame, construct, gate, chain, seal, armory defense, or metal-bearing technique in the region. Make a Metal Check against its DC. On a success, suppress it until the end of your next turn. On a failure, reduce one of its major numerical benefits by your Cultivation Level until the end of your next turn and learn one of its protection rules.
The Ore Remembers the Mountain. Choose a point on metal-bearing ground, stone with ore, a mine, a forge floor, a battlefield covered with weapons, an armory, a city gate, or comparable terrain. Until the end of your next turn, the ground in a 60-foot radius becomes Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures, and the first time each hostile creature moves more than 10 feet through it, it takes piercing damage equal to your Cultivation Level.
The Tiger Passes Judgment. Hostile creatures of your choice in the region that are Bloodied, Frightened, carrying your Metal Qi, holding a weapon, wearing armor, standing among battlefield metal, or maintaining a violent technique make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, a creature cannot take Reactions, cannot benefit from Invisibility against you, and has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn. On a success, it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
The Body Becomes a Bell of Iron. Until the end of your next turn, you gain Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, Lightning, and Thunder damage; cannot be forcibly moved unless the enemy wins an opposed check against your Metal Check; and your first Metal talent hit each turn deals additional damage equal to 4d8.
Limits: Ten-Thousand-Metal Sovereign Edict does not permanently steal weapons, destroy artifacts, erase mountains, shut down ancient city arrays by default, bypass immunity, command nonmetal creatures without a metal-bearing condition, or defeat stronger domain-scale authority without an opposed Cultivation Check.

You unfold the World-Array Scripture. For a short time, the surrounding world is treated as if it had always been built from your Nodes, Gates, and Flow Lines.

Choose five World Laws from the list below. The area becomes a World Array with those laws.

Law of the Eye: You always know the location of creatures inside the area unless hidden by a Secret technique or stronger effect. You do not learn their thoughts, statistics, or secrets.

Law of the Gate: Keyed allies may teleport up to 60 feet inside the area as a Bonus Action. Hostile creatures attempting to teleport inside, out of, or through the area must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or the teleport fails.

Law of the Locked Road: Hostile creatures treat the entire area as Difficult Terrain. Once per round when a hostile creature moves more than 10 feet, you may force it to make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, its movement ends.

Law of the Hidden Road: Keyed allies have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks and may Hide while Lightly Obscured inside the area. Hostile creatures have Disadvantage on checks made to find your Nodes, Eyes, hidden Gates, or concealed keyed allies.

Law of the Killing Line: Once during each of your turns, choose a line up to 120 feet long inside the area. Hostile creatures on that line make Dexterity saving throws. A creature takes 8d8 Force damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success.

Law of the Returning Breath: Once per round when a keyed ally inside the area is reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, it instead drops to 1 Hit Point and is moved up to 30 feet to a legal space inside the area. A creature can benefit from this law only once per use of the inheritance.

On a success, the effect works, but the creature cannot benefit from this law again until the start of its next turn.

Law of the Shattered Formation: Choose one non-Secret Formation, Barrier, Domain, or prepared magical battlefield effect inside the area. Make a Formation Check against its creator’s save DC. On a success, suppress it while this inheritance lasts. On a failure, suppress one of its minor benefits until the end of your next turn.

Law of the Nine Palaces: Divide the area into up to nine visible or invisible palaces. Once per turn, when a hostile creature crosses from one palace into another, it must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, choose whether it becomes lost, slowed, or exposed until the start of your next turn. A lost creature cannot willingly move closer to a chosen objective. A slowed creature’s Speed is halved. An exposed creature cannot benefit from Invisible or Half Cover.

Law of the World Anchor: Create nine Anchors. Each Anchor has AC 19, Hit Points equal to 15 × your Proficiency Bonus, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. The World Array does not require Concentration while at least five Anchors remain. If fewer than five remain, you must Concentrate to maintain it. If fewer than three remain, it collapses.

While this inheritance lasts, you may Pulse one Pattern Layer or World Law once during each of your turns without using an action.

Limits: This inheritance does not permanently create territory, erase a kingdom, make you omnipotent, automatically kill creatures, rewrite the past, or suppress a stronger Secret Inheritance without a contested scene. Secret Drunken Style Inheritance

As a Reaction

Wrong

Target: The attack or single-target technique targets a different legal creature within range of the original effect.

Wrong Place: Move yourself and up to a number of willing creatures equal to your Proficiency Bonus up to 30 feet each to legal spaces you can perceive. If this makes the original effect illegal, it fails against those creatures.

Wrong Beat: The triggering creature becomes Off-Rhythm from you, loses its Reaction, and has Disadvantage on the triggering attack roll or grants Advantage on the triggering saving throw.

Wrong Certainty: If the triggering effect would hit you or make you fail a saving throw, turn that hit into a miss or that failed save into a success.

CL18 — Sovereign Soul Contract

Create Sovereign Contract

Ritual Time: 1 hour  
Range: All parties and required Anchors present  
Cost: 10 Qi  
Duration: Indefinite until fulfilled, released, broken, or destroyed

A Sovereign Contract may govern sect succession, dynastic marriage, national tribute, immortal service, possession of a Saint-class treasure, prison of a great cultivator, transfer of a bloodline, protection of a world gate, or another major obligation.

It requires a physical or cultivated Sovereign Contract Anchor such as a tablet, throne seal, ancestral book, blood altar, spirit brand, weapon, city Formation, or world-gate inscription.

Sovereign Contract Anchor

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC + 2
- Hit Points: 12 × your CL
- Resistance: All damage from lower-Source-CL attacks
- Immunity: Poison and Psychic damage
- Source CL: Your CL
- Repair: Equal/higher Contract, Soul, Oath, Formation, or artifact procedure

Sovereign Terms

A Sovereign Contract may pledge:

- An entire Cultivation Point resource.
- One Path, Subpath, Method, Foundation active system, Golden Core, Nascent Soul, Domain Armament network, or Sphere family.
- A soul fragment or reincarnation right.
- Up to ten years of lifespan.
- A bloodline transmission.
- A Saint-class or lower real item.
- A city, sect, office, Formation, route, or treasury recognized by the setting.
- A named future service that remains possible.

A Secret Law, Immortal authority, artifact soul, entire true identity, or world principle can be pledged only when its own Source Rule permits it or the Contract’s authority is equal or higher.

Sovereign Breach

A Sovereign breach creates Claims equal to your Proficiency Bonus and activates one printed Sovereign Penalty:

- Suppress pledged cultivation collateral.
- Seal the breacher’s movement to a named territory.
- Transfer a pledged office, item, resource, or authority.
- Inflict Tier III or Tier IV cultivation harm matching the collateral.
- Call the breacher before the Contract Anchor.
- Place the soul fragment or reincarnation right in escrow within the Anchor.

Contract Court

Action  
Area: 40-foot-radius field centered on the Sovereign Anchor  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

Inside the Court:

- Contract terms, Claims, pledged collateral, breach status, and authorized assignees become visible.
- A party cannot conceal a breach through a lower-Source-CL effect.
- Foreclosure costs one fewer Claim, minimum 1.
- Call the Contracted Party and Foreclose Cultivation may target any party in the field without range limits.
- A Contract challenge can be heard and resolved.

Final Foreclosure

Once during the Court, choose one party in Sovereign breach with at least four Claims. It makes a Charisma saving throw.

Failed Save

Choose one pledged result:

- Collect All Qi: Remove all current points from one pledged resource and prevent recovery for 1 hour.
- Close the Cultivation Collateral: Suppress all explicitly pledged cultivation systems; if every active system was pledged, impose Complete Cultivation Suppression.
- Seize Soul Escrow: Remove the pledged soul fragment, reincarnation right, or spirit collateral into the Anchor.
- Collect the Named Price: Transfer the exact pledged item, office, lifespan, memory, bloodline, service, or authority.
- Compel Performance: Move the party by a legal route to the named site and prevent voluntary departure for 1 hour when the Contract lawfully pledged that service.

Successful Save

One pledged system is suppressed until the end of the target’s next turn, it loses current Cultivation Points equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus, and one Claim remains unspent.

Breaking a Sovereign Contract

A Sovereign Contract can be broken through:

- Fulfillment or mutual release.
- Destruction or lawful alteration of the Sovereign Anchor.
- Equal/higher Contract, Oath, Karma, Fate, Soul, Void, Name, Samsara, or Conceptual authority.
- A successful challenge proving that a required party, term, collateral, or acceptance state was supernaturally falsified.
- A campaign-scale revolution, succession, conquest, artifact intervention, or heavenly judgment recognized by the setting.

Breaking the Contract ends future foreclosure. It does not automatically restore collateral already consumed, transferred, aged, severed, or destroyed; that requires the shared reconstruction procedure.

Contract Is Not Karma

The Contract Court asks whether a valid term was breached and whether named collateral may be foreclosed. It does not decide whether the Contract was just, whether the breacher deserved punishment, or whether unrelated deeds created Karmic Merit or Burden.

Cultivation Level 6 — Extract and Redirect Affliction

You can pull an affliction into a prepared needle, vessel, or your own meridians.

Prepare Extraction Needles

After a long rest or Full Cultivation Session, prepare a number of Extraction Needles equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

A prepared Needle may be:

- A physical medical needle.
- A talisman needle.
- A projected Qi needle.
- Another recorded medical vessel.

A Needle remains prepared until used or until you prepare a new set.

Extract Affliction

Action  
Range: Touch  
Cost: 3 Qi and one Extraction Needle

Choose one condition or affliction affecting a willing target:

- Bleeding.
- Blinded from bodily damage or irritants.
- Deafened from bodily damage.
- Disease.
- Poisoned.
- One poison.
- One meridian blockage.
- One Speed reduction.
- One ordinary paralysis or numbness effect.
- One identified cultivated bodily impairment.

If its Source CL is lower than yours:

- Remove it from the target.
- Seal it inside the Needle.

If its Source CL equals yours:

- Make a Cultivation Check against its save DC.
- On success, remove and seal it.
- On failure, suppress it until the start of your next turn.

If its Source CL exceeds yours:

- Make a Cultivation Check against its save DC.
- On success, suppress it for 1 minute and seal an echo rather than the full source.
- On failure, suppress one printed penalty until the end of the target’s next turn.

Extract Affliction cannot fully remove at this CL:

- A Curse.
- Foundation Injury.
- Hidden Injury.
- Possession.
- Permanent transformation.
- Soul Damage.
- Destroyed cultivation structure.
- Secret Law effect.

Sealed Affliction Needle

A Needle containing an affliction is a Tiny Cultivation Asset.

- AC: 15
- Hit Points: 1
- Immunity: Poison and Psychic damage
- Source CL: The higher of your CL or the extracted effect’s Source CL

The sealed affliction remains until:

- The scene ends.
- You safely neutralize it during 10 minutes of treatment.
- The Needle is destroyed.
- You implant it into another target through a feature.

If the Needle is destroyed before neutralization:

- The affliction returns to the original target when it is within 60 feet and on the same plane.
- Otherwise, it affects the nearest legal creature within 10 feet that could suffer it.
- If no legal target exists, the affliction dissipates unless its Source Rule says it cannot.

Redirect Affliction

Action  
Range: Touch  
Cost: 1 Qi and one Sealed Affliction Needle  
Target: One willing creature or one unwilling creature you have successfully hit with a medical implement during the current turn

An unwilling target makes a Constitution saving throw.

Failed Save: Receive the sealed affliction using its remaining duration and Source CL.  
Successful Save: The Needle remains sealed and is not consumed.

Redirecting a disease, poison, curse-like injury, or hostile condition into an unwilling creature may be illegal, condemned, or forbidden by a tradition. It does not automatically receive a Daemonic tag.

tianxia.subpath.qi.nine_arts_transcenden.player_text:
CL14 — Nine Arts Convergence

Action  
Cost: Normal costs of both techniques, plus 2 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

Choose two techniques you currently know or have prepared.

They must come from different Spheres, be Qi-powered, normally require an Action or Bonus Action, have a base Qi cost of 4 or less each, and have legal targets or origins when Convergence begins. They cannot be Secret, Legendary, permanent, strategic-scale, resurrection effects, or techniques creating additional complete turns or activations.

Convergence Procedure

1. Declare both techniques, targets, origins, and optional surcharges.
2. Pay both complete Qi costs and the 2-Qi surcharge.
3. Resolve the first technique completely.
4. Resolve the second if legal targets remain.
5. If the second no longer has a legal target, it fails and its Qi remains spent.

Principle Bridge

Before resolution, choose one bridge between the two techniques:

- Shared Origin: The second may originate from one legal origin of the first.
- Carried Movement: One target moved by the first may become a legal target of the second despite ending outside the second’s normal initial range, provided it remains within 60 feet of you.
- Transmuted Element: One damage type used by either technique becomes a damage type used by the other.
- Guarded Transition: After the first resolves, gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus or move 10 feet without provoking.
- Sustained Pattern: If both require Concentration and qualify for Split-Meridian Focus, the first upkeep payment is waived.

Principle Bridge does not create extra attacks, extra targets, additional save instances, or item-property duplication.

Convergence Limits

- A technique cannot target itself as the source of a recursive activation.
- An additional attack cannot generate another additional attack.
- A Barrage cannot copy the second technique across every projectile unless the second expressly permits that structure.
- A weapon-delivered technique applies only to its first qualifying attack unless explicitly stated otherwise.
- Qi Technique Potency applies once to each distinct activation, not once per target or projectile.
