CL10 — Battlefield Covenant

Action  
Area: 30-foot-radius aura centered on you or your Oath-Ledger Domain Armament  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required  
Cost: 5 Qi

Declare one Reciprocal Covenant in a language or symbolic form creatures in the area can understand. The aura moves with its center.

A Covenant must offer both a rule and a clear benefit, protection, right, or release available to creatures that accept it.

Acceptance

- A willing creature may accept when the Covenant appears.
- A creature that enters later may accept without using an action.
- A hostile creature accepts by explicitly agreeing or by knowingly claiming the Covenant’s benefit and remaining in the aura.
- A creature may reject the Covenant and receive none of its benefits. Rejection alone creates no Mark.
- A surrendered, lawfully sentenced, or Completely Subdued creature may be compelled to accept on a failed Charisma save when the Covenant represents clear surrender or confinement terms.

A bound creature gains a Breach Mark only when it knowingly violates the accepted Law. It gains a Fulfillment Mark when it meaningfully honors the Law under pressure.

Choose one Law:

Sanctuary Covenant

Benefit: Accepted creatures gain +1 AC against attacks made by another accepted creature and Advantage against forced hostility.

Term: Do not make hostile attacks, deal hostile damage, or force hostile saves against another accepted creature.

Guarded Passage

Benefit: Accepted creatures ignore Opportunity Attacks from other accepted creatures while following a declared route.

Term: Remain on the route and do not attack protected travelers, guides, or route Anchors.

Honorable Contest

Benefit: Accepted duelists gain Advantage on saves against outside interference and cannot be directly targeted by nonparticipants with lower Source CL.

Term: Attack only the declared opponent, do not use named forbidden techniques, and stop when the victory condition occurs.

Protect the Weak

Benefit: Accepted protectors gain Temporary Hit Points equal to Proficiency Bonus at the start of each turn while within 10 feet of a protected creature.

Term: Do not knowingly harm the named class of civilians, surrendered enemies, healers, prisoners, wounded creatures, or Anchors.

Formation Duty

Benefit: Accepted allies gain +1 AC or +5 Speed while occupying their assigned Formation region.

Term: Remain within the assigned region, maintain the named role, and do not abandon the Formation without the stated release signal.

Forbidden Art Accord

Benefit: Accepted creatures gain Advantage on saves against the named technique, Sphere, damage type, weapon group, movement mode, or cultivation category.

Term: Do not activate that category within the aura.

CL18 — Heaven as Witness

Action  
Area: 40-foot-radius, 40-foot-high cylinder centered on you or your Oath-Ledger Domain Armament  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

A visible heavenly ledger, ancestral court, constellation of witness seals, or equivalent cultural expression fills the field.

For the duration:

- Every clear promise, surrender term, office declaration, covenant acceptance, fulfillment, and breach spoken or enacted inside becomes perceptible to you.
- A creature cannot conceal whether it understood and accepted a term through a non-Secret effect whose Source CL is lower than yours.
- Place one Fulfillment or Breach Mark per creature per round without using your Reaction.
- Spending an Oath Mark costs no Qi and may occur once during every turn, no more than once per turn.
- Recorded Oath rewards and sanctions can affect a target anywhere in the field.

Heavenly Confirmation

At the start of each of your turns, choose one accepted obligation active in the field and one party to it.

If the party is presently honoring the term, grant one:

- Restore 3d8 + your modifier Hit Points.
- Restore 2 Cultivation Points.
- Grant +2 AC until the start of your next turn.
- Move 15 feet without provoking.
- End one lower- or equal-Source-CL condition that directly obstructs fulfillment.

If the party is presently breaching the term, impose one:

- Deal 3d8 Psychic or Force damage.
- Remove 2 current Cultivation Points.
- Prevent Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Move it 15 feet toward a required position or away from a forbidden one.
- Suppress the exact technique, item function, movement mode, or system used for the breach until the start of its next turn.

Final Witness

Once during the activation, choose one creature bearing at least four Fulfillment Marks or four Breach Marks.

An unwilling target makes a Charisma saving throw.

Fulfillment — Failed or Willing

Choose one:

- Fulfill one remaining ordinary payment, passage, protection, or delivery term through heavenly substitution when the required resource is present in the field.
- Restore all Hit Points and up to half maximum Cultivation Points.
- End one non-Secret oath, contract, restraint, curse, or suppression that the fulfilled obligation was meant to release and whose Source CL is no higher than yours.
- Grant Witnessed Authority for 1 minute: Advantage on all saving throws and Cultivation Checks made to complete or defend the fulfilled obligation.

Breach — Failed Save

Choose one:

- Apply the Recorded Sanction at maximum effect without spending Marks.
- Suppress every technique and item function used to commit the breach for 1 minute.
- Compel return to one legal boundary, prison, employer, beneficiary, or place of surrender named by the obligation. The movement follows legal route and sealed-boundary rules.
- Impose Complete Cultivation Suppression until the end of its next turn; a target 6+ CL lower remains suppressed until it accepts a possible restitution or release term.

Successful Save

- Fulfillment target receives half the chosen benefit.
- Breach target loses Reactions and Cultivation Points equal to Proficiency Bonus until the start of its next turn.

Limits of the Heavenly Ledger

Heaven as Witness enforces accepted or lawfully imposed obligations. It does not:

- Punish unrelated violence merely because it is harmful.
- Reward unrelated aid merely because it is generous.
- Infer an unwitnessed contract.
- Seize unpledged soul collateral.
- Replace Karma’s independent cause-and-consequence authority.

CL6 — Invoke the Clause

When you spend a Fulfillment or Breach Mark, choose one additional effect appropriate to the recorded obligation. A creature can be affected by one Invoke the Clause effect per turn.

Fulfillment Effects

Honored Performance

The creature regains 2d8 + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier Hit Points or gains the same amount as Temporary Hit Points.

Granted Passage

Move it up to 15 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks, including across a boundary the fulfilled term authorizes.

Witnessed Authority

It gains Advantage on its next Charisma, Wisdom, or Cultivation Check made to prove, enforce, explain, or complete the obligation.

Released Burden

End one non-Secret Restrained, Charmed, Frightened, or oath-created condition whose Source CL is no higher than yours when fulfillment expressly releases it.

Breach Effects

Pain of Perjury

Deal 2d8 Psychic or Force damage, increasing to 3d8 at CL11 and 4d8 at CL17.

Return to the Boundary

Push or pull the creature up to 10 feet toward a position required by the breached term.

Stay the Violating Hand

One held object or one Domain Armament used in the breach cannot be stowed, dismissed, remotely moved, or activated until the start of your next turn. A higher-authority sentient or artifact item may resist using its own save DC.

Forfeit the Moment

Choose one beneficiary of the obligation within 30 feet. It may move 10 feet without provoking or gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 2 × Proficiency Bonus.

CL14 — Oathkeeper’s Record

You may maintain three Recorded Oaths simultaneously.

Record a Voluntary Oath

Ritual Time: 1 minute  
Range: Touch, or all participants within 10 feet  
Cost: 2 Qi

Record a clear obligation accepted by every participant. It lasts until fulfilled, breached and resolved, dismissed by all surviving participants, its duration ends, or higher authority severs it.

A Recorded Oath can last indefinitely when its completion and release terms remain possible.

Fulfillment

When a meaningful Recorded Oath is fulfilled, choose one participant to receive one:

- Regain 3 Qi.
- Regain 4d8 + your key ability modifier Hit Points.
- Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 4 × Proficiency Bonus.
- End one lower- or equal-Source-CL oath, fear, charm, restraint, or curse that the fulfillment was meant to resolve.
- Gain Advantage on one saving throw before the end of the next scene.
- Receive one truthful symbolic clue concerning the oath’s direct consequences.

A trivial or self-fulfilling oath cannot generate repeated rewards.

Breach

When a Recorded Oath is knowingly breached:

- Place Breach Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus on the breacher.
- The breacher cannot conceal its direction from you on the same plane through lower-Source-CL effects.
- Choose one Recorded Sanction established when the Oath was made.

Legal Sanctions include:

- 6d10 Psychic or Force damage.
- Loss of current Cultivation Points equal to twice Proficiency Bonus.
- Suppression of one named Sphere, technique family, Domain Armament function, or movement mode for 1 minute.
- Inability to cross one named boundary for 8 hours.
- Compelled return of an item, payment, office, or authority actually governed by the Oath.
- Charmed or Frightened of one named beneficiary for 1 minute, with repeat saves at the end of each turn.

A Sanction cannot seize an entire soul, unrelated property, or a cultivation structure not pledged or governed by the Oath.

Compelled Record

Action  
Range: Touch  
Cost: 7 Qi  
Saving Throw: Charisma  
Requirement: The target is Completely Subdued, has formally surrendered, has accepted release or aid under stated terms, or is subject to a lawful or conquered authority recognized by the campaign.

State one clear obligation with a duration no longer than 30 days at this level.

- Failed Save: The Oath is recorded.
- Successful Save: The target is not bound and cannot be targeted by your Compelled Record again until the end of the scene.
- Target 3+ CL higher: You must also win a Cultivation Check against its save DC.
- Target 6+ CL lower and Completely Subdued: It automatically fails unless protected by explicit anti-oath authority.

Compelled Record is coercive oath authority, not consent. Its use may be legal, tyrannical, criminal, or ordinary depending on the setting.

---

Action  
Range: 60 feet

Successful Save

False Distance

The target treats all spaces more than 15 feet away as 15 feet farther for range and movement calculations.

Reversed Gate

Hidden Origin

Broken Sequence

Misnamed Target

At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the Intelligence save, removing one Maze Riddle on success.

- Success: Remove one Maze Riddle.
- Success by 5 or more: Remove all Maze Riddles.
- Failure: One Riddle of your choice activates its penalty immediately if possible.

CL18 — Palace of the Final Riddle

Action  
Range: 90 feet  
Area: 30-foot-radius, 30-foot-high cylinder  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

A shifting palace, board, labyrinth, archive, court, lockwork world, or geometric impossibility overlays the area. The Palace is a Puzzle Formation with one central Riddle Core and four visible Clue Nodes.

Riddle Core

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 10 × your CL
- Resistance: All damage until at least one Clue Node is solved or destroyed
- Immunity: Poison and Psychic damage
- Source CL: Your CL

Clue Nodes

Each Node represents one Method: Observe, Infer, Test, or Contradict.

- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 4 × your CL
- Resistance: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from noncultivated attacks
- Immunity: Poison and Psychic damage
- Source CL: Your CL

A creature adjacent to a Node may use an Action and the Node’s Method.

- Success: The Node is solved and becomes inactive.
- Success by 5 or more: It is solved, and every ally in the Palace gains Advantage on its next Solve attempt.
- Failure: The creature takes 4d8 Force or Psychic damage and is moved 10 feet to a legal space chosen by the Palace.

Destroying a Node also makes it inactive, but causes 2d8 Force damage to every creature within 10 feet.

Enter the Palace

When a hostile creature enters for the first time during a turn or starts there, it makes an Intelligence saving throw.

- Failed Save: Gain one unresolved Final Riddle for each active Clue Node, maximum four.
- Successful Save: Gain one Final Riddle of your choice until the start of its next turn.

Each unresolved Final Riddle imposes one stage:

1. Lost Roads: Speed halved; no willing teleportation, phasing, or remote origins.
2. Broken Sequence: No Reactions; cannot repeat the same named technique on consecutive turns.
3. Closed Meridians: Cannot recover Cultivation Points and cannot spend more than Proficiency Bonus during one turn.
4. The Unanswered Heaven: Complete Cultivation Suppression under the shared rule.

A creature with fewer than four Riddles suffers only the first stages equal to its count. A creature always retains ordinary movement, speech, perception, and the ability to take the Solve action unless another effect removes them.

Solve a Final Riddle

A creature may use its Action and choose one active Clue Node’s Method.

- Success: Remove one Final Riddle from itself and count one success toward solving that Node.
- Success by 5 or more: Remove two Final Riddles and solve that Node immediately.
- Failure: It gains one additional Final Riddle, maximum four.

A creature can also earn a true clue by observing another creature solve a Node, identifying a repeated Palace behavior, or using an explicit Puzzle, Divination, Strategy, Formation, Name, Karma, or Conceptual authority.

Effect of Solved Nodes

For every inactive Clue Node:

- The maximum Final Riddles a creature can bear decreases by one.
- Every creature immediately removes one Final Riddle of its choice.
- The Riddle Core loses resistance against all damage.

When all four Nodes are inactive, the Palace ends.

Master Key

A creature that solved a Logic Lock through a success by 5 or more during the current scene, possesses an authorized Key you named when creating the Palace, or has already solved one Clue Node may use a Bonus Action once per turn to grant itself or one creature it can see Advantage on a Solve attempt.

Leaving the Palace

Leaving the area does not count as solving the Puzzle. At the end of a creature’s turn after it leaves and remains outside:

- Remove one Final Riddle.
- Repeat until all Riddles are gone on later turns.

If the creature re-enters before all Riddles are removed, its remaining Riddles return to full effect.

Puzzle, Not Seal

The Palace does not create direct Seal Pillars, chains, or an unconditional binding. Every stage is encoded through visible, interactable logic. Destruction is possible, but understanding the Formation is usually faster than overpowering it.

Create a wall up to 30 feet long, 15 feet high, and 1 foot thick, composed of shifting tiles, script, doors, mirrored paths, interlocking blocks, or another Puzzle form.

Cultivation Level 14 — Behead the Standard

You strike the node that makes an army more than a collection of individuals.

Action  
Range: Weapon reach, or 60 feet through your Halberd Domain Armament  
Cost: 5 Qi

Choose one target identified as at least one of the following:

- Primary Formation Anchor.
- Secondary Formation Anchor.
- Command banner or standard.
- Formation commander.
- Creature serving as an aura’s origin.
- Creature serving as a remote technique hub.
- Cultivation Asset coordinating other assets.
- Vehicle, platform, or artifact serving as a linked power core.

Make one halberd-family weapon attack or Halberd Domain Armament Attack.

Hit Against an Object or Asset

Deal:

- Normal weapon or Domain Armament damage.
- 8d8 additional Slashing, Piercing, or Force damage.

- Treats ordinary Damage Threshold as 0.
- Ignores ordinary Resistance to Slashing, Piercing, and Force.

Successful Save: Until the start of your next turn:

- It cannot serve as a Remote Technique Origin.

Decapitation by Realm

When the creature is 5 or more CL lower than you and fails its save:

- It does not repeat the saving throw during the first two turns.
- Any lower-CL linked structure for which it is the sole commander is completely suppressed during that time.

- A floating Domain Armament.
- A banner.
- A mobile Anchor.
- A flying Cultivation Asset.
- A creature no more than one size larger than you.

Cultivation Level 6 — Break the Rank

You can use this when  You hit a creature or asset participating in a linked cultivation structure with a halberd-family attack, Halberd Domain Armament Attack, or halberd-delivered technique.  
Cost: 2 Qi  
Limit: Once per turn

Choose one link identified by Read the Array or visibly functioning through the target.

Examples include:

- A Formation benefit.
- An aura.
- A shared Reaction.
- A command connection.
- A remote origin.
- A banner benefit.
- A shared defense.
- A linked movement effect.

The target makes a Charisma saving throw. An unattended Anchor or asset uses its Source Rule; if it has no saving throw, compare Source CL as described below.

Failed Save

Sever the selected link until the start of your next turn.

While severed:

- The target neither grants nor receives the selected shared benefit.
- It cannot transmit commands, targeting, power, or movement through that link.
- It is not treated as adjacent or connected for the selected Formation procedure.

Successful Save

The selected link flickers until the end of the current turn.

During that time:

- It cannot provide a Reaction.
- It cannot reduce the Qi cost of another creature’s feature.
- It cannot transmit remote targeting through the target.

Source CL Against Assets

Lower Source CL

An unattended Anchor or asset’s selected link is severed automatically until the start of your next turn.

Equal Source CL

Make a Cultivation Check against its save DC.

Success: Sever it until the start of your next turn.  
Failure: Apply the successful-save flicker.

Higher Source CL

Make a Cultivation Check against its save DC.

Success: Apply the successful-save flicker.  
Failure: The link remains intact, but its direction and Anchor are revealed until the scene ends.

Drag from Formation

After severing a link, move the struck creature up to 15 feet to a legal space.

This movement:

- Does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from creatures participating in the same severed structure.
- Cannot pass through a solid barrier.
- Cannot place the target inside an occupied space.

If the target is an immobile Anchor, move yourself up to 10 feet instead.

A field of severing lines, hooked currents, and broken command paths fills the area.

A hostile creature or asset participating in a linked cultivation structure makes a Charisma saving throw when it:

- Enters the field for the first time during a turn.
- Starts its turn inside the field.

Failed Save: Until the start of its next turn:

- It receives no aura or Formation benefit from outside the field.
- It cannot transmit a shared Reaction.
- It cannot serve as a Remote Technique Origin for another creature.
- Its first Cultivation Point expenditure during the turn costs 1 additional point.
- It cannot teleport through a linked Formation route.

Successful Save: Until the start of its next turn:

- It cannot transmit a shared Reaction.
- It cannot serve as a Remote Technique Origin for another creature.

- Formation Anchors, command links, banner channels, and remote-origin paths whose Source CL is lower than yours become visible.

Effect: Area: 60-foot-radius, 60-foot-high cylinder

When the field appears, choose one hostile linked cultivation structure you can perceive or have identified through Read the Array. It may be a battlefield Formation, banner network, command aura system, remote weapon array, linked shield wall, construct-control lattice, distributed ritual, or vehicle or fortress power network.

Reveal the Army: Active participants, Anchors, links, command nodes and remote origins of the selected structure inside the field become visible if their Source CL is lower than yours. For equal or higher Source CL, make a Cultivation Check against the structure’s save DC. Success: reveal them. Failure: reveal the number and direction of concealed nodes, but not their exact spaces.
Collapse Strikes: Choose up to PB visible nodes. Each can be a creature, Anchor, banner, Domain Armament, Cultivation Asset, command implement or linked structural section.

Each creature makes a Dexterity saving throw. Failure: 8d8 Slashing, Piercing or Force damage; sever its links to the selected structure for 1 minute, and prevent its Reactions until the start of its next turn. Success: half damage and sever its links until the start of its next turn.
Objects and assets take 8d8 damage without a saving throw. Double the damage against primary Anchors and command assets.
Formation Collapse: After all Collapse Strikes resolve, determine how much of the structure remains.

All Primary Anchors or Command Nodes Broken: If its Source CL is no higher than yours, the structure ends immediately. If higher, suppress it inside the field for 1 minute; it may reconstitute outside the field or after the duration under its own rules.
At Least Half of Primary Nodes Broken: Suppress the structure throughout the field for 1 minute. Outside the field, it works only through surviving links that do not cross the field.

Fewer Than Half Broken: For 1 minute inside the field, halve all shared bonuses, rounded down; shared Reactions and linked Cultivation Point reductions cannot function, and remote origins cannot cross the field.
Broken-Array Territory: For the duration, hostile creatures and assets inside the field must overcome your severing authority to establish a new linked cultivation structure.
Lower Source CL: The attempt fails. No Cultivation Points are spent if the illegality is known before activation.
Equal Source CL: The creator makes a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC. Success: establish the structure. Failure: the attempt fails and its cost remains spent.
Higher Source CL: The structure forms, but its links inside the field are visible and cannot reduce Cultivation Point costs.
Choices: General’s Hook: Once during each of your turns while the field persists, choose one visible linked creature or asset inside it and move it up to 15 feet. An unwilling creature makes a Strength saving throw; success moves it 5 feet instead. This can pull participants out of aura ranges, break physical formations or expose Anchors.
Limits: Available at CL 18.

Cultivation Level 3 — Three Edges Doctrine

A halberd carries three answers: point, blade, and hook.

Once per turn before making a halberd-family weapon attack, choose one Edge.

Spear Point

For that attack:

- Increase reach by 5 feet.
- Ignore Half Cover.
- On a hit, deal additional Piercing or Force damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

Crescent Blade

On a hit, choose one different creature or object within 5 feet of the target and within your weapon’s reach.

The secondary target takes Slashing or Force damage equal to:

your Proficiency Bonus + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier

This secondary damage:

- Does not require an attack roll.
- Does not deliver a cultivation technique.
- Does not trigger itself.

Formation Hook

On a hit, the target makes a Strength saving throw.

Failed Save: Choose one:

- Pull it 10 feet.
- Push it 10 feet.
- It drops one nonartifact weapon, shield, banner, or implement it is holding.
- Rotate it into a different legal facing or position when facing matters to a Formation.

Successful Save: Push or pull it 5 feet.

An artifact or bound item can be dropped only when its Source Rule permits disarming.

Halberd Conduction

When you activate a Qi-powered technique, you may deliver it through a halberd-family weapon you are wielding when all of the following are true:

- You are proficient with the weapon.
- The technique targets one creature, one object, one Formation Anchor, or one Cultivation Asset.
- The technique has a range of Touch, 5 feet, or 30 feet or less.
- The technique has an instantaneous effect or applies its duration directly to the struck target.
- The technique does not create an area, separate asset, summoned creature, or location-based field.

Additional Cost: 1 Qi

Make one attack with the halberd-family weapon as part of the technique’s activation.

A miss fails to deliver the technique and does not refund its cost.

Halberd Conduction applies only to the first qualifying attack unless another Source Rule expressly expands it.

At Cultivation Level 9, a Halberd Domain Armament may deliver the technique through its floating attack.

Read the Array

Bonus Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 1 Qi

Choose one visible creature, Formation, field, banner, command asset, or Cultivation Asset.

Learn all of the following that apply:

- Whether it participates in a linked cultivation structure.
- The number of visible linked participants within range.
- The direction of the nearest visible or metaphysically traceable Anchor.
- Whether it grants or receives an aura, shared reaction, command, movement, targeting, or defensive benefit.
- The structure’s Source CL.
- Whether the selected target is a primary Anchor, secondary Anchor, commander, participant, or beneficiary.

A concealed link requires a Cultivation Check against its save DC.

Failure:

- You know that a concealed link exists.
- You do not learn its exact structure or Anchor.
- You cannot retry until the structure changes or a new scene begins.

Read the Array does not reveal unrelated statistics, secret techniques, or the contents of a creature’s thoughts.

tianxia.subpath.qi.go_stone_cultivator.f.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 — Capture the Group

You learn to turn encirclement into an actual cultivation prison.

Bonus Action  
Range: 90 feet  
Target: One creature Surrounded by your board  
Cost: 4 Qi  
Duration: 1 minute  
Saving Throw: Dexterity

A creature within 10 feet of four or more Stones has Disadvantage on the initial saving throw.

Failed Save — Captured

The target becomes Captured.

While Captured:

- It is Restrained.
- It cannot willingly teleport, phase, become Incorporeal, or use a spatial passage.
- It cannot move or originate a Domain Armament outside the boundary surrounding it.
- Its Cultivation Point costs increase by 1.
- It cannot use a feature whose sole function is movement without first succeeding on a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC.

At the end of each turn, it may repeat the Dexterity saving throw.

A repeated save is made with Disadvantage while at least three contributing Stones remain.

On success, Captured ends.

Successful Save

Until the start of your next turn:

- Its Speed is reduced by 15 feet.
- It cannot willingly teleport.

Capturing Boundary

Record the Stones contributing to Capture the Group.

The capture ends early when:

- Fewer than two contributing Stones remain.
- The target leaves the closed boundary through an effect that explicitly overcomes the capture.
- You end it without using an action.
- The duration expires.

Break the Board

A Captured creature or its ally may attack, move, suppress, or destroy contributing Stones normally.

A creature may also use an Action to attempt a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC.

On success, choose one:

- Suppress one contributing Stone until the start of the creature’s next turn.
- Ignore Restrained until the start of the creature’s next turn.
- Pay 3 Cultivation Points to ignore the increased cost and spatial restrictions until the start of its next turn.

This escape procedure is intentionally expensive and temporary.

---

player_card.summary: Create a Heavenly Board that controls movement and can seal a heavily surrounded creature.

Effect: Area: 50-foot-radius, 50-foot-high cylinder

Place up to nine temporary Go Stones in legal spaces inside the field. Each may be Black or White, has two different Shapes of your choice, AC 18 and Hit Points equal to 4 × your Qi Cultivation CL, and disappears when the field ends. Existing Stones inside join the Heavenly Board and receive the same AC and Hit Points if those values are higher. The entire field counts as Claimed Territory.
Heaven Owns the Board: During each of your turns, you may move up to three Stones 20 feet without using an action. Once during each of your turns, you may change the Shapes of any number of Stones.

Allies you choose ignore Difficult Terrain and may move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks at the start of their turns. Hostile creatures treat the field as Difficult Terrain; their teleportation, phasing, Incorporeal movement and spatial passage inside it require a Charisma save against your Cultivation Save DC.
Capture the Group costs 0 Qi once per turn. A creature Surrounded by four or more Stones has Disadvantage on all saves against your Go-Stone features.

Board Judgment: A hostile creature makes a Dexterity saving throw when it first enters the field during a turn or starts its turn inside; a creature is affected once per turn. Success: reduce its Speed by 10 feet until the start of its next turn. Failure: choose one Board Judgment effect below.
Choices: Board Judgment, failed save: Its Speed becomes 0 until the start of its next turn.
Board Judgment, failed save: Push or pull it 15 feet.
Board Judgment, failed save: It cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Board Judgment, failed save: Increase its next Cultivation Point cost before the start of its next turn by 2.
Board Judgment, failed save: It cannot willingly teleport, phase or become Incorporeal until the start of its next turn.

Take the Entire Group: Action. Target: One creature inside the field Surrounded by at least five Stones. Cost: 5 Qi. Use limit: Once during each activation. Saving Throw: Charisma. Compare its Source CL with yours as below.
Target Source CL 6 or More Below Yours: It saves with Disadvantage and receives no automatic repeated saves.
Target Source CL Within 5 of Yours: It saves normally and may use the escape procedure below.
Target Source CL 3 or More Above Yours: It saves with Advantage. On a failed save, it receives a repeated save at the end of each turn.

Heavenly Capture, failed save: For the remaining duration, the target is Restrained, its Speed is 0, and it cannot teleport, phase, become Incorporeal, cross planar or spiritual passages, move its Domain Armament, or recover Cultivation Points. Its Cultivation Point costs increase by 2.

While under Heavenly Capture, it cannot activate a Path, Subpath, Sphere, Recorded Art, Forged Technique, Immortal Art, Method, Foundation-active, Golden Core, Nascent Soul or cultivated-item feature costing more than its PB.
Take the Entire Group, successful save: Until the start of your next turn, halve its Speed, prevent it from teleporting and increase its Cultivation Point costs by 1.
Escape Heavenly Capture: A target entitled to an escape attempt may use its Action for one option below.
Make a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC.
Destroy or suppress one of the five contributing Stones, then repeat the Charisma saving throw.
Spend Cultivation Points equal to your PB and accept one level of Exhaustion to repeat the Charisma saving throw with Advantage.
Accept a Hidden Injury, damaged meridian or temporary maximum-Cultivation-Point reduction established by the injury rules to end Heavenly Capture immediately.
Limits: Available at CL 18.
An ally may destroy Stones, suppress the field, break Concentration or use an appropriate counter-seal normally.

tianxia.subpath.qi.go_stone_cultivator.f.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 — Living Board

Your board ceases to be a set of fixed objects and becomes a moving cultivation formation.

Move the Stones

Once during each of your turns, move one Stone up to 20 feet without using an action.

The Stone:

- Travels along a visible legal path.
- Cannot pass through Total Cover, sealed Formations, or spatial locks.
- Does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.

Reassign Shape

Once during each of your turns, change one Stone’s Shape without using an action.

Claim Territory

Action  
Requirement: At least three connected Stones form a closed boundary  
Duration: Until the boundary is broken, you claim another territory, or the scene ends  
Cost: 3 Qi

The enclosed area becomes your Claimed Territory.

You may maintain one Claimed Territory.

Inside it:

- Allies you choose ignore Difficult Terrain created by your board.
- Allies gain +1 AC.
- Hostile creatures treat the area as Difficult Terrain.
- Hostile creatures cannot benefit from ordinary concealment against your awareness of their position.
- A hostile creature crossing a Board Line pays 5 additional feet of movement.
- Your Board features use any Stone on the boundary as their origin.

Territory Tax

The first time during each turn that a hostile creature inside Claimed Territory spends Cultivation Points, choose one:

- Increase the cost by 1.
- Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
- Move one Stone 10 feet.
- Move one ally inside the Territory 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

A cost cannot be increased more than once by Territory Tax during the same turn.

Take the Liberty

Reaction  
You can use this when  A hostile creature inside Claimed Territory destroys, suppresses, or removes one of your Stones.  
Limit: Once per round

Choose one:

- Place one temporary Stone in a legal space within 15 feet of the destroyed Stone. It lasts until the start of your next turn.
- Make a Cultivation Attack against the triggering creature. On a hit, deal 3d8 Force damage.
- The triggering creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Move one ally inside the Territory 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

---

Cultivation Level 3 — Place Stone

Bonus Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 1 Qi  
Duration: 1 hour

Place one Black or White Go Stone in an unoccupied space on a stable surface.

You may maintain a number of Go Stones equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

Creating another beyond this maximum removes one Stone of your choice.

Go Stone Statistics

- Size: Tiny
- AC: 14
- Hit Points: 2 × your Qi Cultivation CL
- Resistance: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing
- Immunity: Poison and Psychic damage
- Source CL: Your CL

A Stone:

- Occupies no space.
- Does not provide Cover.
- Cannot be moved by ordinary wind or incidental contact.
- May be picked up by a creature using an Action after succeeding on a Strength check against your Cultivation Save DC.
- Is destroyed if carried more than 60 feet from every other Stone you control.

Black Stone Pressure

A hostile creature treats spaces within 5 feet of a Black Stone as Difficult Terrain.

The first time during each turn that a hostile creature crosses a Board Line connected to a Black Stone, reduce its remaining Speed by 5 feet.

A creature can suffer this reduction once per turn.

White Stone Opening

An ally within 5 feet of a White Stone gains +1 AC against Opportunity Attacks.

The first time during each turn that an ally crosses a Board Line connected to a White Stone, it may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

A creature can receive this movement once per turn.

Read the Board

While at least two Stones remain active, you know:

- The location of every Stone.
- Whether a creature is standing within 5 feet of one.
- Whether a Board Line has been crossed.
- Whether one of your closed boundaries has been entered or exited.

Read the Board does not identify a concealed creature unless another sense could perceive it.

---

Cultivation Level 10 — Heart Transplant

You can move a Heart Aspect from one creature to another.

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 5 Qi  
Targets: One donor and one recipient

The donor may be:

- A creature currently missing an Aspect you stole.
- A willing creature offering an Aspect.
- A creature carrying one of your stored Aspects.

The recipient may be willing or unwilling.

An unwilling donor or recipient makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Resolution

If every unwilling participant fails:

- Remove the selected Aspect from the donor until the end of the scene.
- Implant it in the recipient for the same duration.
- The recipient treats the emotion as genuine while present.
- It remembers that supernatural influence occurred unless a later feature alters memory.

If either necessary participant succeeds:

- The transplant fails.
- No Aspect is removed.

Directed Aspect

Choose one subject for the transplanted emotion:

- You.
- A visible creature.
- A known person.
- A group.
- An object.
- A place.
- A goal.

The emotion can influence decisions, but does not automatically grant complete control.

A transplanted Loyalty or Love can compel the recipient to protect the subject from immediate harm and avoid knowingly betraying it. It cannot force direct self-destruction unless the emotion is defining and a later feature permits it.

A transplanted Hatred, Fear, or Rage can strongly bias hostility but cannot force an illegal action when no valid target or path exists.

Heart Medicine

When used on willing participants, Heart Transplant may instead:

- Move debilitating grief into a prepared vessel.
- Restore courage stolen by another effect.
- Transfer calm to a panicked patient.
- Separate compulsive love from its target.
- Preserve a dying creature’s defining attachment for later restoration.

This can be legitimate healing even when the same technique is forbidden in hostile use.

Cultivation Level 14 — Rewrite the Inner Heart

You can make an emotional alteration lasting or indefinite.

Heart-Rewriting Rite

Ritual Time: 1 hour  
Range: Touch  
Cost: 8 Qi and appropriate ritual materials  
Requirement: The target is willing, helpless, Restrained for the complete rite, unconscious, or contained within a Heart-Sealing Formation.

Choose one Rewrite:

- Remove one Heart Aspect.
- Create one Heart Aspect.
- Redirect one defining emotion toward a new subject.
- Weaken one defining emotion by one grade.
- Strengthen one emotion by one grade.
- Create a permanent Heart Anchor.
- Seal one traumatic emotional trigger.
- Restore an emotion previously stolen by you.

An unwilling target makes a Wisdom saving throw at the end of the rite.

If its Source CL is higher than yours, it has Advantage.

If it is at least 6 CL lower, it has Disadvantage and does not receive automatic repeated saves.

Failed Save

The Rewrite becomes indefinite.

It remains until:

- You willingly reverse it.
- A Heart, Mind, Spirit, Karma, Dream, or soul-healing effect whose Source CL equals or exceeds yours removes it.
- A breakthrough or profound identity event overturns it.
- The target completes a specific printed recovery condition established during the rite.

Successful Save

The Rewrite lasts until the end of the next scene.

Identity Limits

Rewrite the Inner Heart can profoundly alter behavior and relationships, but it does not automatically:

- Replace memories.
- Grant skills or knowledge.
- Change a creature’s creature type.
- Rewrite a true name.
- Transfer a soul.
- Override a Secret Law or higher-authority identity Anchor.

It may still cause a creature to act very differently because its genuine emotional structure has changed.

Heart Scar

An unwilling target bears a visible spiritual scar detectable by Qi Sensing and relevant Mind or Spirit perception.

A healer examining the scar learns:

- That an emotional Rewrite occurred.
- The Source CL.
- Whether it added, removed, redirected, strengthened, or weakened an emotion.

It does not automatically reveal the original or new subject.

---

Cultivation Level 18 — One Cut Divides Ten Thousand Laws

Action  
Range: 120 feet  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

Choose one creature, object, Cultivation Asset, active manifestation, oath, soul, body, name, or other valid target bearing 3 Severance Marks or intersected by Divide Heaven and Earth.

Make one Cultivation Attack or force a Charisma saving throw, chosen according to whether your expression is a cutting strike or direct law.

On a hit or failed save, choose one Sovereign Severance.

On a miss or successful save, apply its listed lesser result.

Body from Soul

Full Severance:

- The target’s soul, consciousness, or animating spirit is removed from its body and appears as a visible incorporeal form in an adjacent space.
- The body is Incapacitated and Stable.
- The soul cannot reenter without reconnecting the severed relation.
- Possession of another body requires an independent legal feature.

Duration:

- Within 2 CL: until the end of your next turn, followed by repeated Charisma saves at the end of each turn.
- 3–5 CL lower: 1 minute with no automatic repeat.
- At least 6 CL lower: indefinite.

Lesser:

- Incapacitated until the end of the current turn.
- Cannot use Spirit, soul, possession, or body-transfer features until the start of its next turn.

Cultivation from Vessel

Full Severance:

Suppress all:

- Path features.
- Subpath features.
- Spheres and talents.
- Methods.
- Foundations’ active systems.
- Golden Core and Nascent Soul features.
- Domain Armaments.
- Recorded Arts.
- Forged Techniques.
- Immortal Arts.
- Cultivated-item active properties.
- Cultivation Point expenditure and recovery.

The target retains mundane movement, speech, ordinary ability checks, and ordinary equipment use.

Duration uses the same authority bands as Body from Soul.

Lesser:

- Cannot spend Cultivation Points or activate powered techniques until the start of its next turn.

Name from Authority

Full Severance:

Sever one supernatural name, title, office, lineage recognition, command authority, ownership bond, contract identity, artifact recognition, or Domain claim from the target.

Consequences may include:

- Artifacts no longer recognize it.
- Oaths and contracts cannot identify it as holder or beneficiary.
- Commanded assets no longer accept orders.
- A lineage inheritance becomes inaccessible.
- A titled Domain or Formation no longer recognizes its authority.
- Divination using the severed name fails.

This does not erase the target’s memories or ordinary social recognition unless the severed name was the actual conceptual basis of those effects.

Lesser:

- One named item, asset, contract, or authority refuses the target until the start of its next turn.

Technique from Source

Full Severance:

Choose one learned Sphere, Subpath, Method, Recorded Art family, Forged Technique, Secret feature, or cultivation system.

The target retains memory of it but cannot connect to its active use.

Duration uses the authority bands above.

Against a target at least 6 CL lower, this may be indefinite.

A Secret or Immortal feature requires a successful Cultivation Check against its save DC after the failed save.

Lesser:

- The chosen system is suppressed until the start of its next turn.

Cause from Effect

Full Severance:

Choose one category:

- Damage.
- Healing.
- Forced movement.
- Conditions.
- Summoning.
- Teleportation.
- Cultivation Point restoration.
- Command.
- Possession.

For the duration, actions and techniques used by the target cannot produce that category of effect.

Costs are still spent on attempted activations unless the inability was obvious before activation.

Lesser:

- The target’s next activation in that category fails to produce the chosen effect.

Target from World

Full Severance:

The target is cut away from ordinary space and exists in an adjacent conceptual interval.

While severed:

- It cannot affect or be affected by ordinary reality.
- It perceives the outside world as distant outlines.
- Its durations continue.
- It does not regain Cultivation Points.
- It may use an Action to make a Cultivation Check against your save DC when its Source CL is within 2 of yours or higher.

Duration:

- Within 2 CL: until the end of your next turn, with checks each turn.
- 3–5 CL lower: 1 minute.
- At least 6 CL lower: indefinite.

This differs from Void erasure: the target and world both remain, but their relation is cut.

Lesser:

- The target is removed until the start of its next turn.

Wound from Victim

Choose a willing creature or yourself.

Full Severance:

Remove one:

- Condition.
- Curse.
- Poison.
- Disease.
- Maximum-Hit-Point reduction.
- Cultivation seal.
- Possession.
- Contract consequence.
- Karmic burden.
- Hidden Injury.
- Permanent transformation.

The removed effect becomes a separate Severed Burden Anchor in an adjacent unoccupied space.

Severed Burden Anchor

- AC: 18
- Hit Points: 6 × your Qi Cultivation CL
- Resistance: All damage except Force, Psychic, and Void
- Immunity: Poison and Psychic damage
- Source CL: The greater of yours or the removed effect’s Source CL

Destroying the Anchor destroys the burden when your Source CL equals or exceeds it.

If the Anchor survives for 1 minute:

- The burden remains separated but not destroyed.
- It can be sealed, transferred, studied, or reattached by appropriate authority.

An effect whose Source CL exceeds yours requires a Cultivation Check against its save DC.

Lesser:

- Suppress the burden until the start of your next turn.

Reconnecting a Sovereign Severance

An indefinite Sovereign Severance can be repaired by:

- Equal/higher Conceptual Severance or conceptual restoration.
- Samsara return to a state before the cut.
- Karma or Fate authority proving and restoring the relationship.
- Name authority restoring a severed identity or ownership.
- Void authority erasing the cut itself without erasing the target.
- Reconstruction through the original complete cultivation source and a major breakthrough.
- An artifact, Immortal, ancestor, heavenly authority, or equivalent source.
- Acceptance of a permanent substitute relation or price established through play.

Ordinary healing, rest, retraining, or reacquiring proficiency does not repair an indefinite conceptual cut.

Cultivation Level 10 — Sever Attribute

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 5 Qi

Choose one creature, object, Cultivation Asset, or active manifestation bearing at least 1 Severance Mark.

Choose one attribute currently possessed by the target.

An unwilling creature makes a Charisma saving throw.

On failure, sever the attribute for the duration.

On success, sever it until the start of its next turn.

Eligible attributes include:

- One movement mode, such as flight, swimming, burrowing, teleportation, or Earth Glide.
- One Resistance.
- One Immunity, which becomes Resistance rather than being completely removed unless your Source CL exceeds the target by at least 3.
- Regeneration or automatic healing.
- Incorporeal movement.
- Invisible.
- One elemental tag or damage conversion.
- One sense, such as Truesight, Tremorsense, or Qi Sensing.
- One weapon property or item property.
- One aura or field-following property.
- One size increase, transformation trait, or manifested limb.
- One Sphere.
- One Method benefit.
- One Golden Core Form.
- One Nascent Soul feature.
- One Domain Armament mode.
- One Foundation active benefit.

Attribute Remains, Relation Ends

Sever Attribute does not erase the underlying source.

Examples:

- A wing remains visible but no longer connects to flight.
- Fire remains present but no longer connects to heat or Fire damage.
- A sword remains magical but no longer connects to one property.
- A cultivator still knows a Sphere but cannot connect it to active use.
- A Golden Core remains intact but cannot express one Form.

Major-System Severance

To sever a complete Sphere, Method, Golden Core, Nascent Soul feature set, Domain Armament system, Subpath, or Foundation active system:

- The target must bear at least 2 Severance Marks.
- Spend 2 marks when activating.
- A target within 2 CL repeats the Charisma saving throw at the end of each turn, ending the major severance on a success.
- A target 3–5 CL lower receives no automatic repeat for the duration.
- A target at least 6 CL lower may suffer an indefinite severance when you spend 2 additional Qi.
- A target 3 or more CL higher requires a successful Cultivation Check against its save DC after it fails the save.

Restoring an Attribute

An indefinite severance requires:

- Reconnection through an equal/higher Conceptual Severance or restoration authority.
- Reconstruction through the original inheritance, item, body, or cultivation source.
- A breakthrough explicitly reconnecting the system.
- Samsara return to a state before severance.
- Karma or Fate authority proving and restoring the relation.
- An artifact, Immortal, ancestor, or equivalent source.

Ordinary rest does not reconnect an indefinite severance.

player_card.summary: Interrupt an active connection between a cultivated effect, creature, object or source.

Effect: Choose one visible or identified active connection. Its maintaining creature makes a Charisma saving throw; if no creature maintains it, make a Cultivation Check against the connection’s save DC.
Failed save or successful check: Sever for 1 minute. Successful save or failed check: sever until the end of the current turn.

Consequences follow the relation: A Concentration effect ends unless it can persist without Concentration. A summon or asset becomes inert, uncontrolled or returns to its origin under its Source Rule. A Domain Armament falls or becomes inert. Possession ends if your Source CL equals or exceeds it. A Formation function is disabled while its Anchor remains separated.

A curse, oath or attunement is suppressed rather than permanently removed unless your Source CL exceeds it by at least 6. A moving field becomes fixed at its current location; a healing or command tether stops transmitting effects.

Higher Authority: A Secret, artifact, Immortal or target at least 3 CL higher receives its save, and you must also succeed on a Cultivation Check against its save DC for the 1-minute duration. Otherwise, severance lasts until the end of the current turn.
Choices: Eligible connections: Concentration to effect; summoner to summon; controller to Cultivation Asset; wielder to Domain Armament; possessing entity to host; talisman to target; Formation function to Anchor; oath to witness; curse to victim; teleportation route to destination Anchor; healing tether to recipient; command link to companion; item attunement to user; Recorded Art to temporary delivery medium; or field to moving origin.

Permanent Connection Cut: Against a connection with Source CL at least 6 lower, spend 2 additional Qi and 2 Severance Marks on its source to make severance indefinite. This may permanently cut item attunement, a possession tether, a summoned servant’s bond, an oath witness, a curse’s attachment or a Domain Armament bond.
Limits: Available at CL 6.

The cut cannot permanently destroy the underlying item, creature, soul, learned feature or oath text. Recovery requires rebuilding or reestablishing the relation through appropriate equal/higher authority.

Cultivation Level 18 — Living Heavenly Tribulation

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

Become a walking tribulation.

For the duration:

- Gain Immunity to Lightning and Thunder damage.
- Gain Resistance to all damage except Force, Psychic, and Void.
- Gain a Fly Speed of 60 feet and Hover.
- Tribulation Cloud Core is active around you in a 30-foot radius without requiring Concentration.
- Gain 1 Tribulation Spark at the start of each turn.
- Thunder Edge costs 0 Sparks once per turn.
- Heaven-Punishing Reprisal costs 0 Qi once per round.
- Your Thunder Seal maximum per creature increases by 3.
- A creature cannot conceal its cultivation structure from you while bearing at least three Seals unless its concealment has higher Source CL and succeeds against your Cultivation Check.

Nine Heavenly Judgments

At the start of each of your turns, choose one Judgment.

Judgment of Lightning

Choose one point within 120 feet.

Creatures in a 10-foot-radius, 60-foot-high cylinder make a Dexterity saving throw.

Failed Save: 6d8 Lightning damage and one Thunder Seal.  
Successful Save: Half damage.

Judgment of Thunder

Hostile creatures within 30 feet make a Constitution saving throw.

Failed Save: 4d8 Thunder damage, Prone, and no Reactions.  
Successful Save: Half damage.

Judgment of Revelation

Choose up to your Proficiency Bonus in creatures bearing Seals.

Until the start of your next turn:

- Invisible and false-body effects do not conceal them.
- You know their current Qi or other Cultivation Point total.
- You know which Path, Subpath, Method, Foundation-active, Golden Core, Nascent Soul, and Domain Armament systems are currently active.

Judgment of Empty Meridians

Choose one creature bearing at least four Seals.

It makes a Constitution saving throw.

Failed Save: It cannot spend or regain Cultivation Points until the start of your next turn.  
Successful Save: Its next Cultivation Point cost before then increases by 2.

Judgment of Heaven’s Prison

Choose one creature bearing at least six Seals.

Remove six Seals and use Sentence the Core without an Action or Qi cost.

On a failed save, you may suppress its entire cultivation instead of one system until the end of its next turn.

Entire cultivation includes:

- Spending or regaining Cultivation Points.
- Path and Subpath active features.
- Sphere talents.
- Recorded Arts.
- Forged Techniques.
- Immortal Arts.
- Methods.
- Foundation active abilities.
- Golden Core and Nascent Soul active systems.
- Cultivated-item active powers.

Passive mundane statistics and ordinary physical actions remain unless another effect says otherwise.

A creature at least 6 CL lower than you receives no initial save if it already bears the required six Seals. It may still use a specific higher-authority escape effect.

Tribulation Rebirth

The first time during the activation you would be reduced to 0 Hit Points without being killed outright:

- Remain at 1 Hit Point.
- Discharge every Thunder Seal within 120 feet.
- Each sealed hostile creature takes 1d8 Lightning damage per Seal removed, maximum 8d8.
- Gain Tribulation Sparks equal to half the total Seals removed, up to your maximum.

Each creature makes a Dexterity saving throw and takes half damage on a success.

tianxia.subpath.qi.hidden_thunder_draw_s.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 — One Cut Before Heaven Hears

Action  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene

Your saber must begin sheathed. You may spend any Stored Thunder, but the feature does not require it.

Choose one visible straight or curved cutting path:

- Up to 120 feet long.
- Up to 10 feet wide.
- Originating from you, your recorded Thunder Sheath, or your bound Draw Saber Domain Armament.

The path may bend once by up to 90 degrees at a visible point.

Before any creature may take a Reaction, resolve the cut against every creature, object, barrier, projectile, Formation Anchor, and active cutting-crossable effect along the path in the order encountered.

Creatures

Each chosen creature in the path makes a Dexterity saving throw.

Failed Save:

- 10d10 Slashing, Lightning, Thunder, or Force damage.
- Cannot take Reactions until the end of its next turn.
- Choose one Severance below.

Successful Save:

- Half damage.
- Cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Objects and Structures

Unattended objects, vehicles, structures, temporary barriers, and Formation Anchors take 12d10 Slashing or Force damage.

This damage:

- Ignores ordinary Resistance.
- Treats Damage Threshold as 0.
- Deals double damage to a single designated load-bearing or anchor section.

Artifacts and higher-authority structures use their printed protections and Source CL contests.

Projectiles and Active Effects

For each visible projectile, line, wall, tether, formation link, remote-origin connection, or spatial route crossed by the cut, make a Cultivation Check against its save DC.

- Success: Sever or dispel the crossed portion.
- Failure: The effect remains, but its Source learns that it was contested.

An effect whose Source CL is 6 or more lower than yours is severed automatically unless it possesses explicit Secret, artifact, or conceptual protection.

Cultivation Level 3 — Thunder in the Sheath

You accumulate Stored Thunder.

- Maximum Stored Thunder equals your Proficiency Bonus.
- Begin each scene with 0.
- Stored Thunder disappears when the scene ends.
- Gain no more than 1 Stored Thunder per round unless a feature expressly says otherwise.

Store Thunder

At the end of your turn, gain 1 Stored Thunder if all are true:

- Your chosen draw saber is sheathed.
- You did not deal damage with that saber during the turn.
- You did not activate a harmful weapon-delivered technique through it.
- You are conscious.

You also gain 1 Stored Thunder when Initiative is rolled while the saber is sheathed.

Hidden Sheath Mode

At Cultivation Level 9, a projected or real bound Draw Saber Domain Armament may enter Hidden Sheath Mode.

While in this mode:

- It occupies no visible floating position.
- It is treated as sheathed and stored against your body, shadow, scabbard, or compressed Qi seal.
- It cannot attack, guard, or serve as a remote origin.
- Calling or drawing it is still subject to effects that seal, restrain, or control the actual item.

Thunder-Draw Attack

You can use this when  You make the first attack with the sheathed saber during a turn.

Before rolling, spend any amount of Stored Thunder.

For each point spent:

- Add 1d8 Lightning, Thunder, Slashing, or Force damage on a hit.
- Increase the attack’s reach by 5 feet for this attack, to a maximum increase of 20 feet.

Choose the distribution before rolling. A point can provide damage or reach, not both.

On a hit after spending at least 2 Stored Thunder:

- The target cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Drawing the saber is part of the attack.

Return to Stillness

At the end of your turn, if you made only one attack with the draw saber and are legally able to sheath it, you may sheath it without using an action.

- 3–5 CL lower: 1 minute with no automatic repeat.
- At least 6 CL lower: until the end of the scene, the recorded harm is genuinely repaired, or equal/higher authority releases it.
- 3+ CL higher: until the start of its next turn unless you also succeed on a Cultivation Check against its save DC.

Choose one recorded victim, bearer of a transferred consequence, or rightful owner of stolen property.

Transfer one wound, condition, maximum-Hit-Point reduction, Cultivation Point loss, stolen property, curse, oath consequence, or other karmically linked burden from that creature to the judged target.

Failed Save — Merit Judgment

Restore the Benefactor

Return the Sacrifice

Restore one item, memory, emotion, lifespan portion, cultivation feature, or other genuine sacrifice the target paid for another creature, provided it still exists within Karma and was not erased by higher authority.

Heavenly Protection

For 1 minute, the target gains:

- Resistance to all damage except Force, Psychic, and Void.
- Advantage on all saving throws.
- Immunity to forced possession and unwilling cultivation theft from a Source CL lower than yours.

Move any number of the target’s Merit Marks to another willing creature and immediately Ripen them without using an action.

Successful Save

- Burden target loses Cultivation Points equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus and cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Merit target regains 4d8 + your modifier Hit Points and gains Advantage on its next saving throw.

Breaking a Heavenly Judgment

A persistent Burden Judgment can be broken by:

- Genuinely repairing, returning, releasing, or accepting the recorded consequence.
- Equal/higher Karma, Fate, Samsara, Void, Name, Oath, or Conceptual Severance authority.
- A major heavenly tribulation or breakthrough explicitly settling the causal thread.
- Proving through real supernatural authority that the recorded cause was false, transferred, or erased.
- Accepting an equivalent consequence approved by the Judgment’s causal structure.

A promise, contract, political pardon, legal acquittal, or disagreement does not automatically alter cultivated Karma. Only the actual cause, consequence, transferred burden, or a superior causal authority changes the thread.

Effect: Ancestral Skill: Choose two skills associated with your lineage and gain proficiency in both. For a skill in which you are already proficient, gain +2 to checks using it instead. Suggested skills by lineage are listed below.

Lineage Authority: For a creature within 60 feet with your lineage, a closely related lineage, or a derivative bloodline, identify whether its inheritance is dormant, awakened, damaged, implanted, stolen, diluted, or transformed; its approximate Source CL relative to yours; whether it actively suppresses its lineage; and whether you share direct ancestral resonance. Against equal- or higher-Source-CL concealment, make a Cultivation Check against the concealment DC.

Ancestral Command: Action; Range: 60 feet; Cost: 4 Qi. Target one creature whose bloodline is directly subordinate, derived from, or spiritually recognized by your lineage. Saving Throw: Charisma; failure permits one command below, while success prevents Reactions until the start of its next turn. Higher-Source-CL creatures have Advantage; creatures at least 6 CL below you have Disadvantage and no automatic repeat save during the command. Resemblance alone is insufficient; a real lineage relationship must exist.
Choices: Dragon suggested skills: Arcana, Intimidation, Nature, Perception.
Phoenix suggested skills: Insight, Medicine, Performance, Religion.
Jade Tortoise suggested skills: Athletics, History, Investigation, Survival.
Nine-Tailed Fox suggested skills: Deception, Insight, Performance, Persuasion.
Kunpeng suggested skills: Athletics, Nature, Perception, Survival.
Qilin suggested skills: Insight, Medicine, Persuasion, Religion.
Heavenly Serpent suggested skills: Deception, Medicine, Perception, Stealth.
Demon-Ancestry suggested skills: Athletics, Intimidation, Insight, Survival.

Memory Before Thought: Reaction; Trigger: You fail an ability check, Cultivation Check, or saving throw. Cost: 2 Resonance; once per round. Reroll and add PB; you must use the new result. Cannot reroll death saves, breakthrough rolls whose procedure forbids rerolls, or rolls already rerolled.
Kneel: The commanded creature falls Prone and cannot stand until the end of its next turn.
Still the Blood: It cannot activate bloodline features until the end of its next turn.
Return: Pull it up to 20 feet toward you.
Reveal: End its bloodline concealment for 1 minute.
Cease: It cannot take Reactions and has Disadvantage on attacks against you until the end of its next turn.
Limits: Available at CL 14.

Your bloodline carries complete techniques, instincts, and fragments of ancestral identity.

Ancestral Skill

Choose two skills associated with your lineage.

Gain proficiency in both. If already proficient, gain a +2 bonus to checks using that skill.

Suggested skills:

- Dragon: Arcana, Intimidation, Nature, Perception.
- Phoenix: Insight, Medicine, Performance, Religion.
- Jade Tortoise: Athletics, History, Investigation, Survival.
- Nine-Tailed Fox: Deception, Insight, Performance, Persuasion.
- Kunpeng: Athletics, Nature, Perception, Survival.
- Qilin: Insight, Medicine, Persuasion, Religion.
- Heavenly Serpent: Deception, Medicine, Perception, Stealth.
- Demon-Ancestry: Athletics, Intimidation, Insight, Survival.

Memory Before Thought

Reaction  
You can use this when  You fail an ability check, Cultivation Check, or saving throw.  
Cost: 2 Resonance  
Limit: Once per round

Reroll and add your Proficiency Bonus.

You must use the new result.

This cannot reroll:

- A death saving throw.
- A breakthrough roll whose procedure forbids rerolls.
- A roll already rerolled.

Lineage Authority

When a creature with your lineage, a closely related lineage, or a derivative bloodline is within 60 feet, you can identify:

- Whether its inheritance is dormant, awakened, damaged, implanted, stolen, diluted, or transformed.
- Its approximate Source CL relative to yours.
- Whether it is actively suppressing its lineage.
- Whether your lineages share a direct ancestral resonance.

Against concealment from an equal or higher Source CL, make a Cultivation Check against the concealment DC.

Ancestral Command

Action  
Range: 60 feet  
Cost: 4 Qi  
Saving Throw: Charisma

Target one creature whose bloodline is directly subordinate, derived from, or spiritually recognized by your lineage.

Failed Save: Choose one command:

- Kneel: It falls Prone and cannot stand until the end of its next turn.
- Still the Blood: It cannot activate bloodline features until the end of its next turn.

- It cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

player_card.summary: Grant a fixed group of allies stronger protective layers and improve Censure.

Effect: Target: Up to your Proficiency Bonus in different willing allies you can see, including yourself. End your previous Empyreal Layer or Court activation, then invest these allies. Each gains +2 AC, +2 on Wisdom saves, and 2d8 + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier Temporary Hit Points, minimum 1; roll once for all recipients.

The first time each round each invested creature would take damage, reduce it by PB + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier, minimum 1, after Resistance. Normal once-per-round and nonstacking layer rules still apply.

While you maintain the Court and are conscious and able to act, Judgment Saber range becomes 30 feet and uses a ranged Cultivation Attack beyond 5 feet. Censure placed during the Court grants 3d8 Radiant damage instead of 2d8; fix its dice when placed, even if the Court ends before the opening is claimed.

Until the start of your next turn

The next time a different ally hits the marked creature with an attack before the mark ends, add 2d8 Radiant damage and consume Censure. The hit must deal positive damage to Hit Points or Temporary Hit Points to claim the opening; double the extra dice on a Critical Hit.
One hit claims only one Censure even if several Administrators marked the target. Use the strongest available mark, breaking ties in favor of the earliest applied.

tianxia.subpath.qi.cultivator_of_seals.f.player_text:
CL18 — Heaven-Sealing Edict

Action  
Range: 90 feet  
Duration: 1 minute  
Concentration: Required  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Limit: Once per scene  
Saving Throw: Charisma

Choose one visible creature. Three immense Seal Pillars appear in legal unoccupied spaces within 30 feet of it. Each Pillar is an Anchor and bears one named binding:

1. Outer Heaven Pillar — movement, teleportation, flight, phasing, possession, and remote origins.
2. Meridian Pillar — Cultivation Point expenditure and recovery, Sphere techniques, weapon-delivered cultivation, and Domain Armament functions.
3. Core Pillar — Path, Subpath, Method, Golden Core, Nascent Soul, Foundation active systems, cultivated-item activations, Recorded Arts, Forged Techniques, and Immortal Arts.

Seal Pillar Profile

- Size: Medium object
- AC: Your Cultivation Save DC
- Hit Points: 6 × your CL each
- Resistance: Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing from noncultivated attacks
- Immunity: Poison and Psychic damage
- Source CL: Your CL
- Movement: None

A Pillar must be placed on a legal surface or in a legal Formation position. If no legal space exists for all three, the activation fails before Qi is spent.

Initial Resistance

The target makes one Charisma saving throw.

Successful Save

Only the Outer Heaven Pillar binds the target until the start of your next turn. The other two Pillars still appear but do not bind unless the target fails a later Edict save.

Failed Save

The target is bound by a number of Pillars based on authority and preparation:

- Within 2 CL or higher: Outer Heaven and Meridian Pillars.
- 3–5 CL lower: All three Pillars.
- At least 6 CL lower, Completely Subdued, or already bearing your Core Seal: All three Pillars, and Core Pillar imposes Complete Cultivation Suppression.

At the end of each of its turns, a target within 2 CL of you or higher repeats the Charisma save. On success, suppress one active Pillar of its choice until the end of its next turn.

A target 3–5 CL lower repeats the save at the end of every second turn. A target at least 6 CL lower receives no automatic repeat save.

Binding Effects

For each active Pillar:

- Outer Heaven: Speed is 0; the target cannot willingly teleport, fly, phase, become Incorporeal, possess, or use a remote technique origin outside its space.
- Meridian: The target cannot spend or regain Cultivation Points, use Sphere techniques, weapon-delivered techniques, or Domain Armament functions.
- Core: The target cannot activate Path, Subpath, Method, Foundation active, Golden Core, Nascent Soul, cultivated-item, Recorded Art, Forged Technique, Immortal Art, or transformation features.

When all three are active, the target suffers Complete Cultivation Suppression under the shared rule.

Break a Pillar

A Pillar ends when reduced to 0 Hit Points, lawfully displaced outside 60 feet of the target, or overcome by an equal- or higher-authority seal-breaking effect.

A creature adjacent to a Pillar may use an Action to attempt a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC. On success, deal Force damage to the Pillar equal to 5 × that creature’s Proficiency Bonus, ignoring resistance.

The bound target may use Break the Seal against one active Pillar. On success, suppress that Pillar until the end of its next turn. A second consecutive success destroys the binding between that Pillar and the target, though the physical Pillar remains until the Edict ends.

Direct Binding, Not a Puzzle

Knowing the Pillars’ names, observing their order, or guessing their inscription does not remove them. There is no Master Key or cognitive solution. The Edict ends through destroyed Anchors, failed Concentration, seal-breaking authority, a printed release clause, or superior Source CL.

Sealed Passage

A creature or effect cannot teleport, phase, summon, or project through the triangle defined by the three Pillars when its Source CL is lower than yours. Equal or higher authority requires a Cultivation Check against your save DC.

- Does not retroactively change an event already resolved.
- Does not rewrite a breakthrough, training, advancement, or campaign-generation roll.
- Does not create a critical hit unless you spend 2 additional Qi and the attack could normally critically hit.

- Does not waive legal target, range, line, material, or activation requirements.

Sovereign Fate Resistance

If the event is protected by one of the following, make a Cultivation Check against the protecting effect’s save DC:

- A Secret Law.
- An artifact fate-lock.
- A conceptual immunity to fate alteration.
- An explicit fate defense whose Source CL is equal to or higher than yours.
- A higher-authority causal effect that has already fixed the outcome.

Success: Rewrite Fate functions normally.

Failure:

- The event resolves normally.
- Spend 4 Qi instead of 8.
- Rewrite Fate’s once-per-scene limit is not expended.
- You cannot challenge that same protecting effect again until it changes or a new scene begins.

Read the Branches

Immediately after Rewrite Fate resolves successfully, learn one immediate consequence before choosing later actions:

- Whether the affected creature retains a Reaction.
- Whether one visible effect triggered or failed to trigger.
- Whether the result reduced a creature to 0 Hit Points.
- Whether the result ended Concentration.
- Whether the result crossed a printed threshold such as Bloodied, broken, or unstable.

Read the Branches does not reveal choices made after the rewritten event.

Action

---

Normalized Procedure — Heaven-Returning Impact

The Afterimage is a projected Body Asset and visual-auditory decoy, not a creature, Complete Soul, Companion, independent person or duplicate body. It occupies its space but has no physical mass except for its printed object manipulation.

It acts immediately after your turn and follows mental commands. Choose one listed action when its turn begins without spending an action; it may move before or after that action. If you give no command, it Dodges and stays where it is. While you are on the same plane and direct control is unblocked, commands have no distance limit.
It may Move, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Hide, Help, gesture, produce faint sounds or manipulate an unattended object weighing no more than 5 pounds.

Help uses the normal action and needs a legal position. It cannot provide knowledge, strength, tools or physical force it lacks. Hide uses its own Stealth check with your Stealth modifier and cannot make it more physically real.

Within 300 feet, you may see and hear through it simultaneously with your own senses unless a Source Rule says otherwise. This grants no special senses, perfect memory or line of effect from your body.

Object manipulation allows ordinary object interactions within its own space and reach, within the weight limit. It cannot attack, deal damage, activate items, use cultivation features, consume or attune items, steal worn objects or use cultivation items.
It is destroyed at 0 Hit Points, duration end or immediately when you create another. Its damage does not transfer to you; no remains or materials persist.
Choices: Shadow Exchange: Bonus Action; Range: 60 feet; Cost: 1 Stamina. Swap spaces with the Afterimage. You may see and hear through it while within 300 feet.

player_card.summary: Move after a hostile creature and strike if you reach it.

After the trigger, move up to current Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Thousand-Mile Legs applies normally. If airborne, you may activate Tread the Empty Sky within this Reaction without its normal Stamina cost or another action.

Your final space must be legally closer to the creature by straight-line distance than your starting space. If no such legal space can be reached, move as close as possible; if no movement would end closer, movement fails but the Reaction and Stamina are spent.
After moving, if the creature remains within unarmed reach, make one unarmed strike against it under the Granted Attack rule; it cannot trigger another granted attack.

Cultivation Level 3 - Guardian at the Gate

Reaction  
You can use this when  A hostile creature crosses your Guarded Threshold.

Make one unarmed strike or melee weapon attack against it before it completes the crossing.

On a hit, its movement ends in the nearest legal space before the threshold, its Speed becomes 0 until the end of the turn, and it cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

A creature can trigger this only once during the same movement. The attack follows the Granted Attack rule.

Normalized Procedure — Guardian at the Gate

- Make exactly one unarmed strike or melee weapon attack against the crossing creature. The attack follows the Granted Attack rule.

- If several spaces are equally near, you choose one that does not place the creature across the threshold. If no legal space exists, use Failed Spatial Movement with the status quo on the originating side.

player_card.summary: Create a stationary gate that controls hostile crossings and protects targets inside.

Effect: Area: 30-foot-radius, 30-foot-high cylinder centered on you. Place its center at the center of your current space; the cylinder and posts remain there when you move. Its boundary is the vertical outer surface and top.
On activation, choose any number of willing allies you can perceive. You and those allies cross freely; other creatures follow their current hostility and the normal crossing procedure.

A hostile creature crosses when ordinary movement would take any part of its space through the boundary, inward or outward. It makes a Strength or Charisma saving throw, its choice. Failure: place it in the nearest legal space on its originating side, deal 4d8 Force damage, set Speed to 0 for the turn, and prevent another crossing attempt that turn. Success: it crosses, paying double movement through the boundary as Difficult Terrain.
Hostile teleportation, phasing, or other spatial movement across the boundary uses one Cultivation Check and Failed Spatial Movement instead of that save.

Ranged attacks and effects crossing the boundary grant Three-Quarters Cover to targets inside. This applies only to a target inside when an attack or cover-sensitive effect originates outside and crosses the boundary. Destroying two posts changes this to Half Cover; destroying all four ends the entire Gate, including crossing restrictions and spatial checks.

Four visible projected Body Anchors appear at cardinal boundary points. Each is a separate Medium object that does not occupy its space and can attach to ground or a solid surface. Each has AC equal to your Cultivation Save DC, Hit Points 3 x CL, Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, and Force, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic. They cannot act, move, attack, or be harvested.

A post is destroyed at 0 Hit Points. Excess damage transfers neither to you nor another post. Healing requires a feature that repairs Body Assets or cultivation Anchors; it cannot restore a destroyed post in this activation unless expressly permitted.
If terrain prevents an exact cardinal position, use the nearest boundary point with line of effect to the center; the cylinder’s area stays the same.
Limits: Available at CL 18.
Maintain only one Heaven’s Closed Gate; a new activation ends the previous one without refunding costs.
