- Successful Save: It crosses, but the boundary is Difficult Terrain for that movement.

A hostile teleport or phase attempt instead uses the Cultivation Check and Failed Spatial Movement rules.

Ranged attacks and effects crossing the boundary grant Three-Quarters Cover to targets inside.

Four visible anchor posts appear at cardinal points. Each has AC equal to your Cultivation Save DC, Hit Points 3 x CL, Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, and Force, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic. Destroying two reduces protection to Half Cover; destroying all four ends the Gate.

You may maintain only one Heaven's Closed Gate.

---

Normalized Procedure — Heaven's Closed Gate

- When activated, choose the point at the center of your current space. The cylinder and anchor posts are stationary at that point for the duration; they do not move when you move.
- Choose any number of willing allies you can perceive when activating the Gate. You and those allies cross freely. A creature not chosen is treated according to its current hostility and the feature's normal crossing procedure.
- The boundary is the cylinder's vertical outer surface and top. A hostile creature crosses when ordinary movement would take any part of its space from outside to inside or inside to outside through that surface.
- On a failed Strength or Charisma save, place the creature in the nearest legal space on the side where the attempt began, deal 4d8 Force damage, set Speed to 0 for the turn, and prevent another crossing attempt that turn. On success, it crosses; movement through the boundary costs double as Difficult Terrain for that crossing.
- Hostile teleportation, phasing, and other spatial movement across the boundary use one Cultivation Check and Failed Spatial Movement instead of the Strength or Charisma save.
- Three-Quarters Cover applies only to a target inside when an attack or cover-sensitive effect originates outside and crosses the boundary. Destroying two posts changes this to Half Cover. Destroying all four ends the complete Gate, including crossing restrictions and spatial checks.
- The four posts are visible projected Body Anchors at the cardinal boundary points. Each is a discrete Medium object that does not occupy its space, can attach to ground or a solid surface, and has the printed AC, Hit Points, Resistances, and Immunities. They cannot act, move, attack, or be harvested.
- A post reduced to 0 Hit Points is destroyed. Excess damage does not transfer to you or another post. Healing a post requires a feature that can repair Body Assets or cultivation Anchors and cannot restore a destroyed post during the same activation unless expressly permitted.
- If terrain makes an exact cardinal point impossible, place the post at the nearest point on the boundary with line of effect to the center. This does not change the cylinder's area.
- You may maintain only one Heaven's Closed Gate. A new activation ends the previous one without refunding costs.

player_card.summary: Gain a larger functional size for physical contests and strengthen a charging unarmed strike.

Effect: Count as one size larger only for carrying, dragging, lifting, pushing, Grappling, Shoving, and determining whether another creature can move you. This changes neither occupied space, reach, weapon damage, equipment size, nor actual creature size.

Gain Advantage on checks and saves against push, pull, Prone, or unwilling movement. This does not automatically prevent teleportation unless that effect is adjudicated as moving you and permits such a save.
Choices: Ivory Charge: Once per turn, after willingly moving at least 15 feet during the current turn along a route that continuously reduces distance to a creature, hit it with an unarmed strike to add PB Bludgeoning or Force damage. Choose the type on the hit; the extra damage is part of it. After damage, the target makes a Strength save. Failure: push it 10 feet; success: push it 5 feet. Push directly away, following legal-placement and collision procedures. A target immune to forced movement still takes the extra damage.
Limits: Available at CL 3.

tianxia.subpath.body.white_elephant_sove.player_text:
Cultivation Level 3 - Sovereign Frame

Count as one size larger for carrying, dragging, lifting, pushing, Grappling, Shoving, and determining whether another creature can move you.

Gain Advantage on saves against being pushed, pulled, knocked Prone, or moved against your will.

Ivory Charge

Once per turn after moving at least 15 feet directly toward a creature before hitting with an unarmed strike, deal additional Bludgeoning or Force damage equal to Proficiency Bonus.

The target makes a Strength save. On a failure, push 10 feet; on a success, 5 feet.

Normalized Procedure — Sovereign Frame and Ivory Charge

- Sovereign Frame grants functional size one category larger only for carrying, dragging, lifting, pushing, Grappling, Shoving, and determining whether another creature can move you. It does not change occupied space, reach, weapon damage, equipment size, or actual creature size.
- Advantage applies to checks and saves made to resist push, pull, Prone, or unwilling movement. It does not automatically prevent teleportation unless that effect is adjudicated as moving you and permits such a save.
- Ivory Charge tracks voluntary movement during the current turn. You must move at least 15 feet along a route that continuously decreases the distance to the target before the qualifying unarmed-strike hit.
- The extra damage applies once per turn and is part of the hit. Choose Bludgeoning or Force on the hit.
- The target makes the Strength save after damage. On failure push 10 feet; on success push 5 feet. The push is directly away from you and follows legal-placement and collision procedures. A target immune to forced movement still takes the extra damage.

player_card.summary: Mark hostile creatures that damage your Hit Points as Remembered until scene end.

Effect: After a hostile creature deals at least 1 damage to your Hit Points, record its identity, Source CL, last known direction, and acquisition event. Maintain up to PB distinct creatures; if exceeding this limit, choose an existing record to forget or decline the new one.
Know a Remembered creature’s direction within 120 feet, without learning exact distance, route, current condition, disguise, plane, or an unknown creature’s identity.
It cannot gain Advantage against you merely because it is unseen. Other Advantage still applies, and your inability to see it can still give you Disadvantage.
Once per turn, add 2d8 Bludgeoning or Force damage to one hit against any Remembered creature; choose the type on the hit.
Add PB only to checks and saves against being moved, Grappled, Frightened, or Restrained by that Remembered creature or its active effect.
Limits: Available at CL 10.

tianxia.subpath.body.white_elephant_sove.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - The Body Remembers

When a hostile creature damages you, mark it as Remembered until scene end. Maintain a number equal to Proficiency Bonus; exceeding the limit requires forgetting one.

Against a Remembered creature:

- Know its direction within 120 feet.
- It cannot gain Advantage against you merely by being unseen.
- Once per turn on a hit, deal an additional 2d8 Bludgeoning or Force.
- Add Proficiency Bonus to checks and saves against being moved, Grappled, Frightened, or Restrained by it.

Normalized Procedure — Remembered Creature Records

- After a hostile creature deals at least 1 damage to your Hit Points, record it as Remembered until scene end. Record identity, Source CL, last known direction, and acquisition event.
- Maintain up to Proficiency Bonus distinct creatures. When exceeding the limit, choose one existing record to forget or decline the new record.
- Direction sense functions within 120 feet and does not reveal exact distance, route, current condition, disguise, plane, or identity of an unknown creature.
- A Remembered creature cannot gain Advantage against you merely because it is unseen. Other sources of Advantage still apply, and you can still have Disadvantage from inability to see it.
- The additional 2d8 applies once per turn on one hit against any Remembered creature. Choose Bludgeoning or Force on the hit.
- Add Proficiency Bonus only to checks and saves against being moved, Grappled, Frightened, or Restrained by that Remembered creature or its active effect.

player_card.summary: Gain Polearm proficiency and integrate wielded Polearms into Body Refining.

Effect: Record the wielded Polearm as integrated. Use Constitution instead of Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage rolls; you may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier for attack rolls.

Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply only as their rules expressly modify integrated weapons. If several rules replace the same damage die, use the highest legal replacement, without adding several weapon dice.

During your turn, increase Polearm reach by 5 feet. Outside your turn, use printed reach plus any active persistent increase. At CL 14, the two turn-only increases combine to +10 feet during your turn.

Heron’s Passing Cut: Trigger: You hit with a Polearm after moving at least 10 feet during the turn. Cost: 1 Stamina; once per turn across all Polearm attacks. After confirming the hit, pay and choose exactly one result below. Count actual voluntary movement completed this turn before the hit; teleportation does not count. Forced movement counts only if you willingly directed or accepted it and its rule counts it as your movement.
Choices: Move yourself 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. This is voluntary granted movement along a legal route.
Push the target 10 feet directly away from you.
Pull the target 5 feet into an unoccupied space within your current Polearm reach, without pulling it through a solid obstruction.
Add 1d8 Slashing or Force damage, increasing to 2d8 at CL 11 and 3d8 at CL 17. Choose the type when applied; this is part of the triggering hit, using only your current CL’s scaling.
Limits: Available at CL 3. Integration grants no weapon Sphere, other Sphere, talent, ammunition, additional attack, or separate weapon instance.

tianxia.subpath.body.white_heron_crescen.player_text:
Cultivation Level 3 - Crescent-Body Integration

Gain proficiency with Polearm weapons.

While wielding one:

- Use Constitution instead of Strength or Dexterity for attack and damage rolls.
- You may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier for attack rolls.
- It is integrated into Body Refining.
- Its reach increases by 5 feet during your turn.
- Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply to it.

This does not grant a weapon Sphere.

Heron's Passing Cut

You can use this when  You hit with a Polearm after moving at least 10 feet during the turn.  
Cost: 1 Stamina  
Limit: Once per turn

Choose one:

- Move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Push the target 10 feet.
- Pull it 5 feet into an unoccupied space within reach.
- Deal an additional 1d8 Slashing or Force damage, increasing to 2d8 at Cultivation Level 11 and 3d8 at Cultivation Level 17.

Normalized Procedure — Crescent-Body Integration and Heron's Passing Cut

- Record the wielded Polearm as an integrated weapon. Constitution replaces Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls, and you may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier for its attack rolls. This integration grants no Sphere, talent, ammunition, additional attack, or separate weapon instance.
- Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply only to the extent those features expressly modify an integrated weapon. If several rules replace the same weapon damage die, use the highest legal replacement rather than adding several weapon dice.
- The 5-foot reach increase applies only during your own turn. Outside your turn, use the Polearm's printed reach plus any currently active persistent reach increase. At Cultivation Level 14, the two turn-only increases combine for +10 feet during your turn.
- Heron's Passing Cut checks actual voluntary movement completed during the current turn before the hit. Teleportation does not count. Forced movement counts only when you willingly directed or accepted it and the movement rule says it counts as your movement.
- Declare Heron's Passing Cut after the hit is confirmed, pay 1 Stamina, and choose exactly one result. The feature remains once per turn across all Polearm attacks.
- The 10-foot self-movement is voluntary granted movement, follows a legal route, and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. The push moves directly away from you. The pull must end in an unoccupied space within your current Polearm reach and cannot pull the target through a solid obstruction.
- The additional damage is part of the triggering hit's damage packet, uses Slashing or Force as chosen when applied, and uses only the scaling appropriate to your current CL.

player_card.summary: Use one Polearm Attack action attack for a sweep that damages chosen nearby enemies.

Effect: Area: Every hostile creature of your choice within your weapon's reach. Replace the attack before rolling it; use your current Polearm reach when the sweep resolves. Each target makes one Dexterity saving throw and is affected once even if it occupies several spaces. Check cover and line of effect from you through the Polearm’s physical sweep.

Choose Slashing or Force for the activation. Damage is one integrated Polearm weapon damage die + Constitution modifier once + 3d8 of that type. On a failed save, deal full damage and choose an option below separately for each target; on success, deal half total damage with no additional effect.
After all saves, damage, and forced movement, move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. This is voluntary granted movement along a legal route.
Choices: Push the failed target 5 feet directly away from you, stopping at the nearest legal space.
Prevent the failed target’s Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Limits: Available at CL 10.
The sweep is one Body technique, not a weapon attack. It cannot critically hit or apply attack-hit effects, weapon mastery effects, or effects requiring a weapon attack to hit.
Additional Attack actions or replacement attacks do not increase the use limit.

tianxia.subpath.body.white_heron_crescen.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Crescent Reaping Circle

When you take the Attack action with a Polearm, replace one attack with a sweeping cut.

Area: Every hostile creature of your choice within your weapon's reach  
Cost: 2 Stamina  
Limit: Once per turn  
Saving Throw: Dexterity

On a failed save, a target takes one weapon damage die + Constitution modifier + 3d8 Slashing or Force damage, and you either push it 5 feet or prevent Reactions until the start of its next turn.

On a successful save, it takes half damage and suffers no additional effect.

After the sweep, move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

This is not a weapon attack and does not apply attack-hit riders.

Normalized Procedure — Crescent Reaping Circle

- Replace one attack of the Attack action before making that attack. The sweep is one Body technique, not a weapon attack, and affects each chosen hostile creature within your current Polearm reach at the moment the sweep resolves.
- Each target makes one Dexterity save and is affected once even if it occupies several spaces. Cover and line of effect are checked from you through the Polearm's physical sweep.
- The damage uses one damage die of the integrated Polearm, adds Constitution modifier once, and adds 3d8 Slashing or Force as chosen for that activation. It does not apply critical hits, attack-hit riders, weapon mastery riders, or effects requiring a weapon attack to hit.
- On a failed save, choose push or Reaction denial separately for each target. A push is 5 feet directly away from you and stops at the nearest legal space. On a successful save, the target takes half total damage and no rider.
- Resolve all saves, damage, and forced movement before taking the printed 10-foot self-movement. That movement is voluntary granted movement, follows a legal route, and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- The sweep remains once per turn even if another feature grants additional Attack actions or replacement attacks.

player_card.summary: Move up to twice your Speed and sweep hostile creatures before entering a guarded stance.

Effect: Choose a continuous route no longer than twice your current Speed. This is voluntary movement, not teleportation, and does not provoke Opportunity Attacks. Cross liquids and vertical surfaces and pass through hostile spaces as Difficult Terrain, while maintaining a line of travel and enough space for your body. Solid barriers, Total Cover, and spaces too small for you block passage.

Choose any number of hostile creatures that come within your current Polearm reach. A creature first becomes eligible when any part of its space enters that reach; resolve its Dexterity saving throw then, at most once per activation. Surviving solid barriers and Total Cover block the physical sweep beyond them.

Failure: choose Slashing or Force for that target and deal 10d8 damage, push it up to 15 feet directly away from your position at that moment along a legal route, and prevent Reactions until the end of its next turn. Success: half damage, push exactly 5 feet if a legal space exists, and prevent Reactions until the start of its next turn. The Reaction restriction lasts its printed duration even if the push is shortened or prevented; forced movement cannot place it illegally.
After all movement and target resolutions, enter a guarded stance until the start of your next turn: +2 AC and +5-foot reach, persistently enlarging your threatened space for that interval.

The first hostile creature physically entering that reach after the stance begins provokes one Opportunity Attack that spends no Reaction. This strike can occur only once, follows the Granted Attack rule, and cannot generate another attack. Expanding reach around a stationary creature is not entry.
Limits: Available at CL 18.
Crossing liquids or vertical surfaces grants no lasting flight. If you end unsupported, resolve falling after the feature finishes unless another rule supports you.

tianxia.subpath.body.white_heron_crescen.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 - Moon over the Reed Sea

Action  
Movement: Up to twice your Speed  
Cost: 7 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

Move without provoking Opportunity Attacks. You may cross liquids and vertical surfaces and move through hostile spaces as Difficult Terrain, but not through solid barriers, total cover, or spaces too small for you.

Choose any number of hostile creatures that come within Polearm reach. Each makes a Dexterity saving throw and can be affected only once.

- Failed Save: 10d8 Slashing or Force damage, pushed up to 15 feet, and no Reactions until the end of its next turn.
- Successful Save: Half damage, pushed 5 feet, and no Reactions until the start of its next turn.

When movement ends, enter a guarded stance until the start of your next turn: +2 AC, reach increased by 5 feet, and the first hostile creature entering your reach provokes one Opportunity Attack that does not consume your Reaction. This strike can occur only once and follows the Granted Attack rule.

Normalized Procedure — Moon over the Reed Sea

- Choose a continuous route no longer than twice your current Speed. This is voluntary movement, not teleportation. It ignores Opportunity Attacks and permits movement across liquids, vertical surfaces, and hostile spaces as printed, but still requires line of travel and sufficient space for your body.
- Moving across a liquid or vertical surface does not grant lasting flight. If the movement ends unsupported, resolve falling after the feature finishes unless another rule supports you.
- A hostile creature becomes eligible the first time during this activation any part of its space comes within your current Polearm reach. It can be affected only once. A surviving solid barrier or total cover blocks the physical sweep beyond it.
- Resolve a target's save when it first becomes eligible. On a failure, choose Slashing or Force damage for that target, then choose a legal push distance up to 15 feet directly away from your position at that moment. On success, push exactly 5 feet if a legal space exists.
- Reaction denial applies for the printed duration regardless of whether the push is shortened or prevented. Forced movement cannot place a target in an illegal space.
- After all movement and target resolutions, enter the guarded stance. Its +2 AC and +5-foot reach are persistent until the start of your next turn and therefore enlarge your threatened space during that interval.
- The stance's reaction-free Opportunity Attack can occur once. It triggers only when a hostile creature physically enters that reach after the stance begins; expanding your reach around a stationary creature does not count as entry. The attack follows the Granted Attack rule and cannot generate another attack.

---

player_card.summary: Make a Polearm attack to interrupt a nearby melee attack and choose a protective result on a hit.

Effect: Trigger: A creature within your weapon's reach makes a melee attack against you or a creature adjacent to you. Declare after it chooses the target and commits the attack, but before its attack roll. Spend the Reaction and cost and resolve one Polearm attack first.
Use the weapon reach that applies outside your turn. Turn-only increases do not apply; persistent increases such as Moon over the Reed Sea’s guarded stance do.

Your granted attack follows the Granted Attack rule and cannot grant another attack. A miss leaves the triggering attack unchanged. On a hit, choose exactly one option before the triggering attack roll.
Choices: Subtract PB from the triggering attack roll only; damage and later attacks are unchanged.
Move the protected creature 5 feet to a legal destination without provoking Opportunity Attacks. A conscious unwilling creature can decline; if it does, choose another result.
Push the attacker 5 feet directly away from you.
Prevent the attacker’s Reactions from after your Polearm hit until the start of its next turn; a Reaction already spent is not canceled.
Limits: Available at CL 6.
After either movement option, recheck the triggering attack’s reach and legal target. If its target is now out of reach, the attack misses without an attack roll.

tianxia.subpath.body.white_heron_crescen.player_text:
Cultivation Level 6 - One-Legged Guard

Reaction  
You can use this when  A creature within your weapon's reach makes a melee attack against you or a creature adjacent to you.  
Cost: 1 Stamina  
Limit: Once per round

Make one Polearm attack before its attack resolves.

On a hit, choose one:

- Subtract your Proficiency Bonus from the triggering attack roll.
- Move the protected creature 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Push the attacker 5 feet.
- Prevent the attacker from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn.

If moved outside its reach, the triggering attack misses. The granted attack follows the Granted Attack rule.

Normalized Procedure — One-Legged Guard

- Declare after the attacker chooses its target and commits to the melee attack but before the triggering attack roll. Spend the Reaction and Stamina, then resolve the granted Polearm attack first.
- “Within your weapon's reach” uses the reach that applies outside your turn. Turn-only reach increases do not apply. A persistent reach increase, such as the guarded stance from Moon over the Reed Sea, does apply.
- If your Polearm attack misses, the triggering attack resolves unchanged. On a hit, choose exactly one printed result before the triggering attack roll.
- Subtracting Proficiency Bonus modifies the triggering attack roll only. It does not reduce damage or affect later attacks.
- Moving the protected creature requires a legal 5-foot destination. A conscious unwilling creature can decline that movement; if it declines, choose another result. The movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks.
- Pushing the attacker is forced movement directly away from you. After either movement result, recheck the triggering attack's reach and legal target. If its target is no longer within reach, the triggering attack misses without an attack roll.
- Reaction denial begins after your Polearm attack hits and lasts until the start of the attacker's next turn. It does not cancel a Reaction already spent before this feature resolved.
- The granted attack cannot grant another attack and remains subject to the once-per-round limit.
tianxia.subpath.body.white_heron_crescen.why: CLARITY3: owner-approved display-only clarity pass; preserve all mechanics.

player_card.summary: Increase your turn’s Polearm reach and move through a struck creature to gain another benefit.

Effect: Gain another 5 feet of Polearm reach during your turn, combining with Crescent-Body Integration for +10 feet. This does not enlarge threatened space outside your turn.

Once during each of your turns, after a Polearm hit resolves, move through that creature’s space as Difficult Terrain, up to half your current Speed, ending in an unoccupied legal space. You do not provoke Opportunity Attacks from that creature; others interact with the movement normally.
When you leave its space, choose one result below. Choose one printed result after reaching the destination.
Choices: Make one Polearm attack against a different creature currently within reach, following the Granted Attack rule.
Push the original creature 10 feet directly away from your final position unless no legal route exists.
After your movement, the original creature makes one Strength saving throw. Failure: knock it Prone; success: it remains standing.
Gain +2 AC after the movement until the start of your next turn. This is a bonus, not a replacement AC formula.
Limits: Available at CL 14.

You cannot pass through Total Cover, a solid obstruction, or a space too small for your body. If you cannot complete at least 5 feet of legal movement through the triggering creature’s space, you gain no ending result.

tianxia.subpath.body.white_heron_crescen.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - White Wing Crosses the Reed Field

Your Polearm reach increases by another 5 feet during your turn.

Once during each of your turns, after hitting a creature with a Polearm, move through that creature's space as Difficult Terrain without provoking its Opportunity Attacks, up to half your Speed, ending in an unoccupied space.

When you leave its space, choose one:

- Make one Polearm attack against a different creature within reach.
- Push the original creature 10 feet.
- Knock the original creature Prone if it fails a Strength saving throw.
- Gain +2 AC until the start of your next turn.

The additional attack follows the Granted Attack rule.

Normalized Procedure — White Wing Crosses the Reed Field

- The additional 5-foot reach increase is turn-only and combines with Crescent-Body Integration for a total +10 feet during your turn. It does not enlarge threatened space outside your turn.
- Trigger after a Polearm hit once during your turn. The movement occurs after that hit resolves and can pass through the triggering creature's occupied space as Difficult Terrain. It cannot pass through total cover, a solid obstruction, or a space too small for your body.
- Move no more than half your current Speed and end in an unoccupied legal space. This movement does not provoke Opportunity Attacks from the triggering creature; other creatures interact with it normally.
- Choose one printed result after reaching the destination. The additional Polearm attack must target a different creature currently within reach and follows the Granted Attack rule.
- The 10-foot push moves the original creature directly away from your final position unless no legal route exists. The Prone option calls for one Strength save after your movement; on a success, the creature remains standing.
- The +2 AC begins after the movement and lasts until the start of your next turn. It is an AC bonus and does not replace your AC formula.
- If you cannot complete at least 5 feet of legal movement through the triggering creature's space, you do not gain a chosen ending result.

player_card.summary: Gain ascetic defenses, rest through meditation, and conserve Stamina while still.

Effect: Gain Immunity to mundane disease and environmental cold. These do not include supernatural disease, Cold damage, curses, Tribulations, or cultivation afflictions unless the Source Rule classifies them as mundane or environmental.

You no longer need ordinary food or drink for normal nutrition. Spirit appetites, Method requirements, Offerings, medicine, rare-material costs, and Source Rules consuming specific substances still apply.

Complete a Long Rest with 4 hours of meditation while aware of your surroundings, if all other Long Rest requirements are met. You are still resting: you cannot perform strenuous activity, guard through active combat, train, craft, or maintain incompatible Concentration.

Gain Advantage on saving throws against Exhaustion, possession, and forced bodily transformation. For possession and transformation, Advantage also applies to contests resisting entry, control, or alteration; it cannot remove an established effect unless that effect permits a repeated save.
Choices: Still as the Peak: At the start of your turn, if any body part touches earth, stone, or worked masonry and you have not willingly moved since the end of your previous turn, reduce the Stamina cost of your next Body Refining Path or Subpath feature activated before the end of the turn by 1, minimum 1. Forced movement does not break eligibility; any voluntary movement does. Apply this to the first eligible activation and expend the benefit, available once per round, even if the feature has multiple costs.
Limits: Available at CL 14.

tianxia.subpath.body.yamabushi.feature.a.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - Ascetic Body

You gain:

- Immunity to mundane disease.
- Immunity to environmental cold.
- No requirement for ordinary food or drink.
- The ability to complete a long rest through 4 hours of meditation while remaining aware of your surroundings.
- Advantage on saving throws against Exhaustion, possession, and forced bodily transformation.

Still as the Peak

At the start of your turn, if you are touching earth, stone, or worked masonry and have not willingly moved since the end of your previous turn, reduce the Stamina cost of the next Body Refining Path or Subpath feature you activate before the end of the turn by 1, to a minimum of 1. This functions once per round.

Normalized Procedure — Ascetic Body
- Mundane disease and environmental cold are distinct from supernatural disease, Cold damage, a curse, a Tribulation, or a cultivation affliction unless its Source Rule classifies it as mundane or environmental.
- Not requiring ordinary food or drink removes normal nutritional upkeep. It does not waive a spirit appetite, Method requirement, Offering, medicine, rare-material cost, or Source Rule that consumes a specific substance.
- The 4-hour meditation completes a Long Rest only if all other Long Rest requirements are met. You remain aware but are still resting and cannot perform strenuous activity, guard through active combat, train, craft, or maintain an incompatible Concentration effect during the meditation.
- Advantage against possession and forced bodily transformation applies to saves and contests resisting entry, control, or alteration. It does not remove an effect already established unless that effect permits a repeated save.
- Still as the Peak. Determine eligibility at the start of your turn. Forced movement since the end of your previous turn does not break the requirement; any voluntary movement does. Touching earth, stone, or worked masonry with any part of your body qualifies. Apply the reduction to the first eligible Body Refining Path or Subpath activation before the end of that turn, then expend the once-per-round benefit even if the feature has multiple costs.

An effect with lower Source CL than yours cannot push, pull, knock you Prone, or teleport you unwillingly. An equal- or higher-CL effect contests your Cultivation Check when attempting to move or teleport you.
Once per turn when you hit with an unarmed strike or integrated Staff weapon, add 2d8 Bludgeoning or Force damage.
Limits: Available at CL 18.

player_card.summary: Blast nearby creatures for 6d6 Bludgeoning or Force damage and turn the ground into Difficult Terrain.

Effect: Area: 20-foot-radius sphere centered on you. Saving Throw: Dexterity. Each other creature inside makes one save and is affected once; allies are affected unless another feature protects them. You are not a target. Choose the damage type on activation for all its damage.
Failure: full damage and Prone. Success: half damage and remain standing.

The shock requires line of effect through ground or surrounding physical medium. It cannot pass a complete blocking barrier unless this activation destroys that barrier and its rule permits simultaneous passage.
Unattended objects, structures, temporary barriers, and terrain take double damage once. Worn, carried, wielded, piloted, and actively controlled objects are not unattended.

Ordinary ground inside becomes Difficult Terrain. Each affected 5-foot square remains so until cleared by 1 minute of ordinary work with suitable tools, repaired by appropriate cultivation or crafting, or replaced by terrain authority of equal or higher Source CL.
Limits: Available at CL 10. The terrain change stays inside the area and causes no world-scale geological damage beyond printed damage to discrete targets.

tianxia.subpath.body.yamabushi.feature.m.player_text:
Cultivation Level 10 - Mountain's Wrath

Action  
Area: 20-foot-radius sphere centered on you  
Cost: 4 Stamina  
Saving Throw: Dexterity

On a failed save, a creature takes 6d6 Bludgeoning or Force damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half damage and remains standing.

Unattended objects, structures, temporary barriers, and terrain take double damage. The ground becomes Difficult Terrain until cleared or repaired.

Normalized Procedure — Mountain's Wrath
- The sphere is centered on you and affects each other creature in the area once. You are not a target. Allies are affected unless another feature protects them.
- Choose Bludgeoning or Force when you activate the feature; all damage from that activation uses the chosen type.
- The effect requires line of effect through the ground or surrounding physical medium. It does not pass a complete barrier that blocks the shock unless that barrier is itself destroyed by the same activation and its rule permits simultaneous passage.
- Listed unattended objects and terrain take double damage once. Worn, carried, wielded, piloted, or actively controlled objects are not unattended.
- Ordinary ground in the area becomes Difficult Terrain. It remains until each affected 5-foot square is cleared by 1 minute of ordinary work with suitable tools, repaired by an appropriate cultivation or crafting procedure, or replaced by terrain authority of equal or higher Source CL.
- The terrain alteration is bounded to the 20-foot-radius area and does not create world-scale geological damage beyond the printed damage to discrete targets.
tianxia.subpath.body.yamabushi.feature.m.why: CLARITY3: owner-approved display-only clarity pass; preserve all mechanics.

player_card.summary: Gain aquatic movement, breathing, senses, and a temporary liquid form.

Effect: Gain a Swim Speed equal to walking Speed and breathe air and water. Gain Darkvision 60 feet, or add 30 feet to existing Darkvision.

player_card.summary: Choose one effect affecting you and try to purify it through its matching option.

Choices: Poisoned: Repeat the original save and DC with Advantage. If none was printed, make a Constitution save against the source's Cultivation Save DC or fallback Authority DC. Success ends that one Poisoned condition. Failure suppresses its effects until the start of your next turn while its duration continues.

Disease: Make a Constitution save against the printed disease DC or fallback Authority DC. Success suppresses that disease's active penalties for 24 hours and adds one success. Three total successes end it. Failure adds no consequence and erases no successes. Track each disease separately; a new infection starts a new record unless the disease says otherwise.

Ongoing Acid or Poison: Repeat one ongoing Acid- or Poison-damage effect's printed save with Advantage. If none exists, make a Constitution save against its source DC. Success ends that effect. Failure reduces only its next damage instance by 2d8 + Constitution modifier, to a minimum of 0, then the reduction expires.

Contaminated Substance: End one temporary numerical penalty directly and solely caused by consumed poison, spoiled medicine, contaminated food, or an ordinary alchemical substance. The source must explicitly identify a penalty to AC, Speed, an ability check, attack roll, save, damage roll, or maximum Hit Points. This does not end damage, a condition, disease, curse, addiction, beneficial tradeoff, or the source item itself.
Limits: Available at CL 6.

This is bodily purification, not general dispelling or exorcism. It cannot remove Exhaustion, Hidden Injuries, Foundation damage, Tribulation scars, curses, possession, permanent corruption, or an effect tagged Curse, Tribulation, Foundation Injury, or Permanent. Any excluded tag makes an effect ineligible even if it also uses Poison or Disease language.
You may try the same effect again on later turns. Spend the Stamina and Bonus Action whether the save succeeds or fails.

player_card.summary: Create a prison that restrains and tethers chosen hostile creatures.

Failed initial save: The creature is Restrained and Prison Tethered to the center. It cannot willingly leave the cylinder; spatial movement outside requires a Cultivation Check against your Cultivation Save DC, with Failed Spatial Movement on failure.

player_card.summary: Interrupt an unwanted spiritual intrusion with Lesser Exorcism.

Effect: Requires Spirit Awakening, CL4+, Spiritual Sense. At level selection, increase Wisdom, Intelligence or Charisma by 1, up to your current Realm’s maximum. Your Source CL is your Spirit Awakening CL.
Target: One creature, object, location, manifested spirit, or Spiritual Anchor that you can perceive with Spiritual Sense or Soul Gaze, or one target bearing your Resonance Mark.

Choose one attached Intrusion you can perceive. Make a Spirit Awakening Cultivation Check against its Cultivation Save DC; if absent use the possessing spirit’s or creator’s Cultivation Save DC, then the Rules Reference fallback Authority DC for the source’s Realm if neither exists.

Failure: the Intrusion remains; learn its broad category, Source CL band relative to you, and whether a creature, Bond, vessel, location, Domain or Spiritual Anchor sustains it. On success, compare its Source CL with yours:

Success, Source CL 6 or More Lower: End one ordinary temporary Intrusion. For Possession, achieve Grade 2 Separation, placing the Intruder in its legal adjacent manifestation, legal vessel or visible noncontrolling outline. Instead suppress a permanent, Secret, artifact, divine or explicitly anchored Intrusion until the scene ends and reveal one printed release requirement.

Success, Source CL 3–5 Lower: Suppress for up to 1 minute with Concentration. The Host immediately repeats one allowed saving throw with Advantage; the Intruder becomes perceptible and cannot conceal its link during suppression.
Success, Source CL Within 2: Suppress until the end of the target’s next turn. The Host immediately repeats one allowed save with Advantage; if none exists, suppression is the complete result.

Success, Source CL 3 or More Higher: No suppression. The Host immediately repeats one allowed save with Advantage. Expose the Intrusion’s manifestation and its sustaining Anchor’s direction to your Spiritual Sense until the end of your next turn.

At CL13, when you gain Spiritual Exorcism from Spirit Awakening: cost becomes 1 Resonance, range 60 feet, successful suppression of a lower-Source-CL Intrusion needs no Concentration; exposing an equal- or higher-authority Intrusion gives the target Advantage on its next save against it before the scene ends.
Choices: Eligible Intrusions: unwilling Possession; unwilling or coercive Hosting; dream intrusion; spiritual contamination; imposed emotional corruption; memory interference; hostile spirit presence; or a curse with a spiritual component in its Source Rule.

A willing Host may waive resistance made on its behalf; a willing Intruder does not resist separation. If both oppose, use the higher relevant Cultivation Save DC; if only one opposes, use that opponent’s DC.
Limits: A specific Intrusion can be targeted by your Lesser Exorcism only once per round.

Cannot target a willing stable Covenant Bond without both parties’ consent; integrated spirit ancestry or a legal Species, Path, Subpath, Foundation, Method, Origin Insight or ordinary memory; completed death, reincarnation, permanent soul destruction or divine custody; or an artifact, Secret, Immortal or world-law effect unless its Source Rule permits ordinary exorcism.

Cannot destroy a Complete Soul, transfer spirit ownership, create a Companion Bond, strip integrated ancestry or remove legal character options; cannot bypass a named rite, material, location, authority or higher Source CL requirement unless the result expressly satisfies it.
Does not grant the Spirit Companions Sphere or replace the Exorcist tradition.

insight.exorcist-s-calling.player_text:
Exorcist's Calling

Requirements: Spirit Awakening, CL4+ (Cultivation Level), Spiritual Sense
Ability Increase (Level Selection): Increase your Wisdom, Intelligence, or Charisma score by 1, to the maximum allowed by your current Realm (a stage of cultivation).
Source CL: Your Spirit Awakening CL.

You have learned to diagnose and interrupt invasive spiritual influences before gaining the Path's complete exorcism feature.

Lesser Exorcism

Use an action.
Range: 30 feet
Cost: 2 Resonance
Target: One creature, object, location, manifested spirit, or Spiritual Anchor that you can perceive with Spiritual Sense or Soul Gaze, or one target bearing your Resonance Mark

Choose one Intrusion attached to the target that you can perceive:

- unwilling Possession;
- unwilling or coercive Hosting;
- dream intrusion;
- spiritual contamination;
- imposed emotional corruption;
- memory interference;
- hostile spirit presence; or
- a curse whose Source Rule has a spiritual component.

You cannot target:

- a willing stable Covenant Bond unless both bonded parties consent to separation;
- integrated spirit ancestry or a legal Species, Path, Subpath, Foundation, Method, Origin Insight, or ordinary memory;
- completed death, reincarnation, permanent soul destruction, or divine custody; or
- an artifact, Secret, Immortal, or world-law effect unless its Source Rule permits ordinary exorcism.

Resolution

Make a Spirit Awakening Cultivation Check against the Intrusion's Cultivation Save DC. If it has no printed DC, use the possessing spirit's or creator's Cultivation Save DC. If neither exists, use the Rules Reference fallback Authority DC for the source's Realm.

On a failed check, the Intrusion remains. Learn its broad category, its Source CL band relative to you, and whether it is sustained by a creature, Bond, vessel, location, Domain, or Spiritual Anchor.

On a successful check, compare Source CL:

- 6 or More Lower: End one ordinary temporary Intrusion. For Possession, achieve Grade 2 Separation and place the Intruder in its legal adjacent manifestation, legal vessel, or visible noncontrolling outline. A permanent, Secret, artifact, divine, or explicitly anchored Intrusion is suppressed until the scene ends and reveals one printed release requirement instead.
- 3–5 Lower: Suppress the Intrusion for up to 1 minute while you maintain Concentration. The Host immediately repeats one saving throw the Intrusion allows with Advantage. The Intruder becomes perceptible and cannot conceal its link during suppression.
- Within 2: Suppress the Intrusion until the end of the target's next turn. The Host immediately repeats one allowed saving throw with Advantage. If no repeat save exists, suppression is the complete result.
- 3 or More Higher: Do not suppress it. The Host immediately repeats one allowed saving throw with Advantage. Expose the Intrusion's manifestation and the direction of its sustaining Anchor to your Spiritual Sense until the end of your next turn.

A willing Host may waive resistance made on its behalf. A willing Intruder does not resist separation. If both Host and Intruder oppose separation, use the higher relevant Cultivation Save DC; if only one opposes, use that opponent's DC.

Limits

- A specific Intrusion can be targeted by your Lesser Exorcism only once per round.
- Lesser Exorcism cannot destroy a Complete Soul, transfer spirit ownership, create a Companion Bond, strip integrated ancestry, or remove legal character options.
- It cannot bypass a named rite, material, location, authority, or higher Source CL requirement unless the result expressly satisfies it.

CL13 Improvement

When you gain Spiritual Exorcism from Spirit Awakening:

- Lesser Exorcism costs 1 Resonance;
- its range becomes 60 feet;
- successful suppression against a lower-Source-CL Intrusion does not require Concentration; and
- when you expose an equal- or higher-authority Intrusion, the target has Advantage on its next saving throw against it before the scene ends.

This Insight does not grant the Spirit Companions Sphere and does not replace the Exorcist tradition.

Effect: At level selection, increase your Constitution, Wisdom, or Charisma score by 1, to the maximum allowed by your current Realm.
Trigger: You would gain one or more Corruption from a single event. Before applying it, make a Wisdom (Insight) check against DC 12 + your current Corruption.
Success: Delay the triggering Corruption until the current scene ends; record its amount and source. At scene end, gain all Corruption delayed by this Insight simultaneously.
Failure: Gain the Corruption immediately and record one Temptation; choose or roll 1d6 using the d6 Temptation table below.
Choices: 1: Conceal the Corruption or its source from an ally or authority.
2: Seize, consume, protect, or study the object or essence that caused it.
3: Accept a further offer of power, knowledge, or access from the source.
4: Isolate yourself from anyone likely to interfere.
5: Spare, obey, imitate, or bargain with the entity behind the Corruption.
6: Prove your superiority through an unnecessary risk, contest, or display.
Limits: Requirements: Daemonic Cultivation and either Spirit Awakening or Wisdom 14+, CL5+.
Ending, suppressing or bargaining with the source does not erase delayed Corruption unless that Source Rule expressly removes Corruption already incurred.
A Temptation is a recorded impulse, not control. It cannot compel an action, impose a condition or create additional Corruption unless another Source Rule says so. It ends with the scene.
An effect expressly saying its Corruption cannot be delayed overrides this Insight.

Applying a Rising Mark

TAL_YANG_BASE_SPHERE_ABILITIES.player_text:
BASE SPHERE ABILITIES

The Yang sphere uses Rising Marks. A Rising Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Rising Marks unless a feature says otherwise.
A Rising Mark represents a motion, wound, breath, oath, technique, or intention that has begun to swell toward completion.
Mark Limit
You can maintain a number of Rising Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature, object, or ongoing effect can have only one Rising Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise.
A Rising Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked subject is no longer on the same plane of existence as you.
Kindled and Overkindled Marks
A Rising Mark has one of two expressions.
Kindled Mark. A Rising Mark on you, a willing creature, an unattended object, or an effect you created is a Kindled Mark. You spend Kindled Marks to help an action complete.
Overkindled Mark. A Rising Mark on an unwilling creature, hostile object, enemy effect, or creature that rejects your assistance is an Overkindled Mark. You spend Overkindled Marks to make hostile exertion overcomplete, exposing or straining the source.
A willing creature may end your Rising Mark on itself at any time, no Action required.
Applying a Rising Mark
You can apply a Rising Mark in three basic ways.
Kindle the Rising. As a Bonus Action, choose yourself or one willing creature, unattended object, or ongoing effect you created within 60 feet that you can perceive. The target gains one Kindled Mark.
Force the Rising. As a Reaction when a creature, object, or effect within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends cultivation points (your Path resource), uses a spell slot, uses a limited feature, teleports, becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Overkindled Mark to the source after the triggering event resolves.
Rising Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Fire, Radiant, or Force damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Overkindled Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Rising Thread Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 (Cultivation Level) | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d6 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi becoming too bright, too hot, or too forceful to remain unfinished.
Spending a Rising Mark
Once per round, when a marked subject you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Rising Mark without using an Action. Choose one Completing Response appropriate to the mark.
Kindled Responses
You may use these responses when you spend a Kindled Mark.
Complete Force.
Trigger: the marked subject deals damage. Add 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier to one damage roll. This bonus increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
Complete Aim.
Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Add 1d4 to the attack roll, or choose one target making the saving throw and subtract 1d4 from that saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Complete Step.
Trigger: the marked subject begins movement during its turn. Increase one of the subject’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or allow it to stand from Prone without spending movement. At CL 11, the Speed increase becomes 20 feet.
Complete Breath.
Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points or gains Temporary HP. Increase the amount gained by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier.
Complete Resolve.
Trigger: the marked subject makes a saving throw against an effect that would reduce its Speed, prevent it from taking Reactions, impose Frightened, Paralyzed, Restrained, Stunned, or Unconscious, or suppress its ability to act. Add 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Complete Revelation.
Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll, Wisdom (Perception) check, or Intelligence (Investigation) check against a creature or effect that is Hidden, Invisible, heavily obscured, disguised by illusion, or concealed by a Yin-like technique. The marked subject ignores Disadvantage from not seeing the target for that roll, provided it can still identify the target’s space or general location.
Overkindled Responses
You may use these responses when you spend an Overkindled Mark.
Overheat Force.
Trigger: the marked subject deals damage, makes an attack roll, or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. After the triggering act resolves, the subject takes Fire or Radiant damage equal to 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This damage increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
Overexpose.
Trigger: the marked subject becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or benefits from a feature that prevents others from perceiving it. Until the start of your next turn, the subject cannot benefit from being Hidden or Invisible against you, and allies you choose within 60 feet know the subject’s current space if they can perceive the area.
Overcommit Step.
Trigger: the marked subject moves at least 10 feet, teleports, or uses special movement. After the movement resolves, the subject cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. If the movement was teleportation and the destination is within 120 feet of you, you know the destination space.
Overgrown Recovery.
Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores cultivation points (your Path resource), or benefits from regeneration. Until the start of your next turn, the first damage roll against that subject gains a bonus equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Overstrain Technique.
Trigger: the marked subject spends cultivation points (your Path resource), uses a spell slot, activates a limited feature, or uses a named cultivation technique. If the subject uses the same named spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability again before the end of its next turn, it gains a Rising Mark immediately after the repeated ability resolves.
Yang Saves
Some Yang features require a saving throw. Unless a feature says otherwise, your Cultivation Save DC equals your Cultivation Save DC.
Cultivation points are the resource used by your Path: Stamina, Qi, or Resonance.

TAL_YIN_BASE_SPHERE_ABILITIES.player_text:
BASE SPHERE ABILITIES

The Yin sphere uses Waning Marks. A Waning Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Waning Marks unless a feature says otherwise.
A Waning Mark represents a motion, technique, wound, breath, or intention that has begun to decline before it finishes expressing itself.
Mark Limit
You can maintain a number of Waning Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature can have only one Waning Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise.
A Waning Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked creature is no longer on the same plane of existence as you.
Marking a Creature
You can apply a Waning Mark in three basic ways.
Mark the Waning. As a Bonus Action, choose one creature within 60 feet that you can see, hear, or otherwise perceive clearly. The target gains one Waning Mark.
Receive Overextension. As a Reaction when a creature within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends cultivation points (your Path resource), uses a spell slot, teleports, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Waning Mark to that creature after the triggering event resolves.
Withdrawing Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Cold or Necrotic damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Waning Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Withdrawing Thread Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 (Cultivation Level) | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d6 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi cooling as the target’s action begins to wane.
Spending a Waning Mark
Once per round, when a marked creature you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Waning Mark without using an Action. Choose one Diminishing Response appropriate to the trigger.
Diminish Force
Trigger: the marked creature deals damage. Reduce one damage roll by 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This reduction increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
Diminish Aim
Trigger: the marked creature makes an attack roll. Subtract 1d4 from the attack roll. At CL 11, subtract 1d6 instead.
Diminish Power
Trigger: the marked creature forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Choose one creature making that saving throw. The chosen creature adds 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the bonus becomes 1d6.
Diminish Step
Trigger: the marked creature begins movement, including teleportation. Reduce one of the creature’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or reduce the distance of one teleportation effect by 10 feet. At CL 11, the reduction becomes 20 feet.
Diminish Recovery
Trigger: the marked creature regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores cultivation points (your Path resource), or benefits from regeneration. Reduce the amount gained or restored by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier, to a minimum of 0.
Diminish Readiness
Trigger: the marked creature takes a Reaction or would gain Advantage on a roll. The creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn, or the triggering Advantage is canceled for that roll.
Yin Saves
Some Yin features require a saving throw. Unless a feature says otherwise, your Cultivation Save DC equals your Cultivation Save DC.
Marked Allies
You may place a Waning Mark on a willing ally. When you do, the mark represents preservation rather than harm. You may spend that mark only for Diminish Force, Diminish Power, Diminish Step, or Diminish Recovery if doing so benefits the ally.

Create a Vessel Imprint

Use an action.
Range: 60 feet 
Cost: 3 Resonance 
Target: One willing creature, or one creature Resonance Marked by you

An unwilling target makes a Charisma saving throw.

Successful Save: No Vessel Imprint is created. The target knows you attempted the link and suffers one ordinary Spiritual Pressure effect until the start of your next turn.

Vessel Ward

Use a reaction.
You can use this when A willing imprinted target within 60 feet of the vessel fails an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw against a spiritual, mental, emotional, dream, memory, possession, or identity effect.

Add your Proficiency Bonus to the saving throw, potentially turning failure into success.

After you gain Spiritual Exorcism, a willing imprinted target within 1 mile can be the target of your Deep Exorcism Rite without being touched. Increase the rite’s Resonance cost by 2. A barrier that blocks the Vessel Imprint also blocks the rite.

player_card.summary: Sense souls and spirits beyond ordinary sight and examine them with Read the Spirit.

Effect: Range by Cultivation Level: 1–10: 10 feet; 11–16: 30 feet; 17–20: 60 feet.

Within range, perceive active souls, spirits, possessing entities, projected souls, spiritually animated corpses and creatures with ordinary living consciousness, even when normal sight cannot perceive them. Against an ordinary living creature, Complete Soul or spirit within range, this functions as Blindsight.

Know whether a perceived entity is broadly Embodied, Manifested, Hosted, possessing, projected, Unbodied, Anchored or Contained; Resonance Marked by you; or under obvious ordinary possession, coercive Hosting or spirit manifestation.
Choices: Read the Spirit: Action; Range: Your Spiritual Sense range. Choose one perceived soul, spirit, possession link, spiritual residue, Soul Fragment or spiritual effect. Learn its broad category; whether its Source CL is lower than, equal to or higher than yours; whether stable, strained, damaged, concealed, Hosted, bound, possessing, Anchored or suppressed; and whether a Complete Soul, Soul Fragment, Spiritual Imprint or uncertain mixture.

For a concealed or protected effect, make a Cultivation Check against its save DC, or 8 + source PB + source key ability modifier if it has none. Failure: you know spiritual concealment or interference is present, but not its exact nature; cannot retry until the effect changes, you obtain a new Source Rule or evidence, or a new scene begins.
Limits: Available at Cultivation Level 1; always active unless suppressed.

Does not automatically perceive soulless traps or objects; mundane writing, color or visual detail; a construct without a mind, spirit or animating soul; a corpse without active spirit or necromantic animation; a creature behind total cover; or a successfully concealed soul, Secret concealment, divine veil, artifact-level masking, sealed spirit or stronger spiritual absence.
Does not reveal exact statistics, thoughts, memories, Soul Anchor, Spirit Nature, Subpath, full Bond terms or hidden Source Rules.

tianxia.subpath.body.black_thorn_demon_b.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 - Calamity Briar Incarnation

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 7 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

Gain Demon Spines to maximum.

For the duration:

- Become Large if smaller.
- Unarmed reach +10 feet.
- Resistance to all damage except Fire, Psychic, and Void.
- Unarmed strikes deal 1d12 before modifiers.
- Once per turn on a hit, additional 4d8 Piercing or Slashing.
- Gain 1 Demon Spine at the start of each turn.
- Maximum Spines +3.
- Healing reduction applies only at 6 or more Spines.

Forest of Impalement

Action  
Area: 30-foot-radius sphere centered on you  
Cost: 4 Demon Spines  
Saving Throw: Dexterity

- Failed Save: 8d8 Piercing, Restrained, Bleeding, and lifted up to 10 feet.
- Successful Save: Half damage, pushed 10 feet, not Restrained.

A Restrained creature repeats the Dexterity save at the end of each turn, ending the state and falling safely to the nearest legal space on a success.

The thorn forest remains until the start of your next turn and is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures.

Normalized Procedure — Calamity Briar Incarnation

- On activation, gain Spines to the transformed maximum after increasing that maximum by 3. Become Large if smaller using transformation and legal-space procedures.
- The printed +10-foot reach is the transformation's reach increase and does not stack with Crown of Black Thorns' +5-foot reach unless the source explicitly says both apply; use the higher +10-foot increase.
- Resistance excludes Fire, Psychic, and Void. The 1d12 unarmed die replaces the normal base die; the once-per-turn 4d8 rider is separate.
- Gain 1 Spine at the start of each turn as a direct gain, even if the ordinary once-per-round gain flag is already used. Healing reduction uses the temporary 6-Spine threshold.
- Forest of Impalement: The Action creates a 30-foot-radius projected Body Field centered on you until the start of your next turn. Each affected creature saves once.
- On failure deal 8d8 Piercing, apply Restrained and Bleeding, and lift the target up to 10 feet vertically if a legal space exists. On success deal half, push 10 feet directly away, and do not Restrict.
- A Restrained creature repeats the Dexterity save at the end of each turn. On success it ends this restraint and moves or falls to the nearest legal supporting space without taking falling damage from the feature's own lift.
- The Field is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures and moves with you because it remains centered on you. It creates no permanent terrain, harvestable demon-wood, or automatic Injury.

---

player_card.summary: Create a Staff barrier that guards allies and stops approaching enemies.

Effect: During the barrier, increase Staff reach by 5 feet outside your turn and 10 feet total during your turn: 5 feet from Staff Form and another 5 feet from this feature.

Gain one additional Reaction each round, refreshing at the start of each round. Use it only for a Staff Opportunity Attack, Deflecting Staff or a Reaction explicitly identified as a Staff feature; it does not remove any once-per-round limit.

Hostile creatures provoke Opportunity Attacks when voluntarily entering your current Staff reach. Forced movement, teleportation, appearing in place or reach expanding around a creature does not provoke unless another rule says so.

A creature hit by your Opportunity Attack has its Speed reduced to 0 for the remainder of the turn. On a Staff Opportunity Attack hit, Speed becomes 0 only for the remainder of the current turn. It does not end a teleport already completed or retroactively cancel movement before the hit.

You and allies within 10 feet gain Half Cover against ranged weapon attacks and physical projectiles. This aura moves with you, requires no action and benefits a creature inside at the instant the attack resolves.
Once per turn after a Staff hit resolves, choose one result below.
Choices: Push the target 10 feet.
Move 10 feet along a legal route without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
Prevent the target’s Reactions until the start of its next turn.
Gain +1 AC until the start of your next turn; this does not stack with itself.
Limits: Available at Cultivation Level 18.

You must wield a Staff for its reach, Opportunity Attack, Deflecting Staff and cover benefits. They become dormant while you stop wielding one; duration continues and the benefits resume when you wield one again.

tianxia.subpath.body.bojutsu.feature.hea.player_text:
Cultivation Level 18 - Heavenly Staff Barrier

Bonus Action  
Duration: 1 minute  
Cost: 6 Stamina  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- Your Staff reach increases by another 5 feet.
- Gain one additional Reaction each round, usable only for a Staff Opportunity Attack, Deflecting Staff, or another Staff feature.
- Hostile creatures provoke Opportunity Attacks when entering your reach.
- A creature hit by your Opportunity Attack has its Speed reduced to 0 for the remainder of the turn.
- You and allies within 10 feet gain Half Cover against ranged weapon attacks and physical projectiles.

Once per turn after hitting with a Staff attack, choose one:

- Push the target 10 feet.
- Move 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Prevent the target from taking Reactions until the start of its next turn.
- Gain +1 AC until the start of your next turn.

---

Normalized Procedure — Heavenly Staff Barrier
- You must wield a Staff to receive its reach, Opportunity Attack, Deflecting Staff, and cover benefits. If you cease wielding one, those benefits become dormant while the duration continues and resume when you wield one again.
- Reach geometry. During the barrier, your Staff reach is increased by 5 feet outside your turn and by a total of 10 feet during your turn: 5 feet from Staff Form and another 5 feet from this feature. This lets entry into the barrier reach provoke as printed.
- The additional Reaction refreshes at the start of each round and can be spent only on a Staff Opportunity Attack, Deflecting Staff, or a Reaction explicitly identified as a Staff feature. It does not remove any once-per-round limit.
- A hostile creature provokes when it voluntarily enters your current Staff reach. Forced movement, teleportation, appearing in place, and the reach expanding around a creature do not provoke unless another rule says they do.
- On a Staff Opportunity Attack hit, Speed becomes 0 only for the remainder of the current turn. It does not end a teleport already completed or retroactively cancel movement before the hit.
- The 10-foot Half Cover aura moves with you, requires no action, and applies only against ranged weapon attacks and physical projectiles. A creature receives the benefit while within the aura at the instant the attack is resolved.
- The once-per-turn hit rider is chosen after a Staff hit resolves. The 10-foot self-movement requires a legal route and does not provoke. The AC option lasts exactly until the start of your next turn and does not stack with itself.

---

Cultivation Level 3 - Staff Form

Gain proficiency with Staff weapons.

While wielding a Staff weapon:

- You may use your Cultivation Attack Modifier for its attack rolls.

Normalized Procedure — Staff Form
- Staff record. A Staff is a quarterstaff or a weapon carrying the Staff tag. Record the specific weapon integrated by this feature. Its item properties, enhancement, damage type, handedness, and other tags remain unchanged unless this Subpath expressly changes them.
- Ability and attack choice. For each Staff attack, choose Constitution or another ability the weapon already permits. If you choose Constitution, use the Cultivation Attack Modifier and Constitution for damage. The same attack cannot add two ability modifiers unless another rule expressly permits it.

Refined Iron Fist and Heavenly Fist apply their cultivation-powered, adamantine, Force-damage, and object-damage permissions; they do not replace the Staff's normal damage die with the Iron Fist die unless another Source Rule explicitly does so.

player_card.summary: Gain defensive Staff benefits and deflect physical projectiles.

Rays, beams, purely energetic bolts, sound, gaze effects, save-based areas and effects expressly impossible to physically intercept are excluded.

Catch the projectile if it is a discrete object small enough for one free hand; this does not duplicate ammunition or an item.
Deflect it into an unoccupied space within 15 feet, ending the triggering attack against its original target without attacking another creature.

tianxia.subpath.body.bojutsu.feature.sta.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - Staff of One

While wielding a Staff weapon:

- Gain +1 AC.
- Gain Advantage against being Disarmed.
- Gain Advantage on Opportunity Attacks made with the Staff.

Deflecting Staff

Reaction  
You can use this when  You or an ally within 5 feet takes damage from a ranged weapon attack or physical projectile.  
Cost: 1 Stamina  
Limit: Once per round

Reduce the damage by 2d10 + Constitution modifier.

If this reduces the damage to 0, choose one:

- Catch the projectile if it is small enough to hold.
- Deflect it into an unoccupied space within 15 feet.
- Move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- Grant the protected ally Half Cover until the start of your next turn.

Deflecting Staff does not block a ray, beam, purely energetic projectile, or save-based area effect.

Normalized Procedure — Staff of One
- The +1 AC requires you to be wielding a Staff. It is an AC bonus, not a base AC calculation, and does not stack with another instance of Staff of One.
- Advantage against being Disarmed applies to checks and saving throws made specifically to retain the Staff. It does not prevent theft while you are helpless or the destruction of the weapon by a legal higher-authority effect.
- The Opportunity Attack Advantage applies only when the attack is made with the Staff.
- Deflecting Staff timing. Declare after the triggering ranged weapon attack or discrete physical projectile has determined damage but before that packet reduces Hit Points. Apply the reduction as an other flat reduction under the shared damage order.
- “Physical projectile” means a discrete material projectile whose path can be intercepted, including ordinary ammunition, thrown weapons, stones, needles, bolts, and comparable manifested matter. It excludes rays, beams, purely energetic bolts, sound, gaze effects, save-based areas, and effects whose rule says they cannot be physically intercepted.
- If a mixed damage packet qualifies because the attack is delivered by a physical projectile, reduce the entire triggering packet. A separate explosion, poison cloud, curse, or area effect created after impact is not canceled unless its Source Rule says interception prevents it.
- If damage becomes 0, choose exactly one printed option. Catching requires a discrete object small enough for one free hand and does not duplicate ammunition or an item. Deflecting into a space ends the triggering attack against its original target; it does not make an attack against another creature. The 5-foot movement must end in a legal space. Half Cover applies only to the protected ally and lasts as printed.
- Deflecting Staff remains once per round even if another feature grants an additional Reaction.

player_card.summary: Make an attacker reroll a hit with Disadvantage, then move up to 10 feet.

Effect: Trigger: An attack roll hits you.
Declare after the hit, before damage or on-hit effects resolve. The attacker uses the reroll even if higher. Compare it with your AC before moving, but do not apply damage yet.

After movement, recheck the same attack’s legal target, reach or range, line of effect and cover from the attacker’s unchanged origin. If the reroll missed your AC, it misses regardless of movement. If it would hit but cannot legally reach or target your new space, it misses; otherwise resolve the attack and its effects normally.
Choices: During the movement, without provoking Opportunity Attacks, you may fall Prone, stand from Prone, pass through one hostile creature’s space as Difficult Terrain, or end in an unoccupied space on the attacker’s opposite side. The opposite-side space must be adjacent to the attacker and legal for you.
Limits: Available at Cultivation Level 14.
Passing through a hostile creature’s space does not let you end there or pass an effect physically blocking passage.
This movement occurs during the triggering attack’s resolution and cannot itself trigger Empty Cup again.

tianxia.subpath.body.drunken_fist.featur.player_text:
Cultivation Level 14 - Empty Cup

Reaction  
You can use this when  An attack roll hits you.  
Cost: 2 Stamina  
Limit: Once per round

The attacker rerolls the attack with Disadvantage and uses the new result.

After the reroll resolves, move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. During this movement, you may fall Prone, stand from Prone, move through one hostile creature's space as Difficult Terrain, or end in an unoccupied space on the opposite side of the attacker.

If the rerolled attack can still reach your new space, resolve it normally. Otherwise, it misses.

Normalized Procedure — Empty Cup

- Declare after an attack roll has hit but before damage or hit riders resolve. The reroll replaces the original attack roll even if the new result is higher.

Effect: Area: 40-foot-radius, 60-foot-high cylinder centered on the Banner. For the duration, the Banner’s Fly Speed becomes 40 feet and it can pass through allied spaces. Gain 1 Dread at the start of each of your turns, use Banner Bite once during each turn without Dread, and pay 1 Dread for Edict of the Calamity Court.

Chosen allies in the field gain +2 AC against ranged attacks and Advantage against Frightened. Hostile creatures treat the area as Difficult Terrain. Hostile teleportation into or out of the field requires a Charisma save against your Cultivation Save DC if its Source CL is no higher than yours.

A hostile creature first entering during a turn or starting its turn inside makes a Wisdom save. Failure: 6d8 Psychic or Necrotic damage, Demon-Marked until the end of your next turn, Frightened and no Reactions until the start of its next turn. Success: half damage and Demon-Marked until the end of your next turn.

Court Collection: Once per round when a Demon-Marked qualifying hostile creature in the field reaches 0 Hit Points, choose an ally in the field. It regains 2d8 + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier Hit Points and may move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks. The same defeated creature triggers this only once, even if revived.

Procession Assets: The spectral demons, guards, beasts, musicians, scribes, and executioners are field manifestations, not independent creatures. They cannot be separately targeted, carry items, flank, or independently trigger resource generation, and disappear when the field ends.
Choices: End of Court: At normal duration end, if you spent at least 5 Dread during the Procession, choose to gain 1 Corruption or make the Banner Hungry until purified. Choose before resolving the ordinary scene-end Corruption trigger.
Limits: Available at CL 18.

Break the Procession: End it on lost Concentration, the Banner reaching 0 Hit Points, an equal- or higher-Source-CL anti-daemonic effect suppressing the Banner for a full round, or a higher-authority exorcism winning its printed contest. If it ends because the Banner was destroyed or exorcised, lose all Dread, gain 1 Corruption, and take 4d10 Psychic damage.

Cultivation Level 18 — Procession of Ten Thousand Demons

You transform the Banner’s court into a moving calamity procession.

Action  
Cost: 8 Qi  
Area: 40-foot-radius, 60-foot-high cylinder centered on the Banner  
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute  
Limit: Once per scene

For the duration:

- The Banner’s Fly Speed becomes 40 feet and it may move through allied spaces.
- Gain 1 Dread at the start of each of your turns.
- Use Banner Bite once during each turn without spending Dread.
- Edict of the Calamity Court costs 1 Dread.
- Chosen allies in the field gain +2 AC against ranged attacks and Advantage against Frightened.
- The area is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures.
- Hostile teleportation into or out of the field requires a Charisma save against your Cultivation Save DC when the teleport’s Source CL is no higher than yours.

A hostile creature that enters for the first time during a turn or starts its turn there makes a Wisdom saving throw.

Failed Save:

- Take 6d8 Psychic or Necrotic damage.
- Become Demon-Marked until the end of your next turn.
- Become Frightened until the start of its next turn.
- Cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

Successful Save:

- Take half damage.
- Become Demon-Marked until the end of your next turn.

Court Collection

Once per round when a Demon-Marked qualifying hostile creature in the field reaches 0 Hit Points:

- Choose one ally in the field.
- It regains 2d8 + your Qi Cultivation key ability modifier Hit Points.
- It may move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

The same defeated creature cannot trigger Court Collection more than once, even if revived.

Procession Assets

The spectral demons, guards, beasts, musicians, scribes, and executioners in the procession are manifestations of the field, not independent creatures.

They:

- Cannot be separately targeted.
- Cannot carry items.
- Cannot flank.
- Cannot trigger resource generation independently.
- Disappear when the field ends.

Break the Procession

The Procession ends if:

- You lose Concentration.
- The Banner reaches 0 Hit Points.
- An equal- or higher-Source-CL anti-daemonic effect suppresses the Banner for a full round.
- A higher-authority exorcism succeeds on its printed contest.

When the Procession ends because the Banner was destroyed or exorcised:

- Lose all Dread.
- Gain 1 Corruption.
- Take 4d10 Psychic damage.

End of Court

At normal duration end, if you spent at least 5 Dread during the Procession, choose one:

- Gain 1 Corruption.
- The Banner becomes Hungry until purified.

This choice is made before resolving the ordinary scene-end Corruption trigger.
